trades.thesis: The 10-Q shows a genuine Q3 inflection — revenue +32% YoY to $67.5M, gross margin ~54%, operating income +76% YoY — against a stock already down 53% from its 1-year high, so the market is pricing the weak nine-month trajectory (revenue -5%, operating income -63%, operating cash flow -$6.4M) rather than the recovering run-rate. The rerating mechanism is concrete: an $80.0M deferred revenue balance built for conversion over coming quarters, plus the company's own flagged backlog-conversion pipeline, gives a dated path for Q4 revenue recognition within the forecast window. Downside is tolerable rather than benign: covenant headroom is wide (funded debt/EBITDA 0.55:1 vs 2:1 max; $39.4M excess availability vs $5.0M minimum) and ~$54.8M of the $110M secured facility is undrawn, so the cash burn is a grind, not a solvency event, over 90 days. The setup is a momentum-inflection long at a deeply depressed price, not a cheapness-only thesis — but conviction is capped by accrual-heavy earnings ($23.7M of the working-capital drag was variable stock-comp payments), rising secured debt, and an unresolved legal/credibility overhang (prior restatement litigation, securities class actions, adverse $2.1M arbitration award under appeal).
trades.catalyst: Q4 2011 holiday-season theater system deployments converting the $80.0M deferred revenue balance into recognized revenue, with continued Q3-style momentum (equipment +36%, rentals +53% YoY) driving upward estimate revisions; secondary positive from potential collection on the $11.3M E-City ICC award.
trades.invalidation: Q4 results or interim disclosures showing theater backlog failing to convert to revenue (explicitly flagged risk), continued negative operating cash flow with further revolver draws toward covenant limits, or an adverse development in the securities class actions / Robots arbitration appeal.

trades.thesis: BAC trades at ~$5.19, down ~56% from its 1-year high, pricing severe distress that the filings do not fully support. The 10-Q documents funded, verifiable capital repair: $5.0B Berkshire preferred/warrant investment, ~$3.5B Tier 1 common from the CCB stake sale, capped preferred/trust-to-common debt exchanges (≤400M shares/$3B notes), and planned long-term debt reduction through 2013. Core credit trends are genuinely improving (Q3 provision $3.4B vs $5.4B YoY; $6.3B nine-month reserve releases on lower card delinquencies), and Project New BAC targets ~30,000 headcount cuts and $5B annual expense savings by 2014 — a credible multi-year earnings-power rebuild. The market is extrapolating worst-case mortgage tails onto a franchise whose liquidity and capital trajectory are demonstrably strengthening. Skeptical caveats are real: Q3's $6.2B net income is dominated by low-persistence items ($4.5B own-credit FV adjustments, $3.6B CCB gain, $1.7B DVA), NII yield compressed 40bps to 2.32%, Moody's downgraded to Baa1, and the all-50-state/DOJ servicing settlement plus GSE R&W claims remain unquantified tails. But the $14.0B nine-month R&W provision plus $2.6B goodwill impairment means much of the known pain is already absorbed, and the combination of extreme drawdown, externally validated capital (Berkshire), mechanical Tier 1 build, and falling credit costs offers both a rerating mechanism and bounded downside within 90 days.
trades.catalyst: Completion of the capped preferred/trust-preferred-for-common exchanges (up to 400M shares / $3B senior notes) plus the Canada card sale closing in Q4 2011 mechanically lifts Tier 1 common without external equity; a de-escalation of the 50-state/DOJ servicing settlement removes the dominant uncertainty discount on a stock already down ~56% from its 1-year high and trading at a deep discount to tangible book.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the global servicing settlement or GSE repurchase demands produce loss estimates materially above the $14.0B already provisioned, if further ratings downgrades force collateral/funding repricing, or if European sovereign contagion re-widens BAC credit spreads enough to force dilutive capital actions beyond the 400M-share exchange cap.

trades.thesis: Lincoln Financial (LNC) trades at ~$11.90 after a -41% drawdown from its 1-year high, roughly 0.25x stated book value ($14.9B equity / ~302M shares ≈ $49/share). The Q3 2011 deterioration (pre-tax income $139M vs $303M, $(138)M realized loss swing, $4.6B account-value decline) is predominantly mark-to-market and macro-driven rather than franchise impairment: nine-month revenues grew +4%, insurance fees +12%, net flows were positive, and the balance sheet strengthened materially (cash doubled to $4.8B, AOCI improved to $2.46B, Series B preferred redeemed). Management's 5x dividend increase and resumed buybacks signal capital confidence. The known ASU 2010-26/DAC reset (~$950M-$1.15B retained earnings cut on Jan 1, 2012) is non-cash and pre-disclosed, limiting surprise value. With such an extreme discount to book, any stabilization in equity markets and credit spreads offers a high-beta rerating mechanism; cheapness alone is not sufficient, but here it is paired with demonstrable liquidity build and shareholder-friendly capital deployment. The bet is effectively on mean reversion of a deeply discounted, well-capitalized insurer rather than on near-term earnings momentum, which remains weak.
trades.catalyst: Macro risk-appetite normalization lifting deeply discounted, high-beta life insurers toward book value; continued AOCI/unrealized-loss recovery and resumed buybacks ($375M YTD) plus the quintupled dividend signal management confidence ahead of the non-cash Jan 1, 2012 accounting reset.
trades.invalidation: Renewed macro/sovereign-credit stress driving further equity-market declines (further account-value erosion and unrealized losses), a debt-ratings downgrade action, or disclosure of material statutory/reserve strain would invalidate the rerating thesis; also a break below the post-cutoff lows on heavy volume.

trades.thesis: Morgan Stanley trades at ~$11.82, down ~46% from its 1-year high and at roughly 0.37x stated shareholders' equity ($61.8B across ~1.93B shares, ~$32/share book). The Q3 2011 10-Q shows a credible fundamental inflection: net revenues +46% YoY to $9.9B on trading strength ($4,961M vs $1,441M), diluted EPS swinging to $1.15 from -$0.07, and asset management fees growing steadily. Critically, the MUFG conversion of $7.8B-face Series B preferred into common eliminated most of the preferred stack ($9.6B -> $1.5B) and removed a persistent dilution/dividend overhang, while the balance sheet has been actively de-risked (repo funding down ~$37.5B YTD, long-term borrowings reduced). This is a classic distressed-multiple setup where a solvency/funding scare has compressed the multiple far below book despite improving operating results. The rerating mechanism is concrete: if wholesale funding markets stabilize and Q4 trading normalizes to a still-solid level, the market can begin valuing the enlarged common equity base on normalized earnings power rather than crisis multiples. However, this is not a table-pounder: nine-month EPS ($1.45 vs $2.15) remains below prior year due to the 27% share count expansion, operating cash flow collapsed to $3.6B from $19.3B on repo runoff, own-credit deterioration is visible (~$12.7B gap between carrying value and fair value of long-term borrowings), and $2.8T credit derivative guarantee notional plus judgment-dependent Level 3 valuations leave genuine tail exposure should the European funding crisis deepen. Position as a sized long candidate with strict invalidation on funding-market deterioration, not a conviction overweight.
trades.catalyst: Normalization of wholesale funding conditions (repo stabilization) plus sustained post-MUFG-conversion profitability would drive rerating toward even half of book value; near-term triggers include Q4 earnings confirmation of trading strength and any regulatory clarity on capital requirements for the enlarged common-equity base.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 results show trading revenue mean-reversion below run-rate, further repo/wholesale funding contraction, or renewed own-credit widening (fair-value discount on long-term borrowings expanding beyond ~$13B), signaling the funding squeeze is intensifying rather than stabilizing.

trades.thesis: Shaw Group screens as a discounted self-help story trading ~7% below its own just-completed $150M Dutch auction tender price ($24.25 vs. $22.66 pre-cutoff close), which is a rare, cash-funded management valuation anchor. The fundamental setup combines a sharp profitability inflection (gross profit nearly doubled to $119.9M; operating income swung to +$50.5M from -$9.3M on flat revenue) with a dated, contractual de-risking event: the fixed-JPY Toshiba put (~124.7B JPY, ~$1.65B) exercisable around October 6, 2012 funds the March 15, 2013 Westinghouse Bond maturity, converting a feared refinancing cliff into a crystallizing cash inflow well inside the 90-day narrative window. Liquidity is adequate ($637M cash + $242.6M ST investments, minimal conventional debt) despite -$140.9M quarterly operating cash flow. The stock is down ~45% from its 1-year high post-Fukushima nuclear overhang, so even partial normalization of sentiment plus buyback support offers a plausible rerating path. Earnings quality caveats are real — the quarter leaned on a $25.2M non-cash FX gain — and the AQC client's $169.6M cost/fee challenge is a genuine tail risk, so this is a sized-long candidate, not a conviction max-weight idea. Cheapness alone would not qualify; here cheapness coincides with a management-anchored price floor, a margin recovery already visible in reported results, and a dated monetization catalyst that resolves the largest balance-sheet uncertainty.
trades.catalyst: Q2 FY2012 earnings report (~April 2012) confirming margin durability and backlog stability, plus disclosure of a concrete refinancing/funding path for the March 2013 Westinghouse Bonds ahead of the October 6, 2012 put exercise window; continued open-market buybacks under the remaining $328.2M authorization provide ongoing share-price support below the $24.25 tender level.
trades.invalidation: Adverse or escalating resolution of the AQC $169.6M cost/fee challenge; continued deeply negative operating cash flow into Q2 FY2012 without working-capital normalization; absence of any disclosed refinancing plan for the March 2013 bonds as the October 2012 put window approaches; renewed JPY strength reversing translation gains.

trades.thesis: Mosaic trades ~41% below its 1-year high ($39.37) despite filings showing accelerating fundamentals: Q2 FY12 net sales +12.7% YoY ($3,014.5M), six-month sales +25.4%, six-month gross margin expanding to 28.4% from 26.2%, and operating earnings up 42.9% to $1,526.6M. Headline EPS decline is optical — it laps a $685.6M one-time investment-sale gain. Two credible rerating mechanisms exist beyond cheapness: (1) completion of the Cargill split-off unwind — all 112,991,398 Class B shares converted post-quarter-end, eliminating the dominant ownership overhang and normalizing float/index treatment; (2) the Dec 7, 2011 tolling agreement settlement freeing Esterhazy potash volumes for market-priced sales, which management flags as potentially materially positive. Balance sheet is a downside buffer: $3.6B cash vs ~$1.55B debt, $1.07B six-month OCF, $729M undrawn revolver, and refinancing at lower coupons. Key risks are idiosyncratic and bounded: the South Fort Meade injunction raises phosphate costs via purchased rock (mitigated by an appeal pending at the Eleventh Circuit), rising unrecognized tax benefits ($416.6M) amid IRS/CRA audits, and commodity/FX sensitivity (AOCI -$310M translation loss). As a fertilizer cyclical at a deep drawdown with strong operating momentum and dated structural catalysts, risk/reward skews favorable but with wide dispersion typical of the sector.
trades.catalyst: Completion of the Cargill split-off unwind (all 112.99M Class B shares converted to Class A post-quarter-end) removing the dominant ownership overhang, combined with the Dec 7, 2011 PCS tolling agreement settlement that frees Esterhazy potash volumes for market sales from 2012, plus upcoming Q3 FY12 earnings (March 2012) showcasing underlying operating earnings growth ex-prior-year one-time gain.
trades.invalidation: Adverse Eleventh Circuit ruling extending the South Fort Meade mining injunction into peak production periods (forcing sustained purchased-rock substitution and potential concentrate plant closures), or a sharp break in potash/phosphate pricing that reverses the gross-margin expansion trend by the Q3 FY12 report.

trades.thesis: Amarin is a pre-revenue late-stage biopharma whose lead asset AMR101 has an SPA-backed NDA under FDA review for the MARINE indication with a hard PDUFA date of July 26, 2012. The 90-day window from the 2012-02-29 cutoff captures the classic pre-PDUFA re-rating period: SPA support plus already-reported favorable Phase 3 MARINE/ANCHOR results give an above-base-rate approval prior, while the January 2012 $150M 3.50% exchangeable notes (~$144.3M net) on top of $116.6M year-end cash provide roughly $260M pro forma liquidity — sufficient for at least twelve months including REDUCE-IT and launch prep, so financing risk does not force dilution before the catalyst. The stock sits ~55% below its 1-year high, suggesting much speculative froth has been cleared. Offsetting factors keep sizing modest: no revenue, $69.1M FY2011 loss with rapidly rising spend, unresolved Ester shareholder dispute, no internal audit function, single API supplier in the NDA, and an undated strategic-process overhang. The rerating mechanism is credible (dated, SPA-supported binary event with funded runway); downside is tolerable because cash covers operations past the decision date, but a complete response letter would be severe given ANCHOR is contingent on MARINE — hence a moderate expected excess rather than aggressive sizing.
trades.catalyst: Dated FDA PDUFA decision on July 26, 2012 for the SPA-backed AMR101 MARINE NDA; the 90-day window captures the pre-decision positioning period ahead of this binary event, with potential upside optionality from an undated strategic collaboration/acquisition process running in parallel.
trades.invalidation: Announcement of an FDA advisory committee meeting, a complete response letter or negative regulatory communications on MARINE, adverse developments in the Ester shareholder dispute, a large dilutive equity raise before approval, or breakdown below the post-offering trading range would invalidate the thesis; also any signal that REDUCE-IT enrollment is stalling, weakening the ANCHOR-dependent longer-term story.

trades.thesis: DexCom enters the window at $2.45, down ~41% from its 1-year high, implying substantial pessimism is already embedded. The filings show a business that is operationally inflecting: Q1 2012 revenue +42% YoY ($20.1M), gross margin expanded ~11 points to ~47% on volume and manufacturing absorption, and new partnership economics (Tandem signed Feb 2012, Roche milestones pending). Against that, losses are widening (operating loss $15.4M), burn is ~$10M/quarter, and management guides liquidity only through March 2013 — so dilution risk is real but not acute within the 90-day horizon. With ~68.8M shares outstanding, EV is roughly $100M against an ~$85-90M annualized revenue run-rate growing >40% with no debt — a depressed multiple where continued execution plus margin trajectory offers a credible rerating mechanism rather than mere cheapness. The June 7 Federal Circuit oral hearing in the Abbott patent dispute is a dated, potentially asymmetric catalyst. Key watch items: stocking-distributor shipments jumped to 35% of revenue (company claims limited channel inventory — monitor for channel stuffing), SBC intensity, and poison pill/anti-takeover provisions capping M&A premium scenarios. Position sizing must respect the binary litigation event and financing overhang.
trades.catalyst: Sequential revenue prints sustaining the ~40% growth rate with gross-margin absorption gains narrowing the operating-loss trajectory; secondary binary: June 7, 2012 Federal Circuit oral hearing in the Abbott patent appeal (favorable outcome would remove a key overhang); partnership milestones (Roche/Tandem) provide minor optionality.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q2 revenue growth decelerates materially below ~35%, gross margins stall or reverse, distributor channel mix keeps climbing without end-demand confirmation, or an equity offering is announced within the window at distressed pricing; adverse signal from the June 7 Federal Circuit hearing would also invalidate.

trades.thesis: Comstock is a leveraged, gas-weighted E&P trading ~49% below its 1-year high with Q1 2012 volumes +28% YoY (oil +267%), which positions it as a high-beta recovery vehicle if depressed natural gas prices normalize. The filing confirms genuine operating momentum (OCF +162% to $133.2M, LOE flat/unit) and a completed $118.5M asset sale (closed May 1) that funds the near-term capex gap alongside $17.2M of remaining Stone Energy shares. However, earnings quality is poor (operating income just $1.5M vs $33.3M of one-time gains), OCF is flattered by a $63.4M payables build, cash is $3.75M, and the borrowing base was cut to $655.5M leaving only ~$45M pro forma headroom against $610M drawn — so this is an asymmetric commodity-timing bet, not a quality compounder. With gas at multi-year lows, rising gas-weighted production, and no near-term maturities (revolver 2015, notes 2017/2019), the setup favors a modestly positive skew over 90 days, but the rerating mechanism is macro-dependent (gas price recovery) rather than company-specific, warranting only moderate conviction and sizing.
trades.catalyst: Natural gas price normalization off cyclical lows driving NAV rerate in a high-beta, deeply discounted gas-weighted E&P; secondary company-specific supports are deployment of the $118.5M sale proceeds toward the funding gap and the June 26, 2012 1031-exchange VIE termination releasing restricted cash and simplifying ownership of ~$344.8M of properties.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if natural gas strip stays below ~$2.50/Mcf through summer (no gas hedges disclosed, ~$21.7M/quarter cash flow sensitivity per $1.00/Mcf), or if the post-sale borrowing base forces visible capex cuts/asset disposals at distressed prices before the gas curve recovers — either would confirm the equity as a melting leveraged option rather than a mean-reversion candidate.

trades.thesis: Pilgrim's Pride (PPC, ~$3.02, -45% from 1y high) presents a credible fundamental inflection rather than mere cheapness. Q2 FY2012 swung to a $144.1M gross profit (+$190.3M YoY) and $69.4M net income attributable vs a $(128.1)M loss, driven by higher U.S. chicken prices per pound (+$96.7M revenue contribution) and portfolio pruning. The turnaround is corroborated across roles: YTD operating cash flow of $80.3M vs $(140.2)M prior year, long-term debt reduced ~$193M to $1,214.6M after the $198.3M rights offering repaid the 50M JBS subordinated loan, and equity rebuilt to $851.7M. At ~$782M market cap (258.9M shares), the stock trades below book equity and at a low single-digit multiple of annualized Q2 earnings — a depressed price that can re-rate if profitability persists. Near-term funded catalysts exist: the agreed Cal-Maine egg operations sale expected to close August 2012 (inside the 90-day window) and active marketing of $44.7M held-for-sale assets. The key tension is the 2012 grain-cost escalation (corn futures high $6.77/bushel): current chicken prices offset feed costs, and industry supply discipline historically allows price pass-through, but this is the principal swing factor for the next two quarters. Governance is a persistent drag (JBS 75.3% control, related-party sales up ~3x, dividend prohibition) but does not block a commodity-cycle re-rating. Position sizing must respect the binary-ish nature of the December covenant test and drought uncertainty.
trades.catalyst: August 2012 closing of the Cal-Maine egg operations sale plus continued quarterly earnings delivery demonstrating the spread recovery is durable; each quarter of positive net income further de-risks the December covenant test and supports multiple re-rating from distressed levels toward even a modest normalized P/E.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 results (due ~November 2012) show gross margin reverting as higher-priced corn flows through cost of sales without matching chicken price increases, or if the Cal-Maine sale is delayed/renegotiated; a renewed covenant waiver request would signal the balance-sheet repair is insufficient.

trades.thesis: Wabash National (WNC, ~$5.43, -40% from 1y high) presents a credible fundamental rerating setup rather than mere cheapness. The Q2 2012 10-Q shows genuine operating inflection: gross margin expanded from 5.7% to ~11% YoY on +26% sales growth, organic trailer volumes grew +5.3%, and backlog rose to $713M from $587M (including $190M Walker). Management guides FY2012 volumes of 48k-52k trailers with strong demand expected into 2013 per ACT industry estimates. The debt-funded $375M Walker acquisition adds $44.3M revenue/$2.9M net income in a stub period and diversifies into Diversified Products (+380% segment sales). Against this, GAAP net income fell YoY ($1.9M vs $3.3M) due to $12.2M one-time acquisition expenses and higher interest — items that should roll off — while the market appears to be pricing integration and leverage fears (debt/equity ~2.5:1, negative H1 operating cash flow of -$11.5M driven largely by a deliberate working-capital/inventory build alongside the backlog surge). At ~$5.43 versus an $11.70 convert conversion price, the equity embeds substantial skepticism about whether margin gains are real. If Q3 confirms sustained double-digit gross margins and positive cash conversion as acquisition expenses abate, a meaningful rerating is plausible within 90 days. Risks that temper sizing: ~$478M debt against $175.8M equity, goodwill (~86% of equity) plus intangibles creating impairment sensitivity, preliminary purchase accounting, Walker excluded from ICFR until FY2013, and a dated Brazil BK appellate ruling expected after Q3 2012 with uncharged exposure up to ~$54M including adjustments. Net: modestly positive asymmetry with real tail risks — a small, disciplined long candidate, not a high-conviction position.
trades.catalyst: Q3 2012 earnings (late October) expected to show first full quarter of combined Wabash+Walker results with sustained double-digit gross margins and continued backlog conversion; secondary dated event is the Brazil BK appellate ruling expected after Q3 2012, where a favorable or contained outcome removes a headline overhang on an uncharged contingency.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if Q3 2012 results show gross margin reverting below ~9% (raw-material pass-through failure under fixed-price contracts), operating cash flow stays materially negative without a working-capital explanation, covenant headroom narrows, or the Brazil appeal produces a large adverse charge; a break of the post-acquisition price low would also signal the deleveraging/rerating narrative has failed.

trades.thesis: Beazer is a high-beta, deeply discounted option on the 2012 US housing recovery. The fiscal Q3 10-Q shows a genuine operating inflection — revenue +47% YoY, nine-month gross profit up ~2.7x, G&A down ~23%, homebuilding segments turning operating-income positive, spec inventory halved, and a fourth consecutive quarter of YoY gains in orders/closings/backlog (+33%). Critically, the July 2012 ~$466M raise (equity + TEUs + 6.625% secured notes) retired the 12% notes and cut annualized interest expense ~$15M, converting a fragile pre-raise liquidity position ($231.6M unrestricted cash vs $1.44B debt) into a workable one (~$418M pro forma cash plus a committed $150M revolver letter). The stock sits 41% below its 1-year high at $11.55, so even partial recognition of the segment-level profitability turn offers substantial rerating torque. This is not cheapness alone: there is a credible near-term mechanism (momentum in orders/backlog plus removal of refinancing tail risk) and tolerable downside given the freshly de-levered maturity profile. Risks are real — ~8x debt/equity, ongoing cash burn, heavy dilution (75.6M→~123M shares), aggressive impairment assumptions, and legal overhangs — which keep this a sized long candidate rather than a conviction position.
trades.catalyst: Continued monthly housing data beats (new home sales, Case-Shiller, builder sentiment) plus Q4 FY2012 results showing first consolidated operating profit and positive free cash flow; completion of the $150M secured revolver closing removes the last liquidity overhang.
trades.invalidation: Net new order growth or backlog decelerating in upcoming disclosures; failure to close the proposed $150M revolver; renewed inventory impairments or an Inspirada JV write-down; any covenant waiver request — each would break the recovery-rerating thesis.

trades.thesis: Sarepta (post reverse-split, renamed AVI BioPharma) screens as a funded-but-dependent development-stage biotech at $23.86, down ~47% from its 1-year high. Positives: $38.0M cash plus ~$22M raised in October ($16.4M ATM + $5.6M warrants), management's 12-month sufficiency assertion, narrowing operating losses (Q3 op loss $6.9M vs $11.3M), and R&D cost cuts. Negatives dominate the near-term setup: the U.S. government terminated the Ebola portion of its largest contract (10/2/2012), removing roughly half of contract revenue; ongoing at-market dilution ($36.3M drawn through Oct 31); shareholders' equity turned negative on a non-cash Level 3 warrant mark; CSO resignation; classified board/anti-takeover provisions; and disclosed NASDAQ listing-compliance risk. Critically, the extractions contain no grounded, dated near-term rerating mechanism for the lead asset (eteplirsen Phase IIb/regulatory pathway details are truncated/missing across all five specialists). Cheapness relative to the prior high is not evidence — the drawdown partly reflects the Ebola termination and dilution. With no credible documented catalyst inside 90 days and material two-sided risk, this does not meet the bar for a long candidate; it remains a watchlist name pending disclosure of a concrete lead-asset regulatory milestone or Marburg option exercise.
trades.catalyst: Potential DoD option exercises on Marburg segments II-IV (~$84.4M) or resolution of remaining December 2012 warrant exercises ($10.4M potential); any disclosed acceleration of the eteplirsen regulatory pathway would be the primary rerating trigger, but none is documented in the available excerpts.
trades.invalidation: A long thesis would be invalidated by further government contract cuts (Marburg stop-work), ATM capacity exhaustion forcing discounted financing, or confirmation that no meaningful eteplirsen regulatory milestone falls within the next two quarters; conversely, entry would require documented evidence of an imminent lead-asset catalyst.

trades.thesis: Boyd Gaming enters the window deeply de-rated (-44% from 1-year high, ~$5.04 price, ~$1.4B equity vs ~$3.9B debt) with a single, well-defined near-term event: the ~$1.45B all-debt-financed Peninsula Gaming acquisition contractually required to close by February 2013, with financing fully secured ($350M 8.375% notes held in escrow plus committed $825M term loan). Closing folds substantial acquired EBITDA into a small equity base — a classic leveraged-equity rerating setup where the stock behaves as a call option on the deal. Critically, the downside is structurally bounded: if the deal fails, the escrowed notes face special mandatory redemption, so the equity does not absorb incremental debt from a broken deal. The bear case is real — Q3 swung to a $(15.8)M net loss as interest expense ($74.1M) exceeded operating income ($48.3M), SG&A and promotional costs grew faster than revenue, operating cash flow declined YoY, current maturities jumped to $403M, and management explicitly depends on revolver availability — but most of this distress appears priced into a stock already down 44%. The bet is that successful closing within the window converts a distressed-looking balance sheet story into a higher-EBITDA, refinancing-capable story, producing positive skew from the current depressed base. Cheapness alone would not qualify; here cheapness coincides with a dated, financed, contractual catalyst.
trades.catalyst: Peninsula Gaming acquisition closing in Q4 2012 (contractual outside date February 2013), which immediately folds acquired property cash flows into the consolidated entity against a small ~$1.4B equity base; any post-close deleveraging guidance or improved pro forma disclosure is an additional rerating trigger within the window.
trades.invalidation: Regulatory approval not obtained and the merger is terminated or pushed beyond February 2013 without a credible new timeline — the escrowed notes are then mandatorily redeemed, leaving the standalone business with declining operating cash flow, rising interest expense, margin compression, and $403M of current maturities against thin free cash flow.

trades.thesis: The stock trades ~44% below its 1-year high despite fundamentals that remain strong: nine-month net sales +22.9% to $1.59B, $272M net income, $218M operating cash flow, ~$590.7M cash/short-term investments, and essentially no debt. The drawdown appears driven by headline/regulatory and litigation fear (channel-stuffing class action, derivative suits, energy-drink safety scrutiny) rather than demand deterioration. Management's conviction is visible: the $500M 2011-2012 repurchase plan was exhausted with post-quarter purchases at $54.99, well above the current price. If the regulatory/litigation overhang stabilizes and growth persists, a meaningful rerating is plausible within 90 days; the net-cash, high-FCF balance sheet makes the downside tolerable. Offsets are real — ~220bps gross margin compression, falling price per case ($9.92 vs $10.26), working-capital build, CCR concentration at ~28% of sales, and Level 3 ARS marks — so this is a risk-aware long candidate, not a table-pounder.
trades.catalyst: De-risking of the energy-drink safety/regulatory narrative (no adverse FDA action or label change materializing), plus a new buyback authorization decision following exhaustion of the $500M plan — either event can re-anchor the multiple toward fundamentals; Q4 earnings in Feb 2013 is the nearest scheduled proof point.
trades.invalidation: Adverse FDA/regulatory action on energy-drink caffeine content, escalation of the channel-stuffing litigation (e.g., damaging discovery or derivative-suit developments), Q4 results showing volume deceleration or further >200bps margin erosion, or disclosure of distributor relationship deterioration with CCR.

trades.thesis: The issuer enters the window with intact, accelerating fundamentals — net sales +17.9% to $4.07B, operating cash flow of $567.8M, improving sales-leader retention (52.0% vs 48.9%) — while the equity sits ~46% below its 1-year high on very high dollar volume, indicating a crowded bear position rather than fundamental deterioration. Management is leaning in: post-year-end borrowings under the credit facility fund additional buybacks (subsequent event), dividends are escalating ($135.1M paid in 2012), and $695.2M of undrawn revolver capacity supports continued capital return. A credible rerating mechanism exists: sustained repurchases plus a recurring dividend-increase cadence into a deeply discounted multiple. Offsets are genuine but mostly bounded: Venezuela remeasurement (~$14M pre-tax / ~$16M cash impact if the 6.3 CADIVI rate applies), China direct-selling licensing uncertainty, ~$88M Mexican VAT assessment (nullified, re-issue possible), and structurally high distributor churn (~48% non-requalification). Cheapness alone would not qualify, but here cheapness coincides with verified double-digit top-line growth, rising retention, self-funded capital returns, and no disclosed impairment or control failures — a plausible squeeze-plus-fundamentals rerating setup within 90 days.
trades.catalyst: Continued open-market share repurchases funded by Credit Facility borrowings (disclosed as subsequent events) plus a likely annual dividend increase announcement in the Feb–Apr window, against a deeply depressed price and heavy short interest that must eventually be covered into improving fundamentals.
trades.invalidation: A formal SEC or FTC inquiry disclosure, an adverse resolution of the Venezuela remeasurement/deconsolidation question materially above the ~$16M flagged exposure, or Q1 2013 results showing decelerating sales-leader growth/retention would invalidate the rerating thesis.

trades.thesis: HALO trades at $5.45, -59% from its 1-year high, with the Baxter HyQ CRL damage largely recognized. The filings show a credible, de-risked near-term rerating mechanism: Roche's subcutaneous Herceptin Phase 3 met co-primary endpoints and EMA line-extension applications were filed in March 2012 (Herceptin) and December 2012 (MabThera), with MabThera's first-stage non-inferiority endpoint also met — meaning EU regulatory decisions are plausibly inside or near the 90-day window and carry milestone/royalty re-rating potential. Roche has elected five exclusive targets with three options remaining, evidencing durable platform validation. Liquidity is adequate for the horizon ($99.9M cash vs guided $45-50M 2013 burn, ~2-year runway), so the dominant risks are the binary Q2 2013 Baxter HyQ FDA meeting (bearish tail given FDA asked patients stop being dosed with rHuPH20 in that program), possible dilution flagged within twelve months, and lumpy collaboration-driven revenue. Cheapness alone is not the thesis; the thesis is de-risked partnered regulatory events against a deeply washed-out price, with tolerable downside given runway and no near-term covenant stress disclosed.
trades.catalyst: EMA review milestones for subcutaneous Herceptin and MabThera line extensions (Phase 3-positive, filed 2012) falling within/near the 90-day window, plus the Q2 2013 Baxter HyQ FDA meeting where a constructive path forward would lift the platform overhang.
trades.invalidation: Adverse or inconclusive outcome of the Q2 2013 Baxter HyQ FDA meeting that extends the dosing halt or questions rHuPH20 platform safety; material slippage of EMA timelines for Herceptin/MabThera SC; or an announced equity raise at depressed prices ahead of the catalysts.

trades.thesis: Cirrus Logic trades at $17.61, down ~61% from its 1-year high, implying roughly $1.1B market cap (63.4M shares) against FY2013 revenue of ~$810M and net income of ~$136.6M — a low-single-digit trailing P/E even before netting ~$226M of cash/securities against just $10.1M of long-term obligations. The fundamentals show real operating momentum: audio product sales more than doubled ($264.8M → $350.7M → $754.8M over three years), the fabless model keeps capex light, working capital is ample ($351.5M), and E&Y issued unqualified opinions on both financials and ICFR. A $200M buyback with ~$114M remaining offers price support. The stock's collapse appears driven by feared Apple order normalization and ASP pressure rather than realized deterioration, so a credible rerating mechanism exists: confirmation of sustained audio content-per-box momentum at the Q1 FY2014 print (late July) heading into the fall smartphone cycle could compress the perceived risk premium. However, this is a concentrated, single-customer story (Apple ~82% of sales, up from 62%) with explicit management-guided ASP declines, no long-term supply contracts, cancellable orders, a sharp finished-goods inventory build ($25M → $85M), and an active securities class action alleging misleading statements about Jul–Oct 2012 results — all of which justify demanding a wide margin of safety and modest sizing rather than aggressive exposure.
trades.catalyst: Q1 FY2014 earnings report (expected late July 2013) demonstrating sustained audio revenue momentum and margin resilience into the fall smartphone upgrade cycle, plus continued opportunistic buyback execution under the remaining ~$114M authorization; July 30 annual meeting is a minor secondary marker.
trades.invalidation: Any pre-earnings channel check or disclosure indicating Apple order cuts, loss of socket/content share, or materially worse ASP erosion than guided; also a Q1 FY14 print showing gross margin compression below trend or another large finished-goods build without corresponding sell-through would invalidate the rerating thesis.

trades.thesis: Vanda trades at $5.84, down ~55% from its 1-year high and roughly half its August 2013 offering price ($11.14), implying a market cap near $194M against $142.2M cash, no debt, and ~$97M deferred revenue — an enterprise value around $52M for a company whose lead asset (tasimelteon for Non-24) has an NDA under active FDA review following July 2013 acceptance. Standard review timing places the FDA decision plausibly inside the 90-day window, providing a concrete binary rerating mechanism rather than mere cheapness. Liquidity is not a constraint: nine-month operating burn of $27.4M (~$9M/quarter) gives multi-year runway post-offering, so the position can be held through delay. Skeptical offsets are material: revenue is largely non-cash ratable amortization of legacy licensing deals, G&A is ramping (+81% YoY) ahead of launch, accumulated deficit is $303.7M, up to $37M in BMS milestones plus low-teens royalties encumber approval economics, and pending securities class actions over tasimelteon Phase III disclosures signal genuine market doubt about the data — raising CRL tail risk. On balance, the asymmetric setup (deep discount to cash + funded runway + dated regulatory catalyst) justifies a long candidate stance with moderate sizing, acknowledging that a CRL would likely produce a severe drawdown toward cash-backed levels.
trades.catalyst: FDA decision on the tasimelteon NDA for Non-24-Hour Disorder, expected within the 90-day forecast window based on standard review timing following July 2013 acceptance; an approval would trigger commercialization inflection, milestone payments ($8.0M BMS, $2.0M consultant), and removal of the primary discount driving the -55% drawdown.
trades.invalidation: A Complete Response Letter or an FDA extension of the review timeline past the 90-day window removes the rerating mechanism; additionally, any new financing at prices materially below the current $5.84 close or escalation of the securities class action (e.g., denial of insurance coverage) would invalidate the thesis.

trades.thesis: Supernus is an early-commercialization specialty pharma trading at -46% from its 1-year high on optically terrible financials (nine-month net loss $69.9M, $48.5M operating burn, FY2012 going-concern history, $22.2M derivative liabilities). The core of the bull case is a mechanical, filing-grounded rerating mechanism: quarter-lag revenue recognition has kept reported product revenue at de minimis levels ($1.3M) while underlying demand compounds — 11,773 cumulative Oxtellar XR prescriptions by September, ~108% sequential script growth, and $10.4M of shipped product sitting in deferred revenue plus 9,030 Q3-filled prescriptions explicitly slated for Q4 2013 recognition. The upcoming Q4 print (Feb 2014) is therefore the first quarter where reported revenue can converge toward true demand, potentially validating management's cash-flow-break-even-by-end-2014 projection and shrinking the perceived going-concern/dilution discount on a ~$6.90 stock. Liquidity is adequate near-term (~$102.5M cash+securities vs. $90M converts), buying time for the launch curve to play out. This is not a cheapness story — equity is $12.5M against $111M liabilities and dilution via the 7.50% converts is real — it is a launch-inflection story where the accounting lag creates a near-term information catalyst. Risks are symmetric and material: Watson's Paragraph IV challenge to Oxtellar XR patents, continued SG&A build ($14.6M/qtr), and residual financing risk if script growth disappoints. Position sizing should reflect small-cap illiquidity (~$3.4M ADV) and binary litigation overhang.
trades.catalyst: Q4 2013 earnings report (~Feb 2014): first quarter of shipment-based revenue recognition for Oxtellar XR plus release of the $10.4M deferred balance and recognition of Q3's 9,030 filled prescriptions should produce a step-change in reported product revenue versus the de minimis $1.3M nine-month base, forcing a reassessment of the break-even-by-end-2014 path. Secondary support: Trokendi XR launch ramp data and SPN-812 PK study initiation in H1 2014.
trades.invalidation: The thesis fails if Q4 2013 prescription TRx growth decelerates materially (Oxtellar XR momentum stalls after the 108% sequential jump), if gross-to-net deductions force large reversals of the deferred revenue, or if the company reverts to going-concern language or announces another dilutive financing before the Q4 print. A negative early development in the Watson Paragraph IV suit would also invalidate.

trades.thesis: Nu Skin trades at ~$50 (down ~46% from its 1-year high) against FY2013 record results ($3.2B revenue +49%, EPS $5.94 vs $3.52, 84% gross margin), implying roughly 8x trailing earnings. The drawdown reflects January 2014 People's Daily allegations and Chinese regulatory inquiries that prompted voluntary suspension of promotional meetings and new distributor applications in Mainland China (~32% of revenue). Critically, the filings frame these as voluntary, cooperative measures with management expecting short-term — not structural — damage, and the disclosed worst case (license revocation) is an extreme tail rather than the base case; likely fines and temporary restrictions are already heavily discounted in a stock that lost nearly half its value in days. The rerating mechanism is concrete: Q1 2014 earnings (due within ~5 weeks) will quantify the actual China hit, and any sign of resumed normal operations in the largest market should trigger sharp multiple recovery from single-digit P/E. Meanwhile the rest of the business (92% non-US, 53 markets, TR90 momentum with ~$550M LTO revenue) is intact, and capital returns are active: dividend raised to $0.345/quarter (payable 3/26) and $394.5M of buyback capacity — roughly 7% of the current market cap — providing per-share support precisely when the float is capitulating. Cheapness alone is insufficient here, but cheapness plus a dated, observable catalyst (earnings/regulatory clarity) plus bounded downside (68% of revenue outside China, modest debt, cash-generative model) meets the long-candidate bar. Expected value skews positive: partial recovery toward even half the prior valuation gap implies 40-70% upside, versus a tail loss if licenses were formally revoked.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2014 earnings report (late April) quantifying the actual China hit and providing guidance; any formal indication from Chinese regulators or company disclosure that promotional meetings/new-distributor applications are resuming; continued aggressive buyback execution at depressed prices.
trades.invalidation: Formal suspension or revocation of Nu Skin's direct-selling licenses in Mainland China, escalation of state-media attacks, extension of suspensions without a timeline past mid-2014, or Q1 disclosure showing Sales Leader/Active attrition spreading beyond China — any of which would shift the distribution toward the license-loss tail and force exit.

trades.thesis: Best Buy (inferred from FY2014 10-K, fiscal year ended 2014-02-01) is a deep-turnaround retail situation trading ~41% below its 1-year high at ~$16.45. The filings show a credible, partially de-risked Renew Blue execution story rather than mere cheapness: (1) return to profitability from continuing operations ($689M net earnings, $1.98 diluted EPS) after a FY2013 burdened by $822M goodwill impairments and $414M restructuring, with FY2014 restructuring down to $159M and no goodwill impairment — the P&L reset is largely complete; (2) material balance-sheet repair: cash up to $2.7B from $1.8B, debt reduced to $1,657M, current ratio 1.4 vs 1.1, $1.1B operating cash flow with capex cut to $547M; (3) unqualified auditor opinions on both financials and ICFR with no material weaknesses; (4) two of three rating agencies (Fitch BB-, S&P BB) moved outlooks from Negative to Stable, validating the credit inflection despite Moody's Negative outlook; (5) tangible transformation execution — ship-from-store at >1,400 locations, 1,400 Samsung and 600 Windows stores-within-a-store, phase-1 space optimization, plus completed portfolio pruning (Europe JV, mindSHIFT). The rerating mechanism is a scheduled, near-term catalyst: Q1 FY2015 earnings (~late May 2014) and the June 10 annual meeting, where stabilization of domestic comps and gross margin against easy post-impairment comparisons could force a re-rating of a stock priced for structural decline. The -41% drawdown embeds substantial pessimism, so even modest fundamental beats carry outsized upside, while the repaired balance sheet ($2.7B cash, reduced debt) makes the classic retail-turnaround failure mode (vendor credit tightening) less imminent. This is a genuine long candidate, not a value trap on cheapness alone — but conviction is capped by still-negative comps, gross margin at a five-year low (22.8%), and extreme supplier concentration (top 5 vendors ~45% of purchases, no long-term contracts).
trades.catalyst: Q1 FY2015 earnings report (~late May 2014) as the nearest hard catalyst: first full quarter to demonstrate whether Renew Blue cost savings and omnichannel initiatives (ship-from-store, vendor stores-within-a-store) can stabilize comps and gross margin; secondary: April proxy/June 10 annual meeting for capital-allocation signals given the untouched $4.0B buyback authorization.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q1 FY2015 results (due within the 90-day window) show continued domestic comp declines with further gross-margin erosion, or if vendors tighten payment terms/credit limits (the 10-K's explicitly flagged liquidity risk), or if Moody's downgrades from Baa2, re-opening the financing-cost spiral. A break back toward the 52-week lows on fundamental deterioration would confirm failure.

trades.thesis: Alnylam exits Q1 2014 with a transformed balance sheet (~$1.0B cash + securities after $723M Genzyme equity proceeds vs ~$41.7M quarterly operating burn — multi-year runway, no debt), which removes the primary existential risk for a clinical-stage biotech. The lead asset patisiran has encouraging preliminary Phase 2 OLE data (~80% sustained TTR knockdown, reduced infusion reactions with micro-dosing) and an ongoing APOLLO Phase 3, while Genzyme's $700M investment plus opt-in to the TTR franchise provides sophisticated third-party validation at prices far above the current $50.26. The stock sits 46% below its 1-year high, suggesting the market has over-discounted dilution and the headline $250.9M loss, which is dominated by a one-time non-cash $224.7M Sirna IPR&D charge rather than operational deterioration. A rerating mechanism exists via continued patisiran data flow and Phase 3 progress against a de-risked capital base; cheapness alone is not the thesis — it is funded pipeline optionality at a depressed price. Risks are real: no product revenue, -56% collaborator revenue decline, +97% R&D growth, further share issuance to Merck in Q2 with re-measurement exposure, and Merck lock-up expiry around September 2014 creating supply overhang. This supports a sized-but-not-maximal long candidate stance rather than conviction.
trades.catalyst: Continued patisiran OLE enrollment/data flow and any APOLLO Phase 3 enrollment or design updates over the summer, plus completion of the Sirna technology transfer (Q2 2014); validation of RNAi platform momentum following the April OLE knockdown and infusion-reaction data.
trades.invalidation: Negative patisiran OLE safety/efficacy updates, evidence of competitive displacement in the ATTR franchise, accelerated cash burn requiring nearer-term financing, or a decisive break below post-Genzyme-raise lows would invalidate the thesis.

trades.thesis: The issuer (Latin American e-commerce/classifieds platform) presents an asymmetric setup: fundamentals are accelerating (Q1 2014 net revenues +12.3% YoY to $115.4M, operating income +19%, net income +73% to $30.3M, EPS $0.69 vs $0.40) while the stock sits ~41.5% below its 1-year high at $82.04, implying the market has priced in the LatAm FX shock far more severely than its earnings impact. The rerating mechanism is credible and near-term: Brazil direct contribution grew +30.7%, sales & marketing spend was flat while product/tech investment scaled, and a Q2 report lands within the 90-day window offering a clean catalyst to re-anchor multiples on ex-Venezuela growth. Downside is tolerable: $218.5M cash + short-term investments plus $45M long-term investments versus only ~$9.5M debt, positive FCF (~$20.5M in Q1), and a committed $7.3M quarterly dividend. The bear case is concentrated but bounded: Venezuela ($73.9M net assets, ~21% of consolidated net assets, remeasured at SICAD 1 = 10.7 BsF/USD while SICAD 2 trades at 49.81, no repatriation since 2011) and Argentina (23% January peso devaluation; software tax holiday expiring Sept 2014 worth ~$0.05/share quarterly). Even a full Venezuelan write-off would be roughly 2% of the implied market cap, and Argentina's headwind is disclosed and quantified. Cheapness alone would be insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with double-digit growth, expanding margins, and a self-funded balance sheet — a genuine rerating setup rather than a value trap, provided one accepts LatAm macro volatility as the price of entry.
trades.catalyst: Q2 2014 earnings report expected in early August 2014 (within the 90-day window): if Brazil-led revenue growth and operating leverage persist despite the already-disclosed Argentine peso devaluation and SICAD-1 remeasurement, the market can re-rate a stock priced for FX distress back toward growth-multiple territory; continued dividend declarations (next payable Jul 15) reinforce the shareholder-return floor.
trades.invalidation: A further step-devaluation of the bolivar toward SICAD-2 levels forcing a large write-down of the $73.9M Venezuelan net asset position, a Q2 print showing Brazilian deceleration or margin compression, or disclosure that Argentine tax-holiday relief will not be renewed under the new law — any of which would confirm that FX/regulatory erosion is overwhelming core growth.

trades.thesis: Puma Biotechnology is a development-stage biopharma with no revenue, a widening Q1'14 net loss ($19.8M vs $11.8M YoY) and ~$17M quarterly operating burn, offset by a fortress post-offering balance sheet (~$196M cash+securities, no debt, runway through 2015 into 2016) following a February 2014 raise of $129.4M net at $122.50/share — nearly 77% above the current $69.40 price. The stock sits ~50% below its 1-year high, so much de-rating has already occurred and recent buyers at $122.50 anchor some valuation support. Lead asset PB272 (oral neratinib, licensed from Pfizer) is in multiple active HER2+ breast cancer and HER2-mutant tumor trials, providing real optionality. However, the filing discloses NO dated near-term catalysts — no readout dates, enrollment milestones, or regulatory events — so the required credible near-term rerating mechanism is absent. Cheapness is not demonstrable either: at ~$2.1B market cap versus ~$196M cash, the equity is almost entirely pipeline hope value. Bear-side quality flags include a growing unreserved $13.3M licensor receivable with slow collections, hedged liquidity messaging, reverse-merger shell history, and explicit future dilution warnings with ~5.2M option/warrant shares outstanding. This is a binary-outcome profile where a single trial result could move the stock ±50%; without a grounded, dated catalyst within 90 days, expected excess return is only modestly positive and dominated by variance.
trades.catalyst: None dated in the filing. The only plausible 90-day rerating mechanisms are (a) interim execution/progress news on the ongoing PB272 HER2+ breast cancer and HER2-mutant NSCLC trials, or (b) mean-reversion in a stock trading ~50% below its 1-year high with a clean, debt-free balance sheet. Absent a scheduled data readout or regulatory event, any rerating is speculative rather than mechanically driven.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated by disclosure of a dated dilutive financing before any positive clinical news, adverse safety/efficacy signals from PB272 trials, deterioration in licensor receivable collectability (reserve establishment), or continued breakdown below post-raise lows indicating loss of institutional sponsorship.

trades.thesis: Veeva trades at $20.75, ~55% below its 1-year high and ~21% below the March 2014 follow-on price of $26.35, despite fundamentals that are rare among 2014 cloud names: Q1 FY2015 revenue +56% YoY ($66.7M) with subscription revenue +74%, GAAP profitability (net income $7.2M), operating cash flow of $18.1M (~2.5x net income), deferred revenue building $7.5M sequentially to $74.9M, and a debt-free balance sheet with $345.5M in cash/investments (~13% of the ~$2.6B market cap). At roughly 8–9x forward EV/revenue for 55%+ growth with real GAAP margins, valuation is undemanding versus cloud comps of the era. The drawdown appears driven by technical/supply factors — the mostly-secondary follow-on (12.41M of 13.8M shares sold by insiders) and the June 16, 2014 lockup expiration (~88M shares eligible) — rather than fundamental deterioration. The bear case is governance (dual-class, 95.9% Class B voting power), rising opex growth outpacing revenue, EGC disclosure exemptions, and salesforce.com purchase commitments (~$496.7M through 2025). Cheapness alone is insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with accelerating fundamentals and an identifiable supply-clearing event within the forecast window, giving a credible rerating mechanism into the September Q2 print.
trades.catalyst: Post-lockup supply absorption after June 16, 2014 followed by Q2 FY2015 earnings (early September) where continued ~50%+ subscription growth and deferred revenue build could re-anchor the multiple toward the $26.35 offering reference price; no other dated catalysts appear in the filing.
trades.invalidation: Failure of the stock to stabilize within 2–4 weeks after the June 16 lockup expiration (sustained trade below ~$18–19), or Q2 FY2015 results showing subscription growth decelerating materially below ~50% YoY or deferred revenue stagnation — either would break the growth-plus-quality rerating mechanism.

trades.thesis: Sturm Ruger screens as a classic cyclical destocking trough rather than structural impairment. The filing shows Q3 sales -43% YoY, gross margin compressed to 24.1% from 36.8%, backlog down from 1.9M to 825K units, and OCF down to $31M from $84M — yet management's own data show underlying consumer demand down only ~3% (NICS-adjusted) versus -44% distributor sell-through, indicating the collapse is predominantly channel inventory correction, which is inherently mean-reverting once distributors reach reasonable levels. The stock is already down ~42% from its 1-year high, pricing substantial pessimism; at ~$31 with roughly 19M shares outstanding, EV is well under 5x annualized trough EBITDA for a debt-free franchise. The feared Q4 items are known and dated: ~$40M pension settlement expense (mostly non-operating, ~$8M cash) terminates a legacy obligation permanently, and the dividend was preemptively cut to $0.14 preserving cash. A credible rerating mechanism exists: the AR-556 launched end-September at a competitive price point with shipments ramping into Q4/Q1, positioning the company to recapture share in the largest category as destocking abates. Downside is tolerable given zero debt, $28.1M cash, unused $40M revolver, unencumbered assets, and cost actions already taken (production -36%, incentive comp -89%). This is a deep-value cyclical turn setup, not a cheapness-only bet: the catalyst path runs through Q4 earnings demonstrating destocking completion and AR-556 traction, with the one-time pension charge absorbed and guided.
trades.catalyst: Q4/full-year 2014 earnings report (~late Feb 2015, inside the 90-day window): first quarter with AR-556 volume shipments, evidence that distributor destocking has abated (orders stabilizing against a -3% underlying demand base), and clear demonstration that the ~$40M pension settlement charge is non-recurring — enabling the market to re-focus on normalized mid-cycle earnings power at ~4x EV/EBITDA rather than trough optics.
trades.invalidation: Q4-to-date order data or the February earnings report showing continued double-digit order declines, further backlog erosion, accelerating market-share loss to discounting competitors, or cash falling materially below ~$20M (forcing dividend elimination or revolver draw) would invalidate the trough thesis; also watch failure to renew the $40M revolver ahead of its June 15, 2015 termination.

trades.thesis: Beaten-down recently-IPO'd SaaS communications company trading at roughly $0.9B market cap (~68.1M shares x $13.07) against ~$215M annualized revenue growing 36% YoY — approximately 1.1x EV/Sales after netting $149.4M cash/ST investments against $27.2M debt. The rerating mechanism is credible: fundamentals are accelerating (gross margin ~66% and rising, deferred revenue +$6.9M YTD, operating cash burn cut from $(20.6)M to $(7.1)M), while the stock's -44% drawdown from its 1-year high suggests expectations have been fully reset after post-IPO/secondary lockup supply. Liquidity risk is minimal ($149M cash, covenant compliance, management runway assertion), so the main risks are sentiment-based rather than solvency-based. Cheapness alone would not suffice, but here cheapness coincides with intact hyper-growth and improving unit economics — a classic setup for multiple recovery in a high-growth SaaS name once overhang clears. Counterweights: GAAP losses are widening ($(38.2)M nine-month), SBC doubled to $11.3M, part of the burn improvement is an $11.3M accrued-liability build, and founder-controlled dual-class governance caps strategic alternatives. Position sizing should reflect small-cap beta and the possibility that loss-making SaaS stays out of favor.
trades.catalyst: Q4/full-year 2014 results (early 2015) showing sustained ~35%+ revenue growth and continued burn reduction against a depressed ~1x EV/S multiple; any upward revision or reaffirmation of the growth trajectory could trigger a sharp rerating given the stock's 44% drawdown and thin float dynamics typical of recent dual-class SaaS IPOs.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 results show revenue growth decelerating below ~30%, sequential deferred-revenue softness, or re-acceleration of cash burn; also invalidated by broader de-rating of unprofitable high-growth SaaS names or further insider selling into weakness.

trades.thesis: Exelixis-equivalent trades at ~$1.70 (~$332M market cap on ~195M shares) against $293.5M cash/investments — an enterprise value near zero after a -79% drawdown from its 1-year high, meaning the market has already repriced the COMET-1 phase 3 failure (65% workforce cut, $(58.5)M stockholders' deficit). The residual equity is effectively a free option on two credible mechanisms: (1) Genentech's cobimetinib NDA filing expected before year-end 2014 following the positive coBRIM phase 3 PFS readout at ESMO (Sept 29, 2014) — a partner-funded, dated regulatory catalyst; and (2) three ongoing cabozantinib phase 3 pivotal trials (RCC/HCC focus) providing 2015 binary upside. COMETRIQ revenue is growing (+32% YoY to $6.3M in Q3) and the restructuring materially cuts go-forward burn. This is not cheapness alone: there is a concrete near-term rerating event (NDA filing) inside the 90-day window. Offsets are real — $185.4M nine-month operating burn, $96.5M of converts now current, SVB collateral covenants, management's own warning that fundraising 'may be severely impaired' by COMET-1, and likely dilution — but at near-zero EV the asymmetry skews modestly positive, with the cash floor cushioning downside while catalysts play out.
trades.catalyst: Genentech's completion of the cobimetinib NDA filing before year-end 2014 (Fast Track designated, coBRIM PFS-positive), followed by advancing expectations for the three ongoing cabozantinib phase 3 pivotal trials (RCC/HCC) into 2015; any Deerfield extension closing also removes a stated condition on runway guidance.
trades.invalidation: Failure or delay of the Deerfield extension amendment (runway guidance is explicitly contingent on it), a deeply discounted emergency financing, adverse/slowed regulatory movement on cobimetinib, or any negative signal from the ongoing cabozantinib phase 3 program would invalidate the thesis; a sustained break below the cash-supported price floor (~$1.40-1.50) on volume would signal forced-seller dynamics overriding valuation support.

trades.thesis: Geron is a single-asset clinical-stage biotech (imetelstat) trading at $2.68, down ~52% from its 1-year high, after a March 2014 FDA full clinical hold crushed the stock. The critical subsequent event: the FDA removed the full clinical hold effective Oct 31, 2014 — days before the cutoff — reopening the path to myelofibrosis pilot study development. The balance sheet provides a floor: $142.5M cash+securities (~$0.91/share against 157.2M shares, ~34% of market price), no debt, ~$96.8M freshly raised at $4.00/share, and management-asserted 12+ month runway against modest burn (~$19.1M operating cash use over nine months). This is a credible near-term rerating mechanism (hold removal → trial restart → data path) combined with tolerable downside (cash floor, no debt, no near-term financing need). Risks are real: single-asset concentration, active securities/derivative litigation alleging misleading imetelstat liver-toxicity disclosures with no reserves, ~22% YoY share dilution, and residual hold/IND risk. But the setup — deeply depressed price, hold just lifted, funded program, cash floor — fits the long-candidate profile better than cheapness alone.
trades.catalyst: Resumption of imetelstat clinical activity following the Oct 31, 2014 full clinical hold removal — trial restarts, enrollment updates, and any early myelofibrosis pilot data readouts over the next 90 days; secondary: potential partnership interest in a de-risked, hold-cleared single asset.
trades.invalidation: Any new or re-imposed FDA clinical hold on imetelstat, disclosure of safety (liver toxicity) issues in restarted trials, a large dilutive financing at depressed prices, or adverse litigation developments; failure of the stock to hold the cash-supported floor (~$2.00-2.20) on trial-restart news would signal the rerating thesis is wrong.

trades.thesis: Coeur Mining enters the window deeply depressed (-69% from 1-year high, ~$3.75) with deteriorating fundamentals: Q3 2014 revenue fell 15% YoY, nine-month net loss widened to $(76.8)M, operating cash flow halved YoY, debt rose ~$152M since year-end, and the revolver was terminated leaving no committed backstop. The headline Q3 swing to $3.5M net income is low quality — driven by $16.1M favorable fair-value marks and a $16.6M tax benefit against a $(13.1)M pre-tax loss. Genuine positives are limited: $245.9M cash plus $49.5M investments, real cost cuts (G&A halved), positive Q3 operating cash flow, and a concrete near-term liquidity catalyst in the Franco-Nevada gold stream ($22.0M of deposits beginning Q1 2015). However, the 7.875% notes due 2021 trade below par ($408M FV vs $440M book), signaling the credit market sees elevated risk, and the equity's fate over 90 days depends overwhelmingly on gold/silver prices rather than any filing-grounded rerating mechanism. Cheapness plus optionality on a metals bounce is not a sufficient basis for a long; the required credible idiosyncratic rerating catalyst is absent.
trades.catalyst: Franco-Nevada gold stream $22.0M deposit begins funding in five quarterly payments starting Q1 2015 (within the 90-day window), plus continued G&A/amortization cost reductions; secondary catalyst would be a precious-metals price rebound given high operational leverage.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if Q4 results show renewed operating deterioration (further margin compression or negative operating cash flow), if the company must issue dilutive equity/debt to fund the March 2015 convert put or 2015 maturities, or if gold/silver prices break lower, pushing the sub-par 2021 notes toward distressed levels.

trades.thesis: Halozyme enters Q4 2014 trading ~48% below its 1-year high ($9.12 vs prior range up to ~$18), with the drawdown largely attributable to the mid-2014 PEGPH20 clinical holds that have since been resolved. The filing set shows a credible near-term rerating mechanism: FDA Fast Track (Sep 2014) and Orphan Drug (Oct 2014) designations for PEGPH20 in pancreatic cancer, removal of both clinical holds (Study 202 resumed Jul 2014 with >100 patients accrued; SWOG mFOLFIRINOX cleared Sep 2014), and a planned NSCLC trial start in Dec 2014 — concrete dated catalysts inside the 90-day window, with Study 202 data disclosure the primary rerating event. The balance sheet supports patience rather than forcing a raise into weakness: $134.5M cash/securities against ~$50M secured debt, guided FY2014 burn of $45–55M implies ~18–24 months runway, covenants are in compliance with no MAC, and amortization only begins Feb 2015. Revenue mix is improving structurally (new royalty stream $5.4M YTD, product sales +89% YTD on Herceptin SC/MabThera SC EU launches), partially offsetting the collapse in collaborative revenue. This is not a cheapness-only case: the stock's discount reflects resolvable clinical-execution risk, and the resolution mechanism is documented and dated. Position sizing must respect the binary nature of oncology data and the documented thromboembolic-event re-halt risk, which caps conviction at moderate levels.
trades.catalyst: PEGPH20 Study 202 data disclosure (interim/updated results in metastatic pancreatic cancer) plus December 2014 NSCLC trial initiation and conference-season updates (JPMorgan Healthcare Conference, January 2015); secondary support from Roche ENHANCE program momentum on Herceptin SC/MabThera SC EU launches generating royalties and potential milestone payments (~$55M clinical / ~$12M regulatory remaining under Roche/Pfizer collaborations).
trades.invalidation: A renewed clinical hold on PEGPH20 due to thromboembolic events, disappointing or delayed Study 202 data, an equity offering before the readout, or loss of Roche collaboration economics would invalidate the thesis; stop/reduce on any hold announcement or confirmed dilutive financing.

trades.thesis: Applied Optoelectronics shows a credible operating inflection: Q3 2014 revenue +76% YoY to $36.5M (9M +72%), gross margin up ~280bps to 33.2%, and a swing to GAAP profitability ($1.6M Q3 net income), driven by data center 10G/40G transceiver demand (+523.6% YoY, now 54.9% of mix). The stock at $11.74 is down 57% from its 1-year high (~$24-27 area, consistent with the March secondary at $24.25), implying the market has not yet re-rated the confirmed inflection; at ~$174M market cap (~1.2x TTM sales) for a company compounding revenue >70% with expanding margins, valuation is undemanding. Balance sheet is fortified ($45.8M cash/investments vs ~$23M debt after the $45.6M March raise, plus a post-quarter $14.0M revolver paydown), removing solvency risk during the capex ramp. This satisfies both prongs: a rerating mechanism (sustained hypergrowth + first profitability, with Q4 results as the natural catalyst window) and tolerable downside (net cash cushion, cheap relative to growth). Key discounts: extreme customer concentration (one data center customer = 49.5% of 9M revenue; top ten ~88%), poor cash conversion ($0.7M OCF vs $3.6M NI on a $15M inventory build with LCM charges doubling), declining China/CATV revenue, no Section 404 attestation, and disclosed China internal-control difficulties. These warrant position discipline rather than rejection, since the inventory build is plausibly deliberate capacity/demand positioning alongside the $24.8M capex program.
trades.catalyst: Momentum confirmation via Q4 2014 results (filed ~Feb-Mar 2015): if data center transceiver shipments sustain >50% sequential growth and gross margins hold above 33%, the market should re-rate a company compounding revenue >70% with fresh GAAP profitability and a de-levered balance sheet; the Oct 3 debt paydown and completed capex ramp remove execution financing overhangs ahead of that print.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 2014 results show data center revenue decelerating sharply or the anchor customer pausing orders (inventory was built ahead of this demand), or if gross margins compress below ~30%; a disclosure of material weakness in internal controls over China operations would also invalidate.

trades.thesis: Arrowhead Research (ARWR, $6.17, -77% from 1y high) enters the window freshly capitalized (~$172.6M net FY2014 equity raises; ~$132.5M cash + ~$44.7M investments ≈ $3.2/share vs. $6.17 price, ~50%+ of the ~$337M market cap in liquid assets), with an unqualified audit opinion and effective ICFR — so the drawdown reflects sentiment/binary-risk repricing, not accounting distress. Two dated catalysts sit inside the 90-day horizon: end-of-2014 regulatory filings for ARC-520 Phase 2b (chronic HBV) and ARC-AAT Phase 1, on top of completed Phase 1 tolerability across nine cohorts and ongoing Phase 2a dose escalation. That is a credible near-term rerating mechanism. It is offset by genuine fragility: zero revenue ($175K), $58.7M net loss with R&D doubling to $23.1M, explicit need for future dilutive capital, an admitted-unproven functional-cure hypothesis, price-adjustment warrant derivative volatility, and fresh securities class actions. Net: asymmetric-but-binary spec position where cash backing cushions downside while filings/data drive upside; sizing must reflect binary clinical risk.
trades.catalyst: ARC-520 Phase 2b regulatory filing (expected by end of CY2014, inside the 90-day window) plus ARC-AAT Phase 1 filing; potential additional upside from Phase 2a dose-cohort updates and 2015 pipeline nominations.
trades.invalidation: Slippage or withdrawal of the end-of-2014 ARC-520 Phase 2b / ARC-AAT filings; negative or ambiguous Phase 2a cohort data; announcement of a discounted equity raise; adverse development in the securities litigation.

trades.thesis: The issuer (a premium U.S. land contract driller, ~$38.58 close, -42% from 1-year high) presents a classic deep-cyclical drawdown setup with genuinely survivable finances: only $81M of debt against $251.6M cash + $165.6M AFS securities and $257.8M undrawn revolver, so bankruptcy/dilution risk is de minimis even in a prolonged downturn. Trailing results are strong (operating income +25.7% YoY, OCF $389.7M), but this is backward-looking: the filing's own subsequent-events disclosure shows U.S. Land rigs falling from 294 to 235 in five weeks, guidance below 200 by Q2 FY2015, >$60M of non-recurring early-termination revenue propping up optics, backlog shrinking to $4.6B with ~70% beyond FY2015, negative FCF after a $369M capex surge, $327.2M of outstanding rig-construction commitments, and $42M after-tax mark-to-market losses on the equity portfolio. Forward estimates will be cut repeatedly. The bull case rests not on fundamentals improving within 90 days but on (a) the -42% drawdown already embedding severe pessimism, (b) a fortress balance sheet that converts sector-wide oil-price stabilization/rig-count deceleration into outsized equity beta recovery, and (c) insider-aligned capital allocation (raised dividend, resumed $59.7M buyback). This is a credible rerating mechanism only conditional on a macro turn in crude — which I cannot underwrite from filings alone — so cheapness-plus-survival earns a watch, not a long. Base-rate skepticism on falling-knife energy services names caps my conviction: roughly coin-flip odds of positive excess return with fat left tail if oil makes new lows.
trades.catalyst: No dated company-specific catalyst within 90 days beyond routine dividend payment (Mar 2, 2015); the realistic rerating trigger is exogenous — stabilization or rebound in crude prices/land rig counts lifting sector multiples off trough levels, amplified by the stock's high beta to oil sentiment from a deeply depressed base.
trades.invalidation: Thesis weakens if U.S. Land rig count keeps making new lows without any oil-price stabilization through April–May 2015, if the company suspends the dividend/buyback or cancels FlexRig construction (signaling worse internal outlook than disclosed), or if an other-than-temporary impairment hits the equity securities portfolio — each would confirm a lower-for-longer regime where trough multiples compress further despite the clean balance sheet.

trades.thesis: Viper Energy Partners is a deeply oversold (-45% from 1y high), oil-levered Permian mineral-royalty MLP (~77% oil production, 91% oil revenue) whose drawdown is almost entirely a function of the WTI collapse from >$105 to <$45, not company-specific deterioration: royalty revenue grew to $77.8M FY2014 from $15.0M, production reached ~4,337 BOE/d in December 2014, and the cost-free royalty model (15.7% weighted royalty, no capex/opex) means cash generation is resilient and the balance sheet risk is limited to a modest secured facility. The rerating mechanism is credible but macro-contingent: any stabilization or rebound in oil prices over the next 90 days should disproportionately benefit this small-float (~$177.5M non-affiliate), high-beta royalty vehicle with 308 identified horizontal locations and a sponsor (Diamondback) with strong incentives to grow production on its own acreage. Offsetting this, governance is structurally poor (GP controlled by Diamondback, fiduciary duties waived, >80% call right, unlimited expense reimbursement), the key drop-down catalyst is purely discretionary with no contractual obligation, and a further leg down in oil would pressure the borrowing base and distribution coverage. This is a beta-recovery bet with tolerable downside, not a cheapness-only story — hence a modest-sized long candidate rather than high conviction.
trades.catalyst: Stabilization or rebound in WTI from sub-$45 levels restoring operator drilling economics and royalty cash flow visibility; potential Diamondback drop-down or acquisition (discretionary, undated) as upside optionality; oversold small-float MLP beta to any oil tape recovery.
trades.invalidation: WTI making new lows below the January 2015 sub-$45 print, a borrowing-base redetermination that forces repayment or distribution suspension, or a distribution cut — any of which would confirm that the cost-free royalty model cannot protect cash flow in a prolonged downturn.

trades.thesis: Ring Energy is a small-cap, 98% oil-weighted Permian E&P that just inflected to profitability ($8.42M FY2014 net income, $33.75M operating cash flow) on ~300% production growth (463,495 BOE vs 115,681 BOE), with 10.4 MMBOE proved reserves and PV-10 of ~$281.7M versus a ~$237M market cap (25.75M shares × $9.20) — a discount to pre-tax reserve value despite a growth inventory of 239 proven plus ~2,480 potential vertical locations. The stock is down ~55% from its 1-year high, so commodity weakness is substantially priced. The credible rerating mechanism is not cheapness alone: (1) the April 1, 2015 borrowing-base redetermination under the new $150M SunTrust facility (initial base $40M, suggesting modest drawn balances relative to cash generation) is a discrete, near-term event that, if neutral-to-positive, removes the most acute liquidity overhang; (2) high oil beta means any stabilization/rebound in crude disproportionately benefits this micro-cap; (3) 24 low-cost re-stimulation candidates offer capital-efficient production adds. Earnings quality caveats (~$4.2M non-cash deferred tax benefit, rising $25.20/BOE depletion, 93% two-customer concentration, related-party lease and Torchlight JDA) temper but do not negate the cash-flow story. Key risks are the ~57% PUD mix requiring capital in a falling-price tape, explicit disclosure that development may require equity/debt issuance, and full-cost ceiling write-downs that could trigger early credit-facility repayment. Position sizing should reflect micro-cap liquidity (~$1M ADV) and binary commodity exposure.
trades.catalyst: April 1, 2015 borrowing-base redetermination under the new SunTrust revolver (initial $40M base) — a reaffirmation or increase removes the nearest liquidity overhang; secondary catalysts are oil-price stabilization/rebound lifting small-cap E&P sentiment and resumption of Kansas drilling after the 3-D seismic evaluation.
trades.invalidation: (1) April 1 borrowing base cut or disclosure of drawn balances near the base; (2) WTI breaking decisively below ~$45, compressing hedged-unprotected cash flow and raising full-cost ceiling write-down risk; (3) announcement of a discounted equity raise; (4) further deferral of Kansas drilling resumption without a revised capital plan.

trades.thesis: Vanda (VNDA, $9.31, -43% from 1y high, ~$390M market cap) is transitioning to commercial-stage: Q1 2015 delivered $22.15M of first-ever product revenue (HETLIOZ $7.5M + newly transferred Fanapt $14.7M), net loss narrowed to $10.2M from $26.5M, and operating cash flow turned positive (+$5.6M). With $134.3M in cash/securities, no debt, and a ~$90M annualized revenue run-rate, EV is roughly $255M (~2.8x run-rate sales) — not deeply cheap, but the -43% drawdown suggests meaningful pessimism is embedded. The credible near-term rerating mechanism is the European Commission's final decision on HETLIOZ, expected mid-2015 and therefore inside the 90-day window, following an April 2015 CHMP positive opinion — approval is the high-probability outcome and would add an EU revenue leg to an inflecting P&L. This is a catalyst-driven setup, not a cheapness-only thesis. The edge is modest, not large: the stock has already de-rated, Fanapt revenue is partly transition/channel-driven, and the market may treat EU approval as largely priced.
trades.catalyst: European Commission final decision on HETLIOZ expected mid-2015 (within the 90-day window) following the April 2015 CHMP positive opinion — a high-probability approval event that would open a second geography for the lead product and validate the commercial transition narrative.
trades.invalidation: EC decision delayed past the window or issued with restrictive labeling; Q2 Fanapt revenue showing transition/channel-stuffing reversal (AR collection failure given 80% AR concentration in three customers); equity financing announced; adverse development in the ANDA suits.

trades.thesis: Akebia is a pre-revenue clinical-stage biopharma trading at $7.56, down ~74% from its 1-year high, with a market cap (~28.8M shares × $7.56 ≈ $218M) only modestly above pro forma liquidity of ~$165M ($100.3M cash/securities at 3/31/15 plus ~$64.6M net April 2015 follow-on proceeds).
