Enterprise value of roughly $50–55M is thin for an asset with positive Phase 2b data (safe, predictable hemoglobin raising in non-dialysis CKD anemia), a planned 2015 Phase 3 initiation, and a dated near-term catalyst: dialysis Phase 2 data expected Q3 2015, plus an end-of-Phase-2 FDA meeting in Q2 2015. The April raise at $8.25 de-risks near-term financing (≥12 months runway per management against ~$8.3M quarterly burn) and leaves recent buyers underwater, reducing immediate dilution pressure. This satisfies the two-part test: a credible, dated rerating mechanism (clinical/regulatory newsflow) and tolerable downside (cash floor covering ~75% of market cap, debt-free balance sheet). However, this remains a binary-event stock: the -74% drawdown and the discounted follow-on show the market has already punished execution/dilution history, and a negative dialysis readout would likely overwhelm the cash floor. Position sizing must reflect that asymmetry; conviction is moderate, not high.
trades.catalyst: Dialysis Phase 2 data expected Q3 2015 (within or just past the 90-day window), preceded by end-of-Phase-2 FDA meeting and start of Phase 3 in non-dialysis CKD anemia during 2015 — a dated, filing-grounded rerating path.
trades.invalidation: Slippage of the Q3 2015 dialysis readout or Phase 3 start beyond the window, negative end-of-Phase-2 FDA meeting feedback, accelerating burn toward another raise, or adverse development in the FibroGen patent disputes would invalidate the thesis.

trades.thesis: Small-cap direct seller trading at -45% from its 1-year high despite explosive reported fundamentals: Q2 net sales doubled YoY to $69.7M (H1 $110.4M vs $57.4M), operating income doubled to $12.3M at ~80% gross margin, H1 operating cash flow of $39.5M built cash to $74.4M on a debt-free balance sheet. At ~$7.69 the equity appears deeply undervalued relative to run-rate earnings and net cash, with shareholder-friendly capital returns ($6.1M buybacks, dividends, new $15M authorization). A concrete catalyst exists: the June 2015 funding of a CNY 20M mandated deposit toward a mainland China direct selling license application, which could unlock the largest addressable market within the forecast window. Key discounts applied: (1) earnings/cash-flow quality is partly float-driven — deferred revenue ($8.2M), accrued commissions ($14.3M), and distributor eWallet balances inflate both revenue conversion and OCF, and commissions now consume >50% of sales; (2) extreme Hong Kong/China concentration with FX controls and direct-selling regulatory risk; (3) director/>5% holder Broady selling into company-funded buybacks and a full DTA valuation allowance. These justify sizing discipline but do not defeat the valuation-plus-momentum setup: the market has already de-rated the stock 45%, so much model/regulatory skepticism appears embedded in price while reported growth keeps accelerating.
trades.catalyst: China direct selling license application (CNY 20M deposit funded June 2015) plus continued quarterly beats; new $15M buyback authorization and dividend declared on filing date provide near-term support.
trades.invalidation: Q3 results showing decelerating revenue or commission ratio rising further above 50% of sales; any regulatory action or negative commentary on China/HK direct-selling model; loss of cash build or reversal of deferred revenue/eWallet float.

trades.thesis: RYAM at $7.34 (-73% from 1y high, ~$310M market cap vs ~$1.1B EV) screens as a cash-flow-driven value/turnaround: Q3 2015 shows a genuine operating inflection (gross margin 27.2% vs 22.0% YoY, operating income +$16M, net income $32.3M vs $19.4M) driven by a $40M cost savings plan, $21M of cost declines, and higher commodity volumes; nine-month adjusted FCF of $92M and OCF of $152M imply a high-teens FCF yield on EV, while $52.1M of term loan repayment, $100M cash, $236M revolver availability, and trivial near-term maturities (~$2.1M remaining 2015) make the leveraged balance sheet survivable near term. The stock's deep drawdown means expectations are reset, and the Q3 momentum plus dividend initiation give a credible rerating path. The thesis is NOT cheapness alone — it is cheapness plus a demonstrated quarterly earnings inflection. The dominant risk is the Eastman litigation (largest customer, ~31% of revenue, seeking to void the contract), a binary overhang that caps conviction and creates real tail risk, alongside industry softness (CS prices -7-8%, China smoking policy, destocking) and a $(17)M stockholders' deficit. Position as a sized, catalyst-aware long candidate rather than a high-conviction bet.
trades.catalyst: Q3 earnings momentum carrying into Q4 prints (cost savings plan ramping, commodity volume gains), continued deleveraging headlines, and any de-risking of the Eastman dispute; deep -73% drawdown leaves expectations reset so even in-line results can drive a sharp rerating in a ~$310M market cap name.
trades.invalidation: Adverse Eastman litigation development (ruling or escalation voiding/limiting the supply agreement), renewed cellulose specialties price cuts or guidance reduction in the Q4 print, or covenant/liquidity stress signals that would convert the thin-equity, $893M-debt balance sheet into a solvency story.

trades.thesis: Coeur Mining (CDE, ~$2.70, -63% from 1y high) is a leveraged precious-metals producer priced for distress: the 7.875% Senior Notes trade at ~61% of par ($260M FV vs $426.5M BV), shares are up ~32% YTD from Paramount dilution, and the just-announced $54M note-for-equity exchange adds another ~11% dilution. Offsetting this, operating cash flow is genuinely improving ($69.1M nine months vs $52.4M prior year), Q3 costs applicable to sales fell YoY, Wharf contributes accretive production, and management executed a concrete deleveraging step on the filing date itself with term-loan lender consent for up to $100M of equity issuance. The equity is effectively an out-of-the-money call option on gold/silver prices layered on top of a self-help deleveraging story. However, the rerating mechanism is incomplete: the exchange is dilutive rather than accretive per share, FCF is roughly breakeven after capex, revenue is still declining, and Bolivia/San Bartolomé poses write-down risk. Cheapness plus distress is not enough without a metal-price tailwind, which cannot be grounded in the filings. Convex upside exists if metals stabilize, but the base rate for deeply leveraged juniors at 61-cent bonds continuing to underperform over a 90-day window argues against committing capital now.
trades.catalyst: Completion of the $54M Senior Notes-for-equity exchange and potential use of the lender-approved $100M equity issuance window ahead of the Feb 1, 2016 redemption deadline; any stabilization in gold/silver prices would disproportionately benefit this leveraged producer via the discounted notes and improving mine-level cash margins.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if gold/silver prices make new lows after the cutoff, forcing further dilutive equity issuance beyond the consented amount or asset-level stress at the secured mines; also invalidated if the note exchange terms slip toward the 14.7M-share maximum or additional liability-management actions signal deepening distress rather than a one-time cleanup.

trades.thesis: Century Aluminum (CENX, $4.28, -86% from 1y high) is a deeply washed-out commodity-cyclical where every specialist signal is bearish — Q3'15 gross loss $(42.4)M, $31M LCM write-down, Ravenswood closure, WARN notices to fully curtail Mt. Holly and cut one Sebree potline by Dec 31, OCF collapsed to $32.5M from $97.7M. The bearish fundamentals are largely known and priced at a ~$370M market cap against $123M cash and $247M senior notes. The contrarian case rests on supply-side mechanics rather than cheapness alone: Century's own Mt. Holly/Sebree curtailments, alongside industry-wide smelter shutdowns, remove high-cost capacity exactly when LME aluminum and Midwest premiums are at multi-year lows — a classic cycle-bottom configuration. A credible rerating mechanism exists within 90 days: stabilization or recovery in LME/premiums post-curtailments flows directly to a leveraged equity with no incremental dilution assumed. Downside is bounded but real: Glencore's take-or-pay contract covers substantially all 2015–2016 North American output (revenue floor despite negative unit economics), $123M cash plus undrawn revolver provide a bridge, and the worst-case news (full Mt. Holly curtailment) is already telegraphed via WARN notices. This is a small, asymmetric position candidate, not a core holding: the fundamental trajectory is deteriorating, and the bet is on commodity-price mean reversion plus supply discipline, with roughly balanced-to-modestly-positive expected excess return versus SPY over 90 days.
trades.catalyst: Aluminum price/Midwest premium stabilization into year-end combined with announced North American smelter capacity closures (including Century's own Mt. Holly/Sebree actions) tightening supply; any Santee Cooper power resolution or partial reprieve for Mt. Holly before Dec 31 would be an immediate positive surprise off a washed-out base.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if LME aluminum makes new lows after the Dec 31 curtailments without a broader industry response, if Q4 results reveal covenant stress or revolver/borrowing-base deterioration, or if the company signals equity issuance — any of which would shift this to reject.

trades.thesis: Sarepta into the Feb 26, 2016 eteplirsen PDUFA is a binary regulatory lottery ticket, not an investable rerating setup. The bull case rests entirely on FDA approval of a drug whose efficacy data are already legally contested — securities plaintiffs explicitly allege misrepresentations about NDA data sufficiency, and the market prices deep skepticism ($25.07 close, -40% from 1y high, ~36% below the Oct 9 offering price of $39.00). Priority review of an exon-skipping NDA with a surrogate (dystrophin) endpoint carries elevated complete-response risk versus naive priority-review base rates. Downside is severe and asymmetric: zero product revenue, accelerating burn ($118.2M operating outflow in 9M 2015, Q3 net loss $51.9M vs $29.2M YoY), committed launch pre-spend that must be unwound on rejection, senior secured debt covenants, and a stated runway of only twelve months even after the $120M raise — meaning a CRL forces immediate retrenchment and dilution. Governance adds friction: interim CEO since March 2015, litigation overhang. Cheapness relative to the offering price reflects genuine information, not mispricing. With roughly even-to-negative event odds and a fat left tail, expected 90-day excess return is materially negative; the position fails both the credible-rerating-mechanism test (mechanism exists but is adverse-skewed) and the tolerable-downside test.
trades.catalyst: Eteplirsen NDA priority review with PDUFA action date February 26, 2016 (~110 days post-cutoff), plus any FDA advisory committee meeting on the contested dystrophin data that would surface before or around the action date.
trades.invalidation: A clearly positive FDA advisory committee vote on dystrophin as a valid surrogate, or early approval/accelerated-approval signals ahead of the PDUFA date, would flip the setup to a long candidate; conversely this thesis is confirmed by any CRL, adcomm negativity, or data-integrity disclosures.

trades.thesis: Corcept shows a genuine commercial inflection: Korlym net product revenue roughly doubled YoY (Q3 $13.261M vs $7.282M; nine months $35.319M vs $17.537M), producing the first positive quarterly operating income ($102K vs $(5.103)M) and cutting nine-month operating cash burn to $(1.033)M from $(25.973)M. With $36.45M cash after $19.7M of warrant/option exercise proceeds and management guiding to cash-flow breakeven without new raises, the balance sheet supports the story near-term. The stock trades ~42% below its 1-year high (~$4.18), so the market has not yet credited the profitability inflection; dated catalysts inside the 90-day window (TNBC Phase 1/2 efficacy data by end-2015, CORT125134 Phase 2 starts in Q1 2016) provide a credible rerating mechanism beyond mere cheapness. Offsets are real but manageable within the horizon: the uncapped-from-2016 Biopharma royalty obligation (~$29.9M remaining, change-of-control acceleration to $45.0M with IP collateral), single-source manufacturing, method-of-use-only patents, and non-GAAP presentation that excludes SBC and accretion. Net: fundamental inflection + near-term catalysts + de-risked liquidity against a washed-out price gives an asymmetric setup, tempered by small-cap beta and binary pipeline risk.
trades.catalyst: Initial triple-negative breast cancer Phase 1/2 efficacy readout by end of 2015 and CORT125134 Phase 2 trial starts in both Cushing's and oncology in Q1 2016, both landing inside the 90-day window; secondary: Q4/full-year 2015 results confirming sustained profitability and cash-flow breakeven.
trades.invalidation: Q4 2015 revenue growth deceleration or receivables/rebate deterioration suggesting channel stuffing or gross-to-net erosion; a disappointing TNBC efficacy readout; any new equity raise at depressed prices contradicting the breakeven claim; covenant breach triggering the punitive 50%-of-sales royalty step-up.

trades.thesis: Deckers trades at a -44% drawdown from its 1-year high (~$9.20) with every specialist flagging the same bear story: six-month operating loss of $(12.5)M, $(328)M operating cash burn, inventories up 149% to $595M, receivables +$142M, and short-term borrowings surging from $5.4M to $316.8M while cash fell to $99.8M. The skeptical read is that this is largely a seasonal working-capital build for a December-concentrated brand (UGG), amplified by a ~210 bps FX-driven gross-margin hit and discretionary debt-funded buybacks — not structural demand collapse: Q2 net sales still grew +1.4% YoY and the quarter itself was profitable ($36.4M net income). The stock appears to have de-rated on optics (cash burn + leverage) rather than fundamentals. A credible 90-day rerating mechanism exists: the fiscal Q3 (December quarter) report in late January 2016 should show holiday sell-through converting the inventory/receivable build back into cash and paying down short-term borrowings; continued execution against the ~$102.9M remaining buyback authorization provides direct share support at depressed prices; and management asserts 12-month liquidity sufficiency with covenant compliance and ~$93M unused revolver capacity. With expectations washed out after a -44% drawdown, even in-line December-quarter execution (stable margins, working-capital normalization) offers asymmetric upside versus SPY, while the deep discount limits relative downside if the season disappoints modestly. This is a contrarian, event-driven long sized for the residual risk that margin erosion (closeouts, sheepskin costs, rising doubtful-account provisions) proves structural rather than transitory.
trades.catalyst: Fiscal Q3 (December quarter) earnings report in late January 2016: confirmation of holiday sell-through, reversal of the $355M inventory and $142M receivable builds into operating cash inflow, paydown of the $317M short-term borrowings, and stabilization of gross margin would directly refute the distress narrative and drive rerating; ongoing buyback execution (~$102.9M remaining) provides continuous support into the print.
trades.invalidation: Failure of holiday sell-through evidenced by: (1) inventories not declining materially and/or heavy incremental markdowns in the Q3 report; (2) short-term borrowings not being paid down toward normal seasonal levels by the March quarter; (3) further gross-margin compression beyond FX (closeouts, sheepskin costs); (4) any disclosure of credit facility amendment, covenant pressure, or reduced buyback activity. Any of these converts the seasonal-build thesis into a structural deterioration thesis and exits the position.

trades.thesis: Hovnanian presents a sharp tension: genuine operating momentum (backlog value +42.1% to $1.2B, net contracts +16.2%, sales pace +5.6%, communities +9.0%) against a stressed balance sheet — $1.85B senior debt, $128M equity deficit, $320.5M FY2015 operating cash burn, and a revolver with only $2.1M remaining capacity. The dominant 90-day variable is a funding wall: $172.7M of 6.25% notes mature 2016-01-15 (within weeks of cutoff) and $86.5M of 7.5% notes 2016-05-15, with management explicitly warning refinancing may not be available on attractive terms. Mitigants exist — ~$300M of newly expanded land banking capacity (Domain $125M + GSO $175M) shows third-party capital engagement, land options offer walk-away flexibility, and audit opinions are clean — but the outcome is close to binary and the equity sits below a large debt stack with covenant-restricted dividends and entrenched family control (~58% votes, 4.9% rights plan) that forecloses takeover/activist rescue paths. Cheapness (-58% from 1y high) alone does not clear the bar; the rerating mechanism depends on a refinancing not yet announced. With roughly symmetric-but-fat-tailed outcomes, this warrants watching for confirmation of the January maturity resolution rather than initiating now.
trades.catalyst: Resolution of the January/May 2016 note maturities via refinancing or extension — successful execution would remove the dominant overhang on an equity trading ~58% below its 1-year high with accelerating backlog; failure or punitive pricing would be the negative catalyst.
trades.invalidation: A failed or materially dilutive/punitive refinancing of the January 2016 notes, further revolver exhaustion, or Q1 FY2016 order/backlog deterioration (especially in Texas) would invalidate any constructive view; conversely, a completed refinancing at acceptable terms converts this to a long candidate.

trades.thesis: Royal Gold enters Feb 2016 down ~55% from its 1-year high with an operating inflection that the market has not yet paid for: Q2 FY16 revenue grew ~60% YoY to $98.1M and operating income swung to +$27.2M as newly acquired streams (Pueblo Viejo silver effective Jan 1, 2016, Golden Star, Andacollo) began delivering. The six-month net loss is optical — driven by a one-time ~$64M tax charge on the Andacollo termination, not operations. Liquidity is adequate ($442.3M total including $300M undrawn revolver; covenants affirmed), covering dated commitments ($70M Golden Star payments, possible $75M Rainy River trigger). The rerating mechanism is credible: contractual stream ramps give visible sequential GEO/revenue growth into the May-quarter report, and the stock is levered to any stabilization in gold after a severe drawdown. Risks are real — debt doubled to $677.5M, ~90% gold revenue sensitivity, four-asset concentration (~65% of FY15 revenue), and Thompson Creek's distress threatening Mount Milligan — but they argue for sizing discipline rather than rejection. Cheapness alone is insufficient here; what earns the long candidacy is the dated delivery ramp plus depressed valuation.
trades.catalyst: Pueblo Viejo silver stream deliveries began Jan 1, 2016 and Golden Star Wassa underground production expected mid-2016 (stream stepping to 10.5%), driving sequential revenue/GEO growth into Q3 FY16 reporting (~May 2016); any stabilization or rebound in gold from the $1,106/oz quarter average would flow through at near-pure margin given the royalty cost structure.
trades.invalidation: Renewed gold-price breakdown below quarter-average levels (~$1,050-1,100/oz) compressing stream margins and reviving impairment risk on the ~$860M development/exploration-stage carrying value (incl. $380.7M Pascua-Lama); evidence of covenant stress or a dividend cut; material adverse development at Mount Milligan operator Thompson Creek.

trades.thesis: Malibu Boats at $12.78 (down ~47% from its 1-year high) pairs genuinely strong operating momentum with a credible near-term rerating mechanism. Q2 FY16 net sales +9% ($60.5M), six-month operating income +58% ($16.3M) on gross margin expansion and G&A discipline, and a swing to +$13.6M operating cash flow (vs -$4.4M) demonstrate the business is executing well despite the stock's de-rating. The $15M buyback authorized Feb 1, 2016 — funded from cash on hand against a $14.9M cash balance — is a concrete, dated catalyst that directly supports the share price into the seasonally strong spring selling season and the May fiscal Q3 print. Valuation is undemanding for the growth rate (annualized H1 net income ~$17M against a market cap in the mid-$200Ms, roughly mid-teens P/E). The bear case is real but mostly structural and known: a $96.6M TRA liability against a stockholders' deficit, ~10x higher interest expense from the 2015 term loan, an $11.7M immaterial NCI error correction, decelerating domestic retail demand, and a MY2016 warranty extension. These overhangs explain the discount but are largely priced in at a 47% drawdown; the first TRA payment (~$3M) is manageable and removes uncertainty. Cheapness alone would not qualify this, but cheapness plus a dated buyback catalyst plus accelerating operating leverage does.
trades.catalyst: Execution of the newly authorized $15M buyback (Feb 1, 2016) into a stock already down ~47% from its 1-year high, followed by fiscal Q3 FY16 results (May 2016) covering the seasonally strongest spring selling quarter; first TRA payment (~$3M) settling in April/May removes a known overhang rather than creating a surprise.
trades.invalidation: Fiscal Q3 FY16 results (due ~May 2016) showing flat-to-down net sales, gross margin compression, or further inventory build would confirm the demand-deceleration risk and invalidate the rerating thesis; failure to commence buyback execution by late Q2 2016, or any covenant amendment/waiver, would also be disqualifying.

trades.thesis: Beazer Homes (BZH, ~$8.04, -62% from 1y high) shows a verified operating inflection: Q1 FY2016 revenue +29.6% to $344.4M, gross margin 16.7% vs 13.2%, operating income swung to +$9.1M from -$9.5M, net income positive. At a deep drawdown with ~$633M book equity (~$19/sh) against an $8 stock, much distress is priced in. The credible near-term rerating mechanism is twofold: (1) resolution of the $148M 8 1/8% June 2016 note maturity — management repurchased $5M in Jan 2016 and intends open-market refinancing, with $144.9M cash plus $116.4M revolver capacity as fallback, so refinancing success removes a key overhang; (2) spring selling season results extending the West-driven momentum (+80% revenue). Downside is tolerable but not trivial: seasonal cash burn ($77.8M used in ops), ~2.4x debt/equity, B3/B- ratings, rising capitalized interest flattering margins, resumed small impairments, and water-intrusion litigation tails. This is a leveraged, high-beta recovery bet where fundamentals have inflected but the balance sheet remains the swing factor — sized as a candidate, not a conviction position.
trades.catalyst: Successful open-market refinancing or redemption of the June 2016 8 1/8% notes (management already repurchasing, $5M in Jan 2016) removes the maturity-wall discount, compounded by fiscal Q2 spring selling-season results showing sustained West-segment momentum and margin expansion.
trades.invalidation: Failure or materially punitive terms on the 2016 Notes refinancing; Q2 FY2016 orders/backlog deterioration or renewed impairments beyond token levels; further cash burn pushing unrestricted cash below comfortable coverage of the maturity plus seasonal burn.

trades.thesis: Deeply distressed Appalachian integrated E&P/coal name trading ~74% below its 1-year high at $7.33, with ~$2.79B long-term debt against a small equity base. Fundamentals are deteriorating: FY2015 swung to a $(374.9)M net loss on an $824.7M shallow-gas impairment, unhedged realizations halved to $2.13/Mcfe, Appalachian basis is negative and forecast to widen, Noble's ~$1.6B drilling carry remains suspended, and management itself acknowledges a funding shortfall between operating cash flow and growth capex. Offsets are real but defensive rather than rerating-oriented: ~223.6 Bcf of 2016 gas hedged at $3.26/Mcf, covenant headroom (5.32x coverage vs 2.50x min), a reaffirmed $2B revolver borrowing base, $343M of recent CNXC IPO proceeds, and a slashed $205–325M capex budget. The claimed ~15% 2016 production growth depends on a discretionary mid-year drilling decision and deferred wet-gas completions, so it is not a bankable catalyst. What would drive a rerating — a durable natural gas price recovery or a dated separation event — is either outside the company's control or explicitly undated. At a -74% drawdown there is embedded mean-reversion optionality, but skeptical base rates for leveraged commodity producers at cycle troughs argue against paying up for that optionality now; cheapness plus survival is not a sufficient long case without a credible 90-day mechanism.
trades.catalyst: No dated near-term catalyst within the window: the mid-year 2016 drilling capital allocation decision is contingent on commodity prices, H2 2016 debottlenecking benefits accrue to 2017 volumes, and the E&P/Coal separation is an explicitly undated aspiration. Any rerating would most plausibly come from natural gas price recovery lifting unhedged realizations off the $2.13/Mcfe trough rather than a company-specific event.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidates if natural gas strip prices make new lows into spring injection season, if the mid-year drilling decision defers new shale drilling outright (confirming growth guidance is unachievable), or if any sign emerges of borrowing-base reduction, collateral posting requirements, or further large reserve impairments — any of which would compress the equity toward distress pricing given the $2.79B debt load.

trades.thesis: The filing evidence is overwhelmingly bearish on operations: Q2 FY16 sales fell 22% YoY ($524.0M vs $675.6M), Industrial segment margin collapsed to 2.4% from 11.2%, energy end-markets declined ~33%, and the quarter was dominated by non-cash value destruction — a $106.1M preliminary goodwill impairment in Infrastructure (goodwill there fully written off), a $133.3M loss on divesting businesses for only $61.1M net proceeds, and $112.2M of restructuring charges after $388.8M a year earlier. Management credibility is strained by repeated large charges two years running, and the impairment is explicitly preliminary with finalization expected in Q3 FY16, creating a known near-term negative-event risk. Against this, the balance sheet is survivable: $139.0M cash, an essentially undrawn revolver against $706.7M total debt, covenant compliance affirmed, positive six-month operating cash flow of $104.5M, and a maintained/raised dividend — though cash flow quality depends partly on finite working-capital drawdown. The one genuine potential rerating mechanism is governance: an abrupt CEO change on February 3, 2016 (DeFeo replacing Nolan) immediately before cutoff, which historically accompanies strategic resets at distressed industrials, plus Phase 1 restructuring completion by June 2016. However, the filings provide no forward guidance, backlog data, or evidence that demand has troughed, so any upside relies on speculative management action rather than documented inflection. Cheapness after a -50% drawdown alone does not satisfy the long-candidate bar; the risk/reward is roughly balanced with fat left-tail risk from further impairments and continued organic decline.
trades.catalyst: Phase 1 restructuring completion by end of FY2016 (June 30, 2016) with realized savings (~$19M/quarter run-rate), plus the newly installed CEO's strategic review following the February 3 leadership change; secondary support from raw-material cost tailwinds and eventual stabilization of channel destocking.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 FY16 results (due ~April 2016) show continued double-digit organic decline without sequential order/backlog stabilization, additional goodwill impairment beyond the preliminary charge, or erosion of the working-capital-supported cash flow; conversely, only a demonstrated demand trough plus concrete new-CEO capital-allocation/cost actions would upgrade this to a long candidate.

trades.thesis: Neurocrine is a clinical-stage biotech trading at $33.70, ~42% below its 1-year high (~$58), in a sector-wide drawdown, with a credible near-term rerating mechanism: valbenazine (NBI-98854) is in Phase III for tardive dyskinesia — a market with zero approved therapies — with data expected during 2016, plausibly inside the 90-day window. Prior Phase IIb evidence and the Mitsubishi Tanabe $30M up-front licensing deal suggest external validation of the asset. The balance sheet is unusually clean for the stage: ~$460M cash/investments, no debt ever, $424M equity, giving multi-year runway at current burn and removing near-term financing/dilution pressure ahead of the catalyst. Unqualified E&Y opinions on financials and ICFR rule out accounting-quality concerns. Offsets are real: widening losses ($88.9M net loss, R&D up ~75%), ~13% share count growth, direct VMAT2 competition from Teva's SD-809 (NDA filed for Huntington's chorea), a Mount Sinai license-breach suit tied to the AbbVie collaboration, and no commercial infrastructure. The setup is a binary-catalyst bet entered at a depressed price with a cash floor (~$5/share) and tolerable downside: a failed trial would likely take shares back toward the lower end of the 12-month range, while success re-rates toward prior highs. Cheapness alone is not the case — the case is a dated Phase III readout in an unmet-need indication from a well-funded balance sheet after a deep drawdown.
trades.catalyst: Valbenazine Phase III (KINECT 3) tardive dyskinesia topline data expected within the 90-day window; a positive readout supports NDA filing for the first-ever approved TD therapy and validates retained US commercial rights plus the Mitsubishi Tanabe ex-US deal, driving a multiple re-rate off a depressed base. Secondary support from AbbVie's continued elagolix Phase III progress.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if valbenazine Phase III misses statistical significance or shows an unfavorable safety profile (first-in-class status would collapse value toward cash floor); also invalidated by adverse Mount Sinai litigation developments impairing elagolix economics, disclosure that Teva's competing SD-809 files/commercializes materially earlier, or a new equity raise signaling runway stress before the readout.

trades.thesis: Small-cap unstructured-data security software vendor trading near post-IPO lows after a ~63% drawdown, yet the just-filed FY2015 10-K shows genuine fundamental inflection: Q4 2015 revenue of $43.8M (+30% YoY) with sequential growth every quarter, license mix rising to ~64% of revenue, ~92.5% gross margins, >90% maintenance renewal rates three years running, and the first GAAP-profitable quarter in company history. The Q4 earnings report lands within days of the cutoff and constitutes a concrete, dated rerating catalyst: confirmation of profitability plus 30% growth against deeply depressed expectations creates asymmetric upside. Downside is partially mitigated by the recurring maintenance base and the fact that expectations are already near trough, though not eliminated — the model is heavily back-end loaded (most deals close in the last three weeks of each quarter), expenses are fixed short-term, and management will guide into a seasonally weak Q1, so a miss or soft guide could extend the downtrend. Net: credible near-term rerating mechanism with tolerable, but real, downside; this is a sized-modestly long candidate rather than a table-pounding setup given missing balance-sheet/cash-flow data and dilution optionality flagged in the filing.
trades.catalyst: Q4/FY2015 earnings report due within days of cutoff: disclosure of first GAAP-profitable quarter ($2.6M net income on $43.8M revenue, +30% YoY) with rising license mix could force a rerating off post-IPO lows; secondary catalyst is FY2016 guidance framing the growth/profitability trajectory.
trades.invalidation: A Q4 print/guidance that misses (revenue below ~$43M trend or renewed GAAP loss), weak Q1 2016 guidance beyond normal seasonality, any equity raise announcement, or loss of the >90% renewal-rate claim would invalidate the thesis; technically, sustained trade below the post-IPO low (~$13.25 area) signals structural demand failure.

trades.thesis: Vanda enters the window deeply de-rated (-45% from 1y high, $7.94 close) largely due to the January-February 2016 biotech drawdown plus a credible but manageable Fanapt generic-cliff narrative. The filing set shows a real commercial inflection — revenue more than doubled to $109.9M in FY2015 from $50.2M, AR grew ~4.5x tracking the HETLIOZ/Fanapt ramp — supported by $143.2M cash and securities versus roughly a $340M market cap (~42% cash coverage), which cushions downside. A dated, quotable catalyst sits inside the 90-day window: the Fanapt long-term maintenance sNDA PDUFA in May 2016, backed by positive June 2015 Phase III data, plus an expected 2016 German HETLIOZ launch and multiple planned Phase III starts in 2H16. Clean PwC audit and effective ICFR remove accounting-quality concerns despite the gross-to-net rebate accrual surge ($0.5M -> $35.6M), which is a scaling artifact rather than a red flag per se. The bear case (Nov-2016 Fanapt NCE expiry, five ANDA filers, widening losses, funding-sufficiency caveats, ~17% option/RSU overhang) mostly bites beyond the 90-day horizon since paragraph IV settlements/stays typically delay generic entry past NCE expiry. This is a modest-conviction long candidate: rerating mechanism exists and downside is buffered by cash, but the setup is volatile and catalyst outcomes are binary-ish.
trades.catalyst: Fanapt long-term maintenance sNDA PDUFA decision in May 2016 (~3 months out), preceded by Q4-2015/Q1-2016 results evidencing the HETLIOZ/Fanapt revenue ramp; secondary support from expected 2016 German HETLIOZ launch and planned 2H-2016 Phase III starts.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4-2015 results reveal HETLIOZ prescription/revenue deceleration or materially worse gross-to-net than the rebate accrual implies, if the company announces a dilutive financing before the PDUFA, or if pre-PDUFA news flow suggests an FDA complete-response risk on the Fanapt sNDA.

trades.thesis: Zillow Group enters the window down ~51% from its 1-year high ($19.18 close 2016-02-11) despite grounded fundamentals that are far stronger than the price action implies: FY2015 revenue nearly doubled to $644.7M (+98%, Trulia-aided), Adjusted EBITDA grew to $87.6M, and liquidity is ample ($523.3M cash/investments and $493.7M working capital against only $230M of 2.75% convertible notes due 2020). The Trulia integration restructuring (~350 headcount reduction) and Market Leader divestiture are complete, so the heaviest one-time costs are behind. The disclosed spring/summer seasonal peak in home sales supports Premier Agent ad spend into Q2, and the first clean post-integration quarterly print is the natural rerating trigger within the 90-day window. The bear case is real but mostly non-cash or backward-looking: the $(148.9)M GAAP loss is dominated by $105-120M of share-based comp and $63M amortization, while operating cash flow of $22.7M remains positive. This is a beaten-down, liquid ($16.7M ADV), still-growing franchise where sentiment — not solvency — drove the derating; cheapness alone would not qualify it, but the combination of deep drawdown, intact demand metrics (123.7M average monthly unique users, +61% YoY), completed restructuring, and a seasonal/catalyst path to a positive print makes it a sized-long candidate with defined invalidation.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2016 earnings report (expected early May 2016, within the 90-day window) as the first clean post-integration quarter, showing whether revenue momentum (+98% FY2015, 123.7M monthly unique users +61% YoY) converts into narrowing losses and stable Agent Advertiser counts during the seasonally strongest spring/summer home-selling period; secondary: resolution or favorable development in the June 2016 trade secrets trial removing the legal overhang.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q1 2016 results show sequential Agent Advertiser declines accelerating (92,366 in Q4 2015 was already down from 103,415 in Q1), revenue guidance implying organic deceleration post-Market Leader divestiture, further OCF deterioration below ~$20M/quarter, or adverse developments in the June 2016 trade secrets trial; a sustained break below the pre-cutoff low on volume would also invalidate the oversold-rerating setup.

trades.thesis: Pre-commercial specialty pharma (abuse-deterrent oxycodone, Xtampza ER) trading at $15.39, down ~46% from its 1-year high, with a dated, high-probability rerating mechanism inside the 90-day window: FDA PDUFA goal date of April 26, 2016 for final NDA approval. The binary is unusually de-risked: tentative approval was granted November 6, 2015, and a February 2016 District Court of Massachusetts judgment in the company's favor removed the Purdue Orange Book patents that caused the 30-month stay, with the Request for Final Approval submitted February 26, 2016. Runway into 2018 (including January 2016 follow-on proceeds) means financing pressure should not force action before the catalyst. This is a catalyst-driven setup, not a value setup — cheapness/fundamentals are irrelevant here (no revenue since 2010, $27.0M FY2015 net loss, rising commercialization losses). The stock has already been de-rated ~46%, so much approval-related skepticism may be priced in, but a clean approval plus launch progress typically drives a meaningful re-rate in a small-cap pre-revenue name. Downside is tolerable but real: a CRL, a narrower-than-expected abuse-deterrent label, or launch delays would likely retrace toward lows; remaining Purdue claims and dilution risk are live. Position as a sized catalyst trade, not a core holding.
trades.catalyst: FDA final approval decision for Xtampza ER at the April 26, 2016 PDUFA goal date (~39 days post-cutoff), followed by commercial launch; approval is heavily de-risked by existing tentative approval and the removal of the patent-stay trigger via the February 2016 court judgment.
trades.invalidation: A CRL, complete response, or approval delay past the PDUFA date; a materially narrowed abuse-deterrent/sprinkling label versus expectations; an equity raise announced before approval signaling runway stress; adverse development in Purdue's remaining patent claims.

trades.thesis: Freeport-class deep-cyclical at ~$9.47, down 54% from its 1-year high, with a credible near-term rerating mechanism: ~$3.75B of signed asset sales (Morenci 13% to Sumitomo $1.0B closing Q2 2016; TFHL/Tenke 70% to CMOC $2.65B; Black Stone royalties $102M closing Q2 2016; Timok $135M already closed May 2) explicitly earmarked for debt repayment against $20.8B total debt. The Q1 2016 $3.8B oil & gas full-cost ceiling impairment is non-cash and backward-looking; operations remain cash generative ($740M OCF, costs and capex cut sharply) with ~$3.0B revolver availability bridging to sale closings. The equity is an out-of-the-money option on deleveraging execution and copper/moly stabilization: if Morenci and royalty sales close on schedule and the Lundin ROFO window on Tenke resolves without exercise, the market should re-rate the survival narrative well before the Q4 Tenke close. Cheapness alone would not qualify, but here cheapness is paired with dated, contracted cash inflows — the required rerating mechanism. Position sizing must respect the stressed balance sheet: equity of $3.7B vs $20.8B debt, springing collateral trigger, dividend ban through March 2017, exhausted ATM capacity, and negative quarterly FCF (~-$240M) mean execution missteps are punished severely.
trades.catalyst: Near-term closings of Morenci 13% ($1.0B, Q2 2016) and Black Stone royalty sale ($102M, Q2 2016) fund immediate debt paydown; resolution of Lundin's 90-day ROFO on the $2.65B Tenke/TFHL sale (window expiring within the forecast horizon) removes the key execution overhang; Timok $135M already closed May 2. Commodity price stabilization plus ~$3.75B of signed disposals against a 54%-drawdown valuation drives equity rerating.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if (1) Lundin exercises its ROFO or the CMOC deal is renegotiated/terminated, (2) Morenci or royalty sale closings slip past Q2 2016, (3) copper prices break below early-2016 lows re-triggering full-cost ceiling impairments, or (4) Indonesia fails to renew PT-FI's export license after August 8, 2016 — any of which would re-open solvency questions with equity at only $3.7B vs $20.8B debt.

trades.thesis: LendingTree enters mid-2016 with strong fundamental momentum — Q1 2016 revenue +86% YoY to $94.7M, operating income doubled to $11.8M, positive and growing operating cash flow ($8.1M) — yet the stock trades ~47% below its 1-year high (~$73 vs. implied ~$138), reflecting the late-2015/early-2016 de-rating of online lenders and rate-hike fears. The disconnect between accelerating fundamentals and a compressed multiple is the core rerating case. Balance sheet is clean: $174.2M cash, no debt, undrawn $125M revolver, and management asserts 12+ month runway. Aggressive capital return ($40.6M repurchased in Q1, ~$56.7M authorization remaining) against a small ~11.9M-share float provides a persistent per-share accretion and scarcity mechanism. Governance is clean (effective disclosure controls, no new risk factors, no off-balance-sheet items). Key offsets: growth is marketing-driven (S&M ~69% of revenue, doubling YoY), so margin expansion is modest; the 41% effective tax rate post-valuation-allowance-release caps GAAP net income leverage; discontinued Loans operations remain a litigation drag; and mortgage-marketplace revenue is rate-sensitive. Cheapness alone is not the thesis — the thesis is accelerating marketplace fundamentals plus buyback support at a deeply discounted price, with tolerable downside given net cash and positive FCF.
trades.catalyst: Continued quarterly revenue beats from the personal-loans marketplace vertical plus aggressive buyback execution against a small float; any de-risking of the discontinued Loans litigation tail would remove a persistent discount.
trades.invalidation: Q2 2016 results showing revenue growth decelerating sharply or marketing efficiency deteriorating (revenue growth falling well below marketing spend growth), renewed large litigation charges from the discontinued Loans business, or a rate-driven drop in lender-marketplace inquiry volumes.

trades.thesis: Micron screens as a classic memory-cycle trough candidate rather than a structurally impaired business. The 10-Q documents maximum pessimism: net sales -25% YoY, gross margin compressed to 17% from 31%, a $(215)M quarterly net loss, and a stock already down ~41% from its 1-year high at $11.61. At this point in DRAM/NAND cycles, marginal producers are loss-making, which historically enforces supply discipline and precedes ASP stabilization; the equity typically inflects well before reported earnings do. The rerating mechanism is concrete rather than purely valuation-based: (1) the pending ~$4.1B buy-in of the remaining 67% of Inotera with Taiwan regulatory approvals already received and a hard outside date of November 30, 2016 — squarely inside the 90-day window — which would consolidate accretive wafer economics Micron currently only captures via equity method; (2) announced restructuring targeting ~$80M/quarter of savings; (3) $5.65B cash and investments providing a buffer while the cycle bottoms. Downside is tolerable because the stock is deeply de-rated, liquidity is adequate near-term, and the largest tail risk (prolonged pricing slide plus secured-debt-funded capex) is real but partially mitigated by the cash position and revolver. This is a contrarian cyclical-timing position, not a quality-compounder bet: sizing must respect that memory pricing could stay depressed longer than the base case.
trades.catalyst: Inotera buy-in completion window (outside date November 30, 2016; Taiwan approvals already received) plus the September-quarter FY16 earnings report as the first checkpoint for sequential ASP/margin stabilization; both fall inside the 90-day forecast horizon.
trades.invalidation: September-quarter results showing another sequential decline in blended ASPs and gross margin (i.e., no trough confirmation), further inventory build beyond $2.9B without order support, or failure/termination of the Inotera transaction (funding conditions unmet or Nanya private placement collapse) — any of which would extend the downcycle and pressure the already-stretched secured-debt-funded capex program.

trades.thesis: Gray Television enters the heart of the 2016 even-year political advertising cycle with strong confirmed operating momentum: Q2 revenue +37% YoY to $196.6M, operating income +39%, and H1 operating cash flow up 36% to $44.0M (exceeding net income), driven by the $443M Schurz acquisition now fully integrated into the run-rate. The stock trades at $7.81, down ~42% from its 1-year high, implying a deeply discounted EV (~$2.1B net of $176M cash against $1.71B debt) relative to annualized EBITDA that will be amplified by Q4 political spend — the filing itself flags that even-year political ads are heaviest in Q4, which lands inside the 90-day forecast window along with the Nov 8 election. This provides the required credible rerating mechanism rather than mere cheapness. Key offsets are material: leverage jumped ~$485M to $1.71B with interest expense +31%, revolver access is covenant-constrained (first lien net leverage ratio), intangibles of $1.89B dwarf $457M equity creating impairment sensitivity, corporate/admin costs grew +82%, and a dual-class structure with no dividend limits support. On balance, the dated political-cycle catalyst plus demonstrated operating leverage against an already-depressed valuation gives a favorable but not high-conviction asymmetry; position sizing must respect the leveraged balance sheet.
trades.catalyst: Q3 earnings (late Oct 2016) revealing accelerating political ad bookings ahead of the November 8 election, plus full-quarter contribution from the Schurz stations; potential upward revisions to FY2016 political revenue expectations driving a rerating of the depressed equity.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 results (due late Oct 2016) show political pacing materially below even-year norms or if acquired-station contribution disappoints such that leverage-adjusted EBITDA growth stalls; also invalidated by any covenant pressure limiting revolver access or signs of national/core ad softness overwhelming the political bump.

trades.thesis: LSB enters the window with a rare fully-funded rerating mechanism: the $364M Climate Control sale to NIBE closed July 1, 2016 (revolver repaid at closing), and management has stated intent to use net proceeds to repay debt and/or redeem the punitive 14% Series E redeemable preferred ($227.3M liquidation preference, ~$19.5M of H1 dividend+accretion drag). A material Q3 gain on sale is already guided, giving a dated positive disclosure event. Against this, the remaining chemical/fertilizer core is deteriorating badly (H1 operating loss $(26.2)M vs +$8.2M, gross margin collapse on UAN -28%/HDAN -39%, cash down to $22.8M after -$146M H1 FCF), with an unresolved securities class action, Golsen family entrenchment, and a Dec 3, 2016 warrant registration deadline. At $8.70 (-69% from 1y high), much distress is priced in, and deleveraging of $200M+ of claims against a sub-$700M common equity base is mechanically meaningful per share. This clears the bar of credible near-term mechanism plus tolerable downside, but only marginally — position as a modest catalyst trade, not a value hold, since cheapness here reflects genuinely loss-making operations.
trades.catalyst: Q3 2016 report (~November): booked material gain on Climate Control sale plus concrete announcement of debt repayment and/or Series E preferred redemption from the $364M proceeds, cutting annual fixed charges (14% preferred dividend/accretion run-rate ~$19.5M H1 alone plus senior note interest) and mechanically improving equity value.
trades.invalidation: Management fails to commit proceeds to debt repayment/preferred redemption (hoards cash or funds further El Dorado capex), Q3 gain comes in below expectations, or fertilizer prices keep deteriorating so continuing-ops losses widen despite lower leverage; also any adverse development in the securities class action.

trades.thesis: PCRX at $32.15 is down ~60% from its 1-year high, and the Q3 2016 10-Q shows the damage is overwhelmingly a discrete, quantified event rather than demand deterioration: a $21.9M COGS charge ($20.7M inventory reserve) from a single out-of-specification EXPAREL batch discovered in October 2016. Strip that out and the quarter shows ~+8-10% YoY product sales growth ($66.1M Q3, $198.3M nine months), positive nine-month operating cash flow (+$16.1M), and adequate liquidity ($161.1M cash + short-term investments vs. $107.6M converts due Feb 2019). The market appears to be pricing a structural margin collapse and regulatory crisis when the filing describes a bounded, single-batch quality event with planned FDA product-exchange communications. A credible near-term rerating mechanism exists: containment of the exchange to one batch plus Q4 results demonstrating normalized gross margins would re-anchor estimates toward the pre-charge earnings power. Downside is tolerable because the balance sheet covers near-term obligations, cash burn is modest, and the -60% drawdown has already de-rated expectations; residual risks (DOJ subpoena overhang, deep-in-the-money convert dilution, 85% top-three customer concentration, single manufacturing site) cap but do not dominate the setup. This is not cheapness alone — it is a specific, quantifiable one-off masking an intact growth asset at a distressed price.
trades.catalyst: Resolution of the October 2016 EXPAREL batch/FDA product-exchange matter (scope confirmation limited to a single batch) plus Q4 2016 results demonstrating normalized gross margins and continued double-digit EXPAREL sales growth, which would reframe the Q3 loss as non-recurring and drive multiple recovery off a washed-out base.
trades.invalidation: FDA communications expanding the affected-batch scope or triggering a broader recall/recall-related consent action; Q4 2016 results revealing gross-margin impairment beyond the reserved amount (e.g., multi-batch stability failures or manufacturing-site remediation costs); DOJ subpoena escalating to formal enforcement with material provisions; or EXPAREL prescription trends rolling over, converting the thesis from 'one-time charge' to 'demand/margin structural problem.'

trades.thesis: Deep-trough offshore driller (Transocean profile: $9.59 pre-cutoff, -43% from 1-year high) where the survival question has been materially deferred: $2.53B cash vs only ~$1.07B debt due within one year, maturity wall pushed out via $1.25B 9.00% 2023 notes and $600M 7.75% 2024 secured notes, plus $1.35B of debt retired below par generating $148M gains. Nine-month FCF was roughly breakeven-positive ($1,278M OCF vs $1,072M capex). The dated catalyst is the related-party Partners buy-in closing in Q4 2016 (unitholder vote Nov 11), removing structural overhang. At a 43% drawdown with solvency risk deferred well beyond the 90-day window, the equity behaves as a high-beta call option on offshore/oil sentiment; any cyclical stabilization or macro energy catalyst can produce large positive excess returns, while the fundamental deterioration (revenue -44% YoY, $276M termination revenue, ongoing held-for-sale impairments) is already heavily discounted in price. This is not a value thesis on fundamentals — it is a liquidity-defused, catalyst-dated, high-beta trough setup with asymmetric but volatile payoff.
trades.catalyst: Partners merger unitholder vote (Nov 11, 2016) and Q4 2016 completion removes an overhang; beyond that, any stabilization in crude/offshore sentiment would drive outsized beta catch-up in a deeply oversold driller trading 43% below its 1-year high.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the merger closes without any re-rating response while Q4 backlog disclosures reveal further contract losses/dayrate resets, or if operating cash flow trajectory implies cash burn against the $2.5B buffer within four quarters; a renewed leg down in crude that re-prices default risk in offshore drillers would also invalidate.

trades.thesis: CXW trades at $10.33 after a -59% drawdown from its 1-year high, a decline driven by the August 2016 DOJ announcement to phase out privately operated federal prisons rather than by deteriorating unit economics. The Q3 2016 10-Q (filed at cutoff) shows the underlying business still functioning: revenue +3.3% YoY, operating income +13% YoY on flat expenses, and nine-month operating cash flow essentially flat at $301.2M. Liquidity is adequate ($42.7M cash + $471.7M undrawn revolver capacity net of $418M drawn) with no debt maturities until April 2020, so there is no near-term refinancing event to force crystallization of the bear case. The stock is priced for severe contraction while current-period fundamentals are merely mixed (rising interest expense, nine-month net income down YoY). The credible rerating mechanism is the November 8, 2016 presidential election: one candidate has campaigned on expanded immigration enforcement and detention, and a favorable outcome could reverse or neutralize the DOJ phase-out directive and shift demand toward ICE/detention contractors — precisely the segment where CCA just extended its South Texas contract through September 2021. This is a policy-optionality trade on a deeply discounted, cash-generative REIT, not a cheapness-only thesis: the discount exists because of a binary political catalyst occurring within days of the cutoff. Downside is tolerable because the asset still produces ~$400M annual operating cash flow, carries no 90-day maturities, and retains unused equity issuance capacity ($200M ATM), though dividends (~$192M YTD) exceed free cash flow and the ICE repricing effective November 2016 caps near-term earnings upside if the status quo persists.
trades.catalyst: The November 8, 2016 US presidential election, four days after cutoff: an outcome favoring stricter immigration enforcement and continued/reversed use of contracted detention facilities would directly attack the regulatory overhang that caused the -59% drawdown, forcing a rapid re-rating of a stock priced for secular decline. Secondary: Q4/full-year results demonstrating the Trousdale Turner ramp and cost cuts offsetting the ICE South Texas repricing.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the election outcome preserves the DOJ phase-out posture and ICE/detention budgets stay flat or shrink; confirmation would be additional customer repricings on South Texas terms, occupancy declines at newly ramped facilities (Trousdale Turner), a dividend cut, or renewed ratings pressure forcing revolver dependence. A post-election rally that fully retraces without fundamental support would also warrant taking profits rather than holding.

trades.thesis: Genco is a distressed dry-bulk owner trading at $3.32 (post 1-for-10 split), down ~78% from its 1-year high, with explicit going-concern doubt: $40.0M cash vs $540.5M debt reclassified as current, nine-month operating cash burn of $(45.9)M, no revolver availability, and covenant waivers expiring November 15, 2016 subject to Sinosure non-objection. Ordinarily this profile is uninvestable. What makes it a candidate is a specific, funded rerating mechanism rather than cheapness: (1) a $125M preferred equity raise priced at $4.85/share — above the current common price — backed by institutional commitments, plus a commitment letter for a New Facility of up to ~$400M that directly addresses the going-concern condition; (2) executed deleveraging (Genco Sugar/Pioneer/Leader sold Oct–Nov 2016 with proceeds paying down facilities, Samsun settlement income); (3) narrowing Q3 operating loss ($(20.1)M vs $(35.3)M yoy) and cost cuts slowing the burn; and (4) a dry-bulk freight cycle that bottomed in early 2016, so the asset/revenue backdrop is no longer deteriorating as fast. If the recapitalization closes around the November 15 waiver deadline, the going-concern discount compresses rapidly against a tiny ~$24M common market cap and thin liquidity; the $4.85 preferred price provides a concrete anchor above the $3.32 common. The payoff is convex: successful recap plus cyclical recovery drives a large excess return, while failure means near-total loss. This is a small-position, event-driven candidate, not a quality long — sizing must respect the bankruptcy tail.
trades.catalyst: Closing of the recapitalization package — execution of the ~$400M New Facility and issuance of the $125M preferred at $4.85 — which extinguishes going-concern doubt ahead of/around the November 15, 2016 covenant-waiver expiry; secondary support from continued deleveraging asset sales and seasonal/cyclical dry-bulk rate recovery off 2016 lows.
trades.invalidation: Sinosure written objection voiding the 2014 Term Loan waivers, failure to sign/close the New Facility before or shortly after the November 15, 2016 waiver expiry, or breach of the $25M minimum cash condition — any of which triggers cross-default acceleration across all nine facilities and probable Chapter 11, reducing common equity toward zero. Also invalidate on recap terms implying heavy common dilution below current price.

trades.thesis: ACAD is a newly commercial biopharma trading ~49% below its 1-year high ($21.69 vs ~$42), with the rerating mechanism being the NUPLAZID launch ramp: first product revenue of $5.3M in Q3 2016 under a conservative sell-through model ($1.9M deferred), with sequential quarterly sales prints as the visible catalyst. Downside is cushioned by $588.9M cash/investments, no debt, and management's 12+ month runway statement after ~$497.5M of 2016 follow-on raises — roughly 22% of the ~$2.6B market cap in net cash. Key offsets: accelerating burn ($147.2M 9M operating cash use), SG&A up ~149% YoY, a securities class action with motion to dismiss denied (Dec 16 reconsideration hearing), and ~23% registered-share insider overhang. The setup is a funded launch at a deeply de-rated price where prescription uptake data can drive rerating, but the ramp is unproven and litigation is an unquantified tail. Modest positive expected excess with wide dispersion; not a high-conviction position.
trades.catalyst: NUPLAZID prescription uptake and Q4 2016 sales ramp disclosure (first full commercial quarters), plus resolution of the Dec 16, 2016 class-action reconsideration hearing; sell-through model implies $1.9M deferred revenue converts to recognized sales, providing visible sequential revenue momentum.
trades.invalidation: Ruling or discovery developments in the securities class action implying material settlement exposure; Q4 NUPLAZID net sales flat or down sequentially versus Q3's $5.3M; new equity issuance or guidance implying cash runway below twelve months.

trades.thesis: Ionis (IONS, $31.46, -51% from 1-yr high) offers a credible near-term rerating mechanism: SPINRAZA met primary endpoints at both Phase 3 interim analyses (ENDEAR Aug 2016, CHERISH Nov 2016) and is under FDA Priority Review and EMA Accelerated Assessment, making an approval decision plausible within the 90-day window. A positive decision would validate the antisense platform's most advanced partnered asset (Biogen) and support milestone/royalty expectations across the collaboration portfolio. Downside is tolerable: $687.8M cash+short-term investments vs $648.5M debt/obligations, converts not due until Oct 2019/Nov 2021, and Q3 showed GAAP profitability ($7.4M net income) on $110.9M revenue from Biogen/Janssen option exercises. Skeptical offsets: earnings quality is low (one-time license fees; 9M net loss $(112.4)M, operating cash flow $(86.1)M), deferred revenue is being drawn down, and ~11.2M conversion shares plus entrenched charter provisions cap upside mechanics. The stock's 51% drawdown suggests pessimism already embedded, so an approval-driven positive surprise skews the payoff asymmetrically, but this is a catalyst-dependent position, not a quality compounder.
trades.catalyst: SPINRAZA regulatory review timeline: FDA Priority Review and EMA Accelerated Assessment of a Phase 3-positive neuromuscular drug imply a likely regulatory decision inside the 90-day window; approval would trigger Biogen launch economics (royalties/milestones) and a valuation reset for Ionis's partnered pipeline.
trades.invalidation: A negative or delayed regulatory outcome on SPINRAZA (complete response letter, extended review), or disclosure that approval economics (royalty tier/timing) are materially worse than expected, removes the rerating mechanism; also invalid if post-Q3 burn accelerates such that new partnership upfronts become necessary within the window.

trades.thesis: LXU trades at ~$6.75, down ~43% from its 1-year high, with an equity market cap of only ~$192M (28.4M shares) against $356.7M net cash realized from the Climate Control divestiture ($60M cash at YE2016) plus $15–20M of pending non-core asset sales. The dominant, quote-grounded catalyst is a formally initiated strategic alternatives process (sale/merger possible) with Morgan Stanley retained — a credible, dated rerating mechanism rather than mere cheapness. Fundamentals are dire (FY2016 gross loss of $(49.3)M, ag selling prices down 28–34%, interest expense up to $30.9M), but the marginal story is improving: the new El Dorado ammonia plant is producing above nameplate (>1,300 tpd vs 1,150) heading toward ~95% on-stream in 2017, and ~$12M/yr of SG&A/plant cost cuts take effect in 2017. With the asset-sale proceeds roughly exceeding the entire equity value, downside appears partially floored, while any deal progress offers asymmetric upside. Risks are real: $375M senior secured notes (principal concentrated 2019), Series E preferred redeemable as early as Aug 2, 2019 (~$139.8M + $88M accrued dividends), restricted use of disposition proceeds, extensive anti-takeover defenses, and insider control concentration — all of which cap conviction and argue for position sizing discipline.
trades.catalyst: Resolution or tangible progress in the Morgan Stanley-advised strategic alternatives process (sale/merger of whole or parts), amplified by the newly ramped El Dorado ammonia plant (>1,300 tpd, ~95% on-stream expected 2017) restoring EBITDA into any valuation discussion; secondary support from $15–20M non-core asset sales closing.
trades.invalidation: Announcement that the strategic alternatives process concludes without a transaction (standalone plan), especially paired with weak Q1 2017 results showing the ammonia ramp/cost cuts failing to close the gross-loss gap, or disclosure of covenant stress restricting use of disposition proceeds.

trades.thesis: Sarepta enters March 2017 down ~48% from its 1-year high at $32.71 (~$1.8B market cap on 54.8M shares) with $329.3M in cash/equivalents/investments — roughly 18% of market cap — and management-stated runway of at least twelve months, so there is no financing cliff inside the 90-day window. The rerating mechanism is concrete: EXONDYS 51, the first disease-modifying therapy approved for DMD (accelerated approval, Sept 2016), posted $5.4M in its first partial year, and the 90-day window should reveal the true slope of the U.S. launch ramp via quarterly revenue. Orphan-drug economics (small exon-51 population, premium pricing) mean even modest patient starts can move the revenue narrative sharply, and the stock's depressed level reflects the 2016 regulatory controversy rather than launch fundamentals. That said, this is a high-variance name by its own disclosure (+74%/-55% single-day moves), with genuine tails: full approval hinges on FDA post-marketing requirements, BioMarin interference appeals could threaten commercialization, and the company explicitly plans further capital raises beyond the runway period. Net: modestly positive expected excess return driven by launch-ramp optionality against a cash-supported floor, but sized as a candidate, not a conviction position.
trades.catalyst: Quarterly EXONDYS 51 revenue prints demonstrating a steep launch ramp (annualized run-rate re-rating toward peak exon-51 sales), plus progress on EU approval path and the planned 2017 PPMO IND filing extending the pipeline narrative.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if quarterly EXONDYS 51 revenue shows a flat or decelerating ramp (payor/reimbursement pushback), if FDA signals dissatisfaction with post-marketing commitments, or if an adverse USPTO interference ruling emerges; a large equity raise would also undercut the liquidity-floor argument.

trades.thesis: Puma Biotechnology is a pre-revenue biotech trading ~57% below its 1-year high (~$30.30) with an explicit going-concern disclosure, ~$194M liquidity against ~$36M/qtr burn (~5 quarters runway), no committed financing, heavy SBC (~41% of net loss), and active litigation (securities class action with MTD denied, derivative suits, CEO defamation suit). Ordinarily this profile is uninvestable. What changes the calculus is a single, dated, high-magnitude catalyst: the neratinib NDA (filed July 2016) with FDA approval expected approximately 2H 2017 — squarely inside the 90-day window. The stock's drawdown suggests substantial pessimism is already embedded, so the payoff is asymmetric IF approval lands: a first product approval converts the narrative entirely and can re-rate the equity sharply, while a complete response letter or delay would compound the funding story and likely produce a severe decline (cash covers only ~5 quarters and commercialization plans are unfunded). This is a legitimate long candidate on catalyst grounds, not cheapness — but sizing must respect that it is effectively a binary regulatory bet with ~27% tail risk of a >40% drawdown, partially offset by the fact that much bad news (going concern, litigation, cash trajectory) was disclosed in the just-filed 10-Q.
trades.catalyst: FDA action on the neratinib NDA expected approximately 2H 2017, i.e., plausibly inside the 90-day window; approval would convert a pre-revenue, going-concern-flagged shell into a commercial company and drive a sharp multiple re-rating off a depressed base.
trades.invalidation: An FDA complete response letter, a refusal-to-file/deferral pushing the decision beyond the window, an emergency financing at depressed prices, or adverse developments in the securities class action would invalidate the thesis; a sustained break below the post-filing low with no regulatory news flow would signal the market is pricing a CRL.

trades.thesis: LULU at $48.27 is 40% below its 1-year high after a GAAP-driven selloff that conflates a contained, small-brand cleanup (ivivva: ~40 of 55 stores closing, $50-60M total FY17 charges, $17.7M already booked in Q1) with core-business deterioration. The core brand is actually improving on the metrics that matter: revenue +5% YoY to $520.3M, gross margin +110bps to 49.4%, adjusted operating margin +50bps to 12.1%, adjusted diluted EPS up YoY ($0.32 vs $0.30). The genuine bear points — comps -1% on traffic, flat e-commerce conversion, OCF halved to $19.4M on inventory build — are real but modest in magnitude and partially cyclical/investment-driven. Downside is cushioned by a fortress balance sheet ($698.3M cash, no debt, $149.2M undrawn revolver) worth roughly $5/share, ongoing buybacks, and the fact that the restructuring charge is front-loaded and dated, setting up easier comparisons in H2. With the stock pricing in brand-level distress that the adjusted P&L does not support, the setup offers a credible rerating mechanism (restructuring execution + Q2 print in late August showing charge roll-off and margin stability) with tolerable, cash-floored downside. Cheapness alone would not qualify; here cheapness coincides with intact core economics and a defined, near-term catalyst path.
trades.catalyst: Execution of the dated ivivva restructuring (charges front-loaded in Q1, tail costs in Q2/Q3) removing the drag; Q2 FY2017 earnings in late August as the nearest rerating event; company-disclosed activist risk implies potential activist involvement could force capital return/operating focus; continued buybacks under the $100M authorization.
trades.invalidation: Q2 FY2017 results showing continued or worsening comparable-sales/traffic declines, further core-brand margin erosion beyond restructuring charges, another guidance cut, or failure of operating cash flow to recover as restructuring charges roll off — any of which would indicate the problem is demand-driven, not brand-portfolio cleanup.

trades.thesis: Boot Barn-equivalent western/work-wear retailer trades at $6.21, down ~63% from its 1-year high, implying roughly $165M equity value and ~$383M EV against $59M Adjusted EBITDA (~6.5x). The market is pricing retail-apocalypse distress, but the filings show a stabilizing, profitable operator: same-store sales inflected positive (+0.3% FY2017 vs -0.1%), net income rose to $14.2M from $9.9M, EBITDA held flat through an energy-state downturn, and the model sells mostly at full price with ~70% automated replenishment. The rerating mechanism is credible and near-term: the next quarterly report within the 90-day window can demonstrate the SSS inflection is real (not just the 53rd week), which at this depressed multiple would drive outsized percentage moves in a $3.3M/day-liquidity microcap. Cheapness alone is not the case — the case is cheap-plus-stabilizing-fundamentals-plus-a-dated catalyst. Downside is tolerable but real: $226M debt vs $8M cash, rising lease obligations ($41.3M and growing), 22 lease expirations in FY2018, goodwill/intangibles of $258M subject to impairment, energy-state demand exposure, and a sponsor (Freeman Spogli, ~51%) whose registration rights and change-of-control default trigger cap takeover-premium scenarios. Position sizing must respect the leveraged microcap structure; this is a moderate-conviction candidate, not a conviction long.
trades.catalyst: Q1 fiscal 2018 earnings report (expected late July / early August 2017): if quarterly same-store sales confirm the FY2017 inflection (+0.3%) and new-store productivity holds, the market's distressed-retailer framing breaks and the ~6.5x EV/EBITDA multiple can re-rate toward specialty-retail norms; secondary support from continued self-funded unit growth (12 planned FY2018 openings at ~$0.8M cash each).
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the next quarterly print shows same-store sales rolling back negative or management cutting FY2018 guidance — confirming the FY2017 SSS uptick was 53rd-week noise rather than a real inflection. Additional invalidators: revolver/term-loan covenant pressure surfacing, a goodwill impairment charge against the $193.1M balance, or a sponsor secondary registration filing that signals insider distribution into weakness.

trades.thesis: GoPro enters the fall 2017 window at a deeply depressed valuation (~$8.26, -52% from 1y high) with an emerging operating inflection: Q2 revenue +34% YoY, opex down 35% YoY, and first positive adjusted EBITDA ($5.1M) from aggressive restructuring. The credible near-term rerating mechanism is the scheduled fall flagship/new-category product refresh into the holiday quarter — historically GoPro's demand concentration — which, combined with the reset cost base, offers asymmetric upside if sell-thru responds. Skeptical counterweights are real: sell-thru fell ~9% YoY while shipments rose 40% (channel fill, not end demand), gross margin compressed 650bps, H1 operating cash burn of $149.4M nearly equals the $149.8M cash balance, and credit facility availability halved to ~$89M. However, the April $175M 3.50% converts due 2022 plus revolver provide a liquidity bridge through the next 90 days, so the realistic downside is further drift/dilution rather than a solvency event inside the horizon. Position sizing must respect the ~20% tail of a failed product cycle compounding channel-inventory write-downs against thin liquidity.
trades.catalyst: Fall 2017 flagship camera refresh and new-form-factor launches ahead of the holiday quarter, paired with demonstrated cost discipline (opex -35% YoY, first positive adjusted EBITDA) that lets incremental high-end unit volume drop through to profitability; any Q3 print showing sell-thru re-acceleration and margin recovery would drive a sharp rerating off the -52% drawdown base.
trades.invalidation: Post-launch data showing sell-thru still negative YoY or flat units at lower price points (launch failing to stimulate end demand), gross margin remaining below ~38% into Q3 reporting, continued double-digit quarterly operating cash burn without seasonal working-capital recovery, or further credit-facility availability erosion below ~$60M signaling the borrowing base cannot support holiday inventory build.

trades.thesis: DexCom enters Nov 2017 down ~47% from its 1-year high despite objectively improving fundamentals: Q3 2017 revenue +24% YoY to $184.6M, gross margin expanding to ~68.8%, operating loss nearly eliminated ($(0.5)M vs $(18.5)M), and positive nine-month operating cash flow of $50.8M. The disconnect between a de-rated valuation and an approaching GAAP-operating-breakeven inflection provides a credible rerating mechanism over 90 days, reinforced by a fortified balance sheet ($525.8M cash/securities, $574.7M working capital, $200M undrawn revolver, $400M 0.75% converts due 2022) that removes financing distress risk. Downside is cushioned by liquidity and secular CGM adoption; the -47% drawdown means much pessimism is already priced. Key discounts: earnings quality is soft (SBC of $81.3M for nine months exceeds net loss; net loss flattered by a $16.4M tax benefit largely non-cash), interest expense now drags ~$4.5M/quarter, opex is growing in line with revenue limiting demonstrated leverage, and no dated regulatory/product catalysts appear in the filings — so this is a fundamentals-driven rerating bet, not a binary-catalyst one.
trades.catalyst: Q4 2017 earnings print confirming sustained ~20%+ growth and first GAAP operating profit quarter; next-gen sensor launch/coverage expansion into early 2018 providing a dated rerating event for a stock still ~47% below its 1-year high.
trades.invalidation: A Q4 print showing sequential revenue deceleration below ~18% YoY, renewed operating-loss widening, or disclosure of channel-inventory/rebate accrual problems would invalidate the operating-leverage thesis; technically, loss of the post-earnings low on heavy volume would signal the rerating has failed.

trades.thesis: CEC is a post-wind-down margin-inflection story trading near multi-year lows (-41% from 1y high) at ~$8.52. The Q3 2017 10-Q shows the structural reset is largely complete: all 17 campus teach-outs finished in Q3, driving a swing to positive quarterly operating income (+$4.5M vs -$0.7M) despite a -13.5% revenue decline, because cost cuts (ed services/facilities -26% YoY, G&A -11%) are outpacing the shrinking base. Forward math is compelling: management guides University Group/Corporate adjusted operating income to $100-105M for FY2017 (vs $89.3M) while teach-out losses fall from $40-45M in 2017 to only $10-15M in 2018 — an incremental ~$30M consolidated profit tailwind into 2018. Against a ~$589M market cap, the company holds $175.9M in cash/investments with zero borrowings (EV ~$413M, ~4x guided adjusted operating income), equity of $339M, and guides to ending 2017 at $160-165M cash with positive cash generation beginning in 2018. Demand is stabilizing where it matters: CTU new enrollments +10.9% and AIU total enrollments +5.7% YoY. This satisfies both prongs — a credible rerating mechanism (loss roll-off + enrollment stabilization visible in the next two prints) and tolerable downside (debt-free balance sheet, ~30% of market cap in cash). The bear case is real but mostly backward-looking: the -$29.1M YTD operating cash outflow is substantially explained by one-time $32M legal settlement payments and lease-exit costs rather than core burn, though the $88M working-capital drag and $21.5M bad-debt expense warrant monitoring.
trades.catalyst: Q4 2017 earnings (early 2018) demonstrating sustained GAAP profitability post-teach-out completion plus reaffirmation of the $160-165M year-end cash guide and a credible path to positive 2018 operating cash flow; secondary: continued double-digit new-enrollment growth at CTU/AIU validating demand stabilization.
trades.invalidation: Any ED action placing schools on reimbursement/HCM2 status; Q4 print showing renewed operating losses or failure to hit the $160-165M cash guide; reversal of CTU/AIU enrollment growth; disclosure of a deferred tax asset valuation allowance or goodwill impairment against the $148M DTA / $87.4M goodwill.

trades.thesis: Clinical-stage biopharma trading at $48.25, down ~46% from its 1-year high, with two dated, independent regulatory catalysts landing inside the 90-day window: vestronidase alfa BLA PDUFA on 2017-11-16 (~13 days out) and a CHMP opinion on burosumab pediatric XLH expected around end of 2017. The drawdown appears to have priced meaningful pipeline skepticism (UX007 Glut1 DS seizure miss earlier in 2017, widening losses), so even one approval is a credible rerating trigger while much of the failure case looks discounted. Financially the story is not fragile: $396.0M in cash/equivalents/investments, no debt, and a stated ≥12-month runway give a substantial asset floor (~$9+/share of liquidity against a $48 price), cushioning downside if a catalyst disappoints. The bear side is real and must be respected: operating cash burn accelerated 52% YoY to $172M for nine months, the ~$151M all-cash Dimension acquisition consumes roughly 38% of liquidity, and an active $150M ATM implies continued dilution that will cap and tax any rally. Net: a credible near-term rerating mechanism (two binaries) plus tolerable, cash-floored downside satisfies the long-candidate bar, but position conviction is tempered by dilution mechanics and binary-event variance.
trades.catalyst: Vestronidase alfa BLA PDUFA decision on 2017-11-16 (13 days post-cutoff); CHMP opinion on burosumab pediatric XLH expected around end of December 2017 — both inside the 90-day window, with the burosumab adult/pediatric BLA PDUFA (April 17, 2018) as follow-on momentum just beyond it.
trades.invalidation: A complete response letter or negative CHMP outcome on either lead asset, an abrupt acceleration in ATM issuance into strength, or disclosure that the Dimension close plus burn forces a large discounted equity raise within the window would invalidate the thesis; sustained trading below the pre-cutoff low on heavy volume would signal the market is pricing additional undisclosed pipeline risk.

trades.thesis: Oriental (PR-focused bank holding company) trades at ~0.43x book ($402M market cap / $937.6M equity, $6.58 vs $9.15 at quarter-end) after a hurricane-driven drawdown (-43% from 1y high).
