The damage is identifiable and largely one-time: a $27.0M incremental pre-tax hurricane provision pushed Q3 to a de minimis $(146)K loss to common, while the core franchise remained intact — Q3 NII grew 4.6% YoY on lower funding costs, opex fell 8%, and digital/core banking systems functioned uninterrupted through the storms. Balance-sheet resilience is unusually strong for a disaster-hit bank: cash up to $720.7M, total borrowings halved to $419.3M, deposits +$181M YTD, CET1 ~19.1% ('well capitalized'), and equity actually grew YTD despite the hit. The allowance was built aggressively ($154.2M vs $115.9M) using elevated PD/LGD assumptions management itself flags as conservative and subject to refinement — setting up potential reserve releases once actual post-Maria performance proves better than feared. With most of Puerto Rico still without power at filing, sentiment is at maximum pessimism; the credible rerating mechanism over 90 days is physical/economic normalization (power restoration, federal aid flows, reconstruction lending) plus a Q4 print demonstrating contained credit losses against a deeply discounted valuation. Cheapness alone would not qualify, but here cheapness coincides with demonstrated solvency, liquidity, and an intact earnings engine.
trades.catalyst: Progressive restoration of Puerto Rico's power grid and federal disaster relief/liquidity inflows through Dec 2017–Feb 2018, followed by Q4 2017 earnings (early Feb 2018) demonstrating that the $27M hurricane provision was conservative — enabling stabilization commentary or partial reserve release and a rerating off a ~0.43x tangible-book multiple.
trades.invalidation: Q4 2017 results (due ~Feb 2018) revealing materially higher charge-offs or NPL migration than reserved, disclosure of large unquantified forborne/TDR exposure, further ratings/funding pressure on brokered deposits, or evidence of accelerating post-hurricane deposit outflow and island population loss eroding the loan book faster than expected.

trades.thesis: OSIS is a post-short-report drawdown (-42% from 1y high, ~$55) where the headline GAAP net loss is largely a one-time, mostly non-cash $56M Tax Act charge, while underlying operations are demonstrably strong: Q2 revenue +14% YoY (services +27%), operating income doubled to $18.1M, six-month OCF of $84.7M vs $18.3M prior year, advances from customers up 70% signaling backlog, and the January 2018 two-year SAT Mexico renewal directly neutralizing the short thesis's Mexico revenue risk. The rerating mechanism is credible and near-term: the next 10-Q/earnings (~May 2018) should show the tax charge was non-recurring and that operations are unaffected, at a price already discounting severe distress. However, this is not a clean setup: a disclosed material weakness in ICFR over business combinations, three securities class actions, an SEC FCPA investigation, DOJ interest, an insider-trading probe with action already taken against a senior employee, a $13.5M CEO retention bonus signed amid investigations, and a revolver doubled to $195M all cap conviction. Position as a modest, catalyst-anchored long with the May earnings print as the confirmation event.
trades.catalyst: Q3 FY2018 earnings (~May 2018) demonstrating the Tax Act charge was one-time and non-cash, with continued revenue/OCF momentum and no operational impact from the short-seller allegations; SAT Mexico contract revenue recognition begins under the January 2018 renewal.
trades.invalidation: Q3 FY2018 results showing decelerating revenue/margins, further control failures or restatement signals, material FCPA-related revenue loss (e.g., Mexico contract disruption), or disclosure that the insider-trading probe implicates current leadership in a way that threatens operations.

trades.thesis: Pre-commercial biosimilars developer trading at ~$9.20 after a -64% drawdown, with ~$550M market cap against $126.9M cash/investments. The bull mechanism is genuine: CHS-1701 (pegfilgrastim) carries a large addressable market and management guides to US/EU regulatory action 'as early as 2018' following the June 2017 CRL, with secondary 2018 optionality in anti-TNF partnering (CHS-0214/CHS-1420, both Phase 3-positive) and CHS-3351 clinic start. However, the rerating path is not reliably inside a 90-day window: the BLA must first be successfully resubmitted, and a full review cycle plausibly pushes action beyond early June 2018. Meanwhile the accounting/liquidity profile is hostile — FY2017 revenue of $1.6M, $238.3M net loss, ~$200M operating burn against $126.9M cash, explicit disclosure that substantial additional funding is needed, only $32M ATM capacity remaining (already being tapped at $9.38/share in Jan 2018), and $100M 8.2% converts due 2022 — implying dilution pressure within the horizon. Add an active Amgen trade-secret suit with preliminary-injunction risk and trial set for Jan 2019. Cheapness here reflects real financing and regulatory-timing risk rather than mispricing; the setup warrants monitoring for resubmission confirmation and financing terms rather than immediate commitment.
trades.catalyst: FDA acceptance/action on the CHS-1701 BLA resubmission (or an unexpectedly early regulatory action / EU update) plus potential anti-TNF partnering announcements in 2018; either would provide a dated rerating trigger against a deeply discounted valuation.
trades.invalidation: Thesis weakens if the BLA resubmission is delayed or draws another CRL, if an equity raise is executed well below recent prices before any regulatory progress, or if Amgen obtains a preliminary injunction; absence of resubmission-acceptance news within ~60 days argues for staying on the sidelines.

trades.thesis: Universal Display enters the window deeply de-rated (-55% from 1-year high, ~$86 close vs ~$9.7/share net cash). The headline Q1 deterioration (revenue -21.6% YoY, operating income $4.5M vs $12.1M) is substantially an ASC 606 artifact: adoption cut Q1 revenue by $24.7M versus the prior standard, while cash collections tell the opposite story — operating cash flow of $38.8M (vs $1.6M LY) driven by a $30.3M deferred revenue build and $29.6M AR collection. Critically, the new Samsung Display license effective Jan 1, 2018 (through 2022 + extension option) carries a minimum phosphorescent emitter purchase commitment, giving contracted revenue visibility that the market appears not to be crediting at a 55%-off price. The rerating mechanism is credible: quarterly license-fee installments plus minimum material shipments should progressively convert the deferred revenue balance into recognized revenue over the next 2-3 quarters, forcing upward revisions to consensus models anchored on the depressed Q1 print. Downside is tolerable: debt-free balance sheet with $457M cash/ST investments (~11% of market cap), doubled dividend, and a royalty/moat business model (4,500+ patents) where even a weak handset cycle preserves high-margin licensing income. Cheapness alone wouldn't suffice, but here cheapness coincides with a dated, contract-backed catalyst.
trades.catalyst: Quarterly cadence of Samsung license-fee installments plus minimum emitter-material shipments converting the $59.7M current deferred revenue into recognized revenue over subsequent quarters; next 10-Q (Aug 2018) showing sequential revenue re-acceleration and inventory conversion would validate the billing-led recovery narrative.
trades.invalidation: Next quarterly filing showing declining deferred revenue/billings, failure to convert inventory to shipments, or disclosure that SDC minimum purchase volumes are being renegotiated or under-consumed would indicate the billing surge was one-time license timing rather than durable demand, removing the rerating thesis.

trades.thesis: Alnylam trades ~40% below its 1-year high ($88.31 vs prior peak) despite a well-capitalized balance sheet ($1.57B cash/securities, only $30M debt) and a credible, dated near-term rerating mechanism: patisiran's first-ever NDA/MAA submission (Dec 2017) with management explicitly contemplating 2018 approval and launch, placing a regulatory decision plausibly inside the 90-day window. The headline Q1'18 loss widening ($141.2M vs $107.3M) is partly an ASC 606 artifact ($33.1M revenue reduction under the new standard; underlying loss closer to $108M), so reported deterioration overstates operational decline. The $50M Sanofi Genzyme milestone and settled Dicerna litigation remove secondary overhangs. Skeptical discount applied: this is still a pre-revenue company burning ~$156M/quarter with rising opex, prior program failures (revusiran discontinuation, fitusiran suspension) that justify the drawdown, and acknowledged financing-dependence risk — so position sizing assumes a wide distribution around a binary event rather than high conviction. Cheapness alone is not the driver; the driver is the asymmetric payoff into a plausible approval catalyst against a balance sheet that removes near-term solvency/dilution tail risk.
trades.catalyst: Patisiran regulatory decision expected within the 90-day window (NDA submitted Dec 2017 per filing; management explicitly contemplates 2018 approval and launch), with first product revenue possible in 2018; secondary support from the achieved $50M Sanofi Genzyme milestone and resolved Dicerna litigation removing an overhang.
trades.invalidation: Any negative regulatory development on patisiran (complete response letter, extended review beyond the window, or clinical-hold news on remaining pipeline such as givosiran/fitusiran safety) invalidates the thesis; also invalidated if burn accelerates materially above the Q1'18 pace forcing near-term equity issuance.

trades.thesis: Ultra Clean Holdings trades near $17.33, ~50% below its 1-year high, despite a Q1 FY2018 print showing +54% YoY sales growth ($314.8M), net income of $24.7M (EPS $0.66 vs $0.42), and demonstrated operating leverage (opex +24% vs sales +54%). The disconnect between deteriorating price and improving fundamentals suggests cyclical/macro de-rating of the semi-cap supply chain rather than company-specific failure. The February 2018 $94.3M equity raise lifted cash to $162.4M against $54.8M bank debt, eliminating near-term solvency risk, and disclosure controls are clean with no material litigation. A credible rerating mechanism exists: if the next quarter confirms demand strength and normalizes working capital, the market should re-rate a profitable, well-capitalized grower off a depressed base. However, this is not a table-pounding setup: gross margin compressed (~15.5% vs ~18.3%), operating cash flow halved on a $24.7M inventory build with finished goods doubling, and the business is concentrated among US semi-cap OEMs whose capex outlook drove the sector selloff. Cheapness plus momentum is necessary but the confirmation catalyst is required; sizing should reflect genuine cyclicality risk.
trades.catalyst: Next quarterly report (Q2 FY2018, due early August 2018) demonstrating sustained revenue growth, gross-margin stabilization, and working-capital normalization; broader recovery in semiconductor capital equipment spending sentiment after the spring 2018 de-rating of semi-cap supply-chain names.
trades.invalidation: Evidence that the inventory build reflects softening end-demand rather than build-ahead (order/backlog deterioration at semi-cap customers), further gross-margin compression below ~15%, a guidance cut or working-capital blowout at the next print, or renewed sector-wide de-rating on trade-war/memory-capex headlines.

trades.thesis: Geron (GERN, $3.30, -45% from 1y high) is a binary-event special situation with a hard-dated catalyst inside the forecast window: Janssen's Continuation Decision on imetelstat, expected by end of Q3 2018 per the 10-Q, following the IMbark Phase 2 overall-survival primary analysis (clinical cut-off April 26, 2018). An affirmative decision triggers a $65M Continuation Fee (plus $70M Full U.S. Rights Fee if Geron declines opt-in) and commits Janssen to fund further development — a credible rerating mechanism for a stock that has de-rated heavily on mixed interim data. Downside is partially floored by a debt-free balance sheet: $181.4M cash+securities (~30% of the ~$606M market cap) against only ~$24M annualized operating burn, giving multi-year runway even in the bear case. However, this is not a cheapness story — revenue is negligible (~$208K/quarter), losses are widening, accumulated deficit is ~$999M, and prior IMbark signals were weak (enrollment suspended since Oct 2016 on insufficient spleen response vs. JAK inhibitors), so the decision is genuinely close to a coin flip with fat tails both ways. Ongoing ATM dilution (~$38M raised May–July, ~$60.5M capacity left, plus a new $250M shelf) adds supply overhang that caps upside. Net: the setup offers positive asymmetry (upside plausibly +50–100% on affirmation vs. perhaps -30–40% on termination, cushioned by cash), justifying a small long candidacy rather than a pass, but position sizing must respect the binary risk.
trades.catalyst: Janssen Continuation Decision on imetelstat expected by end of Q3 2018 (per 10-Q Note 3); an affirmative decision triggers a $65M Continuation Fee plus potential $70M Full U.S. Rights Fee and commits Janssen to fund further development, while a negative decision likely ends third-party funding of the lead asset.
trades.invalidation: A negative Janssen Continuation Decision (program termination or rights reversion without committed funding) invalidates the thesis immediately; secondary invalidation is continued heavy ATM selling into strength or disclosure of adverse IMbark/IMerge safety or survival data before the decision.

trades.thesis: Amarin enters September 2018 as a near-pure binary event position: REDUCE-IT cardiovascular outcomes results are guided to be public before end of Q3 2018, well inside the 90-day window. The setup has several features that skew the payoff favorably relative to a generic binary bet. First, the company is acting like it expects success: SG&A up 71% YoY to fund expanded promotion, inventory built to $40.1M, and 3.5M performance RSUs that vest only upon REDUCE-IT results plus regulatory/sales milestones — insider behavior consistent with internal confidence, though not proof. Second, the IP overhang was just de-risked by the May 2018 Teva settlement pushing generic entry to August 2029, so a positive readout converts directly into durable franchise value rather than being contested by ANDA entrants. Third, revenue momentum (+17% YoY to $52.5M at ~75% gross margin) provides a floor of fundamental support. Fourth, liquidity is adequate through the readout ($102.3M cash after a $70M raise at $3.41/ADS), meaning the event occurs before forced financing. Against this: the stock already sits ~43% below its 1-year high, suggesting partial skepticism is priced; a failed or ambiguous trial would likely cut the equity 50%+ and force dilutive capital raises against $99.4M CPPIB royalty obligations and widening burn ($(34.2)M H1 operating cash outflow); and an ~11% preferred conversion overhang caps upside. On balance, the asymmetry — large upside on success versus a defined but survivable downside within the window — justifies a long-candidate stance, sized with explicit recognition that this is event risk, not a quality compounder.
trades.catalyst: REDUCE-IT cardiovascular outcomes results expected before end of Q3 2018 (within ~60 days of cutoff), followed by broader reporting at a scientific conference in Q4 2018 — a dated, hard catalyst disclosed in the 10-Q itself.
trades.invalidation: A slip of the REDUCE-IT data release beyond Q3 2018, disclosure of an equity raise or debt financing ahead of the readout, or any signal of negative/mixed trial results (e.g., delayed conference presentation, data monitoring issues) would invalidate the thesis; also a failure to renew the Kowa co-promotion would weaken the post-readout commercial case.

trades.thesis: UNM trades at $25.51, down ~41% from its 1-year high, after a Q3 2018 GAAP net loss of $(284.7)M driven almost entirely by a one-time $750.8M long-term care reserve increase. Core operations are intact and modestly improving: adjusted operating income grew to $366.3M (Q3) and $1,067.0M (nine months), premiums rose +4.6% YoY, and operating cash flow jumped to $1,083.5M (+24%). The bear case is concentrated in (a) risk of further LTC reserve actions while the review remains open, evidenced by the paused buyback despite $650M remaining authorization, and (b) AOCI/equity deterioration (~-$1.06B) from rising rates plus $496.6M gross unrealized losses including 91 below-IG positions. But the loss is largely a non-cash accrual event; RBC ratios remain above regulatory-action thresholds, holding-company liquidity is adequate ($973M cash, $1.24B short-term investments), the dividend was raised, and management guided toward Q4 buyback resumption. At roughly 3.5-4x annualized adjusted operating earnings, the market has priced substantial further deterioration. A credible near-term rerating mechanism exists: closure of the LTC review with no additional charge plus resumed repurchases into year-end reporting. Cheapness alone would not qualify, but here cheapness coincides with intact cash earnings, growing premiums, and a defined catalyst path.
trades.catalyst: Resolution/conclusion of the LTC reserve review with management commentary that the charge is sufficient, followed by resumption of the ~$650M remaining buyback in Q4 2018 as stated in MD&A; secondary support from continued premium growth (+4.6%) and rate-driven net investment income gains into year-end reporting.
trades.invalidation: Disclosure that the LTC reserve review concluded with additional charges beyond the $750.8M taken, or evidence of adverse morbidity/claim-incidence trend requiring follow-on strengthening; failure to resume buybacks in Q4 2018; credit rating downgrade pressure on the holding company.

trades.thesis: Vicor shows a credible, largely organic fundamental inflection: Q3-18 revenue +37% YoY to $78.0M, gross margin up to 50.0% from 44.2%, operating income swinging to $13.0M from ~breakeven, nine-month OCF of $22.8M vs $0.6M prior year, and $68.2M cash with no debt against a depressed ~$150M market cap after a -40% drawdown from the 1-year high. Eleven straight quarters of sequential booking increases (+41.6% YoY) and accelerating 48V/Power-on-Package datacenter demand give a real rerating mechanism rather than mere cheapness. Haircuts: ~$1.0M of Q3 revenue and ~$444K net income are Topic 606 timing effects, legacy distributor bookings softened sequentially, profitability is highly sensitive to factory utilization, and the SynQor litigation exposure is unestimable. The stock's -40% drawdown reflects the October 2018 semi/market selloff more than company-specific deterioration, so mean reversion plus a strong Q4 print (early Feb 2019, inside the window) could drive excess return — but macro-driven multiple compression can persist for the full 90 days, so position as a candidate, not a conviction hold.
trades.catalyst: Q4-2018 earnings report (due early February 2019, inside the 90-day window) providing a fourth consecutive data point on the bookings/revenue/margin inflection; secondary catalyst is beta recovery of beaten-down semis off oversold levels once macro selling abates.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if Q4 bookings break the eleven-quarter sequential streak or legacy distributor bookings decline materially further, if gross margin retreats below ~46% on utilization shortfalls, or if the broad semi/market drawdown deepens and holds the stock below its pre-cutoff low despite intact fundamentals.

trades.thesis: Huntsman-class specialty chemicals issuer trades ~40% below its 1-year high ($15.60) despite clearly improving core economics: Q3 revenue +12.7% YoY, nine-month operating income +46% ($862M vs $590M), SG&A leverage, and $454M of nine-month continuing-ops free cash flow against only $180M capex. The headline Q3 net loss is entirely attributable to a one-time $270M after-tax valuation allowance on the held-for-sale Venator stake — an accounting charge that both depressed sentiment and sets up a credible rerating mechanism: management states the ~53% retained stake is actively marketed for sale, with proceeds earmarked for revolver repayment, acquisitions, and buybacks under a fresh $950M authorization plus a raised dividend ($0.125→$0.1625). A successful monetization removes the conglomerate discount overhang and funds accretive repurchases at a depressed multiple. Liquidity is adequate ($1,529M combined cash + unused capacity vs $2.5B debt), though rising current debt ($200M vs $40M) and +$265M net revolver draws warrant monitoring. Cheapness alone would be insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with operating momentum, self-funded shareholder returns, and a discrete, disclosed divestiture catalyst inside the forecast window. Risks: cyclical chemical/macro beta in a volatile tape, uncertain Venator sale price (the write-down itself signals value below prior marks), and unquantified environmental contingencies.
trades.catalyst: Monetization of the retained ~53% Venator stake (actively marketed per MD&A), with proceeds earmarked for revolver paydown and buybacks; secondary support from continued Q4 earnings momentum and accelerated repurchases under the $950M authorization into a deeply discounted share price.
trades.invalidation: A failed or further-written-down Venator disposal (additional valuation allowance beyond the $270M taken in Q3), renewed revolver reliance without monetization proceeds, or evidence of peaking polyurethanes margins (MD&A volume/price breakdown unavailable in excerpts) would invalidate the rerating thesis.

trades.thesis: AMD enters November 2018 down ~47% from its 1-year high at $17.20 despite a genuine fundamental inflection: nine-month revenue +29% ($5,056M vs $3,913M), operating income up >3x ($423M vs $129M), and gross margin expansion driven by new higher-margin product ramps (Zen/EPYC). The drawdown has de-rated the equity to a point where continued execution offers asymmetric upside versus a fundamentally improving business. However, this is not a clean story: ASC 606 adoption accelerated recognition (distributor sell-in, semi-custom over-time, one-time $86M IP milestone), nine-month operating cash flow remains negative ($(36)M) on a $753M AR build, the $805M 2.125% converts are deeply in-the-money and will settle in shares (material dilution), and GlobalFoundries' indefinite 7nm halt forces a TSMC transition with WSA shortfall-payment exposure through 2020. Net: a credible rerating mechanism exists (datacenter share gains, 7nm roadmap intact via TSMC, litigation overhang cleared), and the post-crash entry provides tolerable downside, but earnings-quality noise, dilution mechanics, and a high-beta profile in a volatile tape argue for a modest-sized long rather than conviction sizing.
trades.catalyst: Q3 print delivered Oct 31 with 9M operating income up ~3x YoY; next 90 days bring 7nm TSMC-based roadmap milestones (Rome CPU sampling toward 2019 launch), progress on renegotiating/replacing the GF wafer supply agreement, and potential stabilization of the gaming GPU channel that would validate sell-through beneath ASC 606 sell-in accounting.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 guidance or channel checks reveal distributor/gaming inventory digestion behind the ASC 606 sell-in acceleration (i.e., revenue air-pocket), if the GF WSA renegotiation produces material cash shortfall payments without offsetting TSMC capacity commitments, or if the deep-ITM convert settlement plus any equity raise dilutes well beyond ~10% while the stock fails to hold the post-drawdown base.

trades.thesis: SolarEdge (SEDG, ~$41, -40% from 1y high) shows genuinely strong fundamentals into the cutoff: Q3 revenue +42% YoY, nine-month operating income doubled to $115.5M, ~$112M implied nine-month FCF, zero debt, and ~$453M in liquid resources. The post-period close of ~75% of Kokam (Oct 17, 2018) adds a concrete energy-storage growth leg that could support a rerating narrative over the next quarter's reporting cycle. However, the setup is not a slam-dunk long: the stock has already absorbed the strong Q3 print (filed Nov 2), Q3 net income was flattered by a $(12.3)M tax benefit exceeding pre-tax income, working capital is absorbing cash (receivables +$42.4M, inventories +$18.1M), warranty accruals jumped, and supplier/customer concentration is elevated. With a -40% drawdown reflecting both company-specific de-rating and a deteriorating high-beta tape, expected excess return is positive but modest — the rerating mechanism (accelerating growth + storage optionality + fortress balance sheet) is credible, and downside is cushioned by net cash and self-funding, but macro beta and earnings-quality caveats argue against conviction sizing.
trades.catalyst: Kokam consolidation begins appearing in reported results (Q4 print due ~Feb 2019), providing a concrete near-term datapoint that could validate the energy-storage growth narrative and drive rerating of a stock still ~40% below its 1-year high despite accelerating fundamentals.
trades.invalidation: Rerating thesis fails if Q4 guidance/reported results show decelerating core solar revenue or gross-margin erosion beyond opex leverage, if Kokam integration produces charges/minority-interest complexity without disclosed revenue contribution, or if receivables/inventory build accelerates faster than revenue — signaling channel stuffing rather than demand.

trades.thesis: Clinical-stage oncology name trading at $10.96 after a -53% drawdown from its 1-year high, with ~$187.4M in cash and short-term investments against roughly a $420M market cap (~45% cash backing) and only ~$6M of debt recently refinanced into a small SVB facility. At current burn ($38.4M operating cash use over 9M 2018, accelerating but implying ~2 years of runway), there is no forced dilution event inside the 90-day window, which makes the downside more tolerable than typical pre-revenue biotech setups. The rerating mechanism is credible and dated: KO-539 IND targeted Q1 2019 (inside the window), KO-947 Phase 1 dose-escalation data expected in 2019, and ongoing AIM-HN enrollment with potential interim/conference disclosures. The stock has already absorbed the July follow-on at $16.75 and ATM dilution, and the -53% drawdown suggests pessimistic positioning. This is a cash-cushioned, catalyst-dated speculative long, not a quality compounder: sizing must reflect binary clinical risk and demonstrated management willingness to dilute.
trades.catalyst: KO-539 IND submission targeted Q1 2019 (within the 90-day window) plus expected 2019 KO-947 Phase 1 dose-escalation data; any interim AIM-HN enrollment/response disclosure or conference presentation could rerate the story off a deeply depressed base.
trades.invalidation: Thesis weakens if the company announces an equity offering within the window (management has shown willingness to raise aggressively), if KO-539 IND timing slips past Q1 2019, or if negative KO-947 safety/dose-escalation news emerges; a sustained broad-market breakdown in small-cap biotech would also negate the setup.

trades.thesis: Fluent enters the window off a genuinely quote-grounded operating inflection: Q3 2018 revenue +21% YoY to $66.5M, a swing to $6.3M income from operations (vs -$8.3M), G&A down ~29% YoY post red violet spin-off, and nine-month continuing-ops operating cash flow of $22.5M vs $5.0M. The March 2018 spin-off simplified the story to one segment, extinguished insider promissory notes, and refinanced LIBOR+10.5% debt down to LIBOR+7.00%. With the stock -54% from its 1-year high at $15.06 (~$1.13B market cap on ~75.3M shares), the market has not yet paid for the profitability turn, so continued execution into Q4 offers a plausible rerating path. However, this is a qualified candidate, not a conviction long: the quality bar is low. There is an unremediated material weakness in internal controls (non-cash stock comp), an interim CFO, ~24% nine-month share count expansion plus new warrants (including a lender Put Right at $3.83 exercisable through 2019), $20.2M of unbilled revenue based on internally tracked conversions, AR growth with only a ~4.4% allowance, and a $64.9M term loan against $17.4M cash. Annualized adjusted EBITDA (~$44M) implies the equity is not statistically cheap — the case rests on momentum of the inflection, not deep value. Thin liquidity (~$1.5M/day) amplifies both directions, and the broader small-cap tape in late 2018 is a headwind for beta. Net: modestly positive expected excess with wide dispersion; position sizing must respect the control/governance overhang.
trades.catalyst: The just-filed Q3 2018 10-Q (first clean quarter post-spin) showing GAAP operating income and cash flow inflection; follow-through requires Q4 results confirming run-rate profitability and remediation progress on the material weakness. Secondary: any paydown of the $64.9M term loan from the ~$30M annualized operating cash flow, which would reduce the LIBOR+7% burden and signal deleveraging capacity.
trades.invalidation: Q4 2018 results showing decelerating revenue or reversal of the margin gains (G&A cuts were one-time spin-off driven); failure to begin remediating the internal-control weakness or departure of the interim CFO without a permanent hire; renewed AR/unbilled-revenue buildup outpacing revenue; further equity issuance or warrant-driven dilution; sustained breach below the pre-print base (~$13–14) would indicate the market is rejecting the inflection thesis.

trades.thesis: Herc Holdings presents a credible earnings-inflection story trading at a deep discount (-52% from 1-year high, ~$31.47). Q3 2018 shows genuine operating momentum: total revenue +12.8% YoY, equipment rental revenue +8.7%, SG&A down YoY despite growth (real operating leverage), pretax income more than doubled to $45.2M, and a nine-month swing from -$85.5M loss to +$30.5M profit. Operating cash flow improved sharply ($375.0M vs $253.6M) and equity is building. This is a cyclical upcycle with demonstrated cost discipline, not just a low-multiple value trap. However, the setup carries real constraints: $2.23B secured debt plus $110.9M financing obligations against only $554.3M equity, minimal cash ($18.0M) with negative FCF after fleet capex and full reliance on revolver/securitization draws, disclosure controls still NOT effective due to unremediated material weaknesses, and legacy securities litigation/government investigations. Equity issuance capacity is limited by spin-off tax treatment. The rerating mechanism is credible — sustained earnings beats in an equipment-rental upcycle should compress the apparent distress discount — but the leveraged capital structure makes the equity high-beta to credit conditions, so this is a candidate sized for tolerable downside rather than a high-conviction position.
trades.catalyst: Continued quarterly execution: follow-on prints showing sustained rental revenue growth, SG&A leverage, and used-equipment gains could force multiple rerating from distressed-deep-value levels; secondary catalysts include further debt reduction/redemption activity and progress toward ICFR remediation milestones.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if rental revenue growth decelerates materially, used-equipment pricing weakens (fleet gains reverse), operating cash flow deteriorates, or a macro credit shock drives spreads wider on the secured debt stack; also invalidated by any restatement or new control failure stemming from unremediated material weaknesses.

trades.thesis: Ligand enters the window down ~41% from its 1-year high (~$101.67) largely due to the November 2018 biotech/market drawdown, not company-specific deterioration. The Q3 2018 10-Q shows the core royalty engine accelerating (Q3 royalties $36.1M vs $21.9M, +65% YoY; total revenue +37%; YTD operating income $130.6M vs $39.7M) driven by Promacta/Kyprolis momentum, with operating cash flow of $161.5M YTD (vs $57.3M). The near-term capital-structure overhang is actively resolving: most of the $245M 2019 converts ($195.9M) were settled in Q4 2018 under an irrevocable cash-settlement election, eliminating dilution from those notes, while the $750M 2023 issue leaves ~$1.2B liquidity and $951.9M working capital — refinancing/balance-sheet risk inside 90 days is minimal. A fully available $200M buyback (~9% of market cap) provides a credible support mechanism at depressed prices. Headline net income is low-quality (Viking mark-to-market gains, derivative swings), so the rerating case rests on royalty/operating-cash-flow trajectory rather than GAAP EPS. With the stock de-rated ~40% while core economics improved, the setup offers asymmetric upside into the Q4 print, tempered by high market beta in a volatile tape and mark-to-market noise.
trades.catalyst: Q4 2018 earnings report (~Feb 2019) demonstrating continued Promacta/Kyprolis-driven royalty growth and clean post-conversion capital structure; active use of the fully available $200M buyback into weakness providing price support; removal of the 2019 Notes overhang by August 2019 maturity.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 results show royalty deceleration or material sales weakness spreading beyond the single-quarter dip, if the company suspends/dilutes the buyback, or if continued broad-market deleveraging drives the stock below the pre-correction base (~$85-90) despite unchanged fundamentals — indicating the discount is structural rather than sentiment-driven.

trades.thesis: Collegium enters the window down ~47% from its 1-year high at $15.48, a discount that already prices substantial opioid-sector stigma. The fundamental picture is a genuine commercial inflection: Q3 2018 net product revenues of $70.2M vs $12.0M a year ago (nine months $207.0M vs $17.7M) from the first full year of Nucynta ER/IR alongside Xtampza ER, with operating losses narrowing and nine-month operating cash flow swinging to +$127.1M from -$53.7M. The most credible near-term rerating mechanism is dated and contractual: the November 2018 Third Amendment with Assertio eliminates the $135M guaranteed minimum annual royalties after January 1, 2019 (converting to sales-based tiers) and removes the standby letter-of-credit requirement, materially de-risking the cash flow profile right as Q4 results land in late February. Liquidity is adequate ($139.8M cash, modest $11.5M SVB term loan, covenant relaxed to 1.5x, ~$26M residual ATM capacity). That said, this is a candidate, not a high-conviction one: earnings quality is weak (GAAP gross margin near zero once $94.3M of non-cash Nucynta amortization in COGS is included; $130.5M accrued rebates/returns/discounts vs $15.8M at year-end flatters operating cash flow and signals large gross-to-net estimates that could reverse), $401.2M of asset-acquisition obligations ($116.3M current) absorb much of the cash generation, and unquantified Purdue/Teva patent litigation plus sector-wide opioid marketing/distribution exposure create fat left tails. On balance, the combination of a deeply discounted entry, self-funded operations, and a specific January 1, 2019 economic improvement ahead of a Q4 print gives a modestly positive asymmetry versus SPY, sized conservatively.
trades.catalyst: Assertio Third Amendment takes effect January 1, 2019 (eliminating $135M guaranteed minimum royalties and the letter-of-credit requirement), followed by the Q4/full-year 2018 report (~late February 2019) expected to confirm Nucynta run-rate revenue and the improved post-amendment cash conversion profile.
trades.invalidation: Q4 2018 results (or interim channel checks) showing Nucynta net revenue deceleration, a material increase in gross-to-net deductions or rebate-reserve true-ups, or escalation of opioid-related litigation naming the company would invalidate the thesis; sustained trade below the pre-cutoff low on volume would signal the drawdown reflects unresolved fundamental deterioration rather than sentiment.

trades.thesis: Extreme Networks enters February 2019 at $6.93, down ~54% from its 1-year high, trading as if the turnaround had failed while the fiscal Q2 FY19 10-Q shows the opposite: first positive quarterly operating income ($4.75M vs -$31.1M a year ago), revenue +9.3% YoY with service revenue +12%, deferred revenue building ($186M RPO), and a dramatic operating cash flow inflection ($61.6M for six months vs $14.2M prior year, driven by AR collection). The stock's de-rating appears driven by macro/small-cap beta and the December selloff rather than deteriorating fundamentals. A credible rerating mechanism exists: confirmation of sustained GAAP profitability at the fiscal Q3 report (due late April/early May, inside the 90-day window), removal of the long-running securities class action overhang via court-approved settlements (preliminary approval granted; final hearings April 25 and May 3, 2019), and management alignment via PSOs with a $10.00 price hurdle plus an active $60M buyback ($15M executed at $6.34/share — insiders buying below current price). Balance sheet risk is tolerable: $141M cash against $185M secured term debt, covenants met, only $9.5M due within a year, and H1 FCF (~$50M) comfortably covering obligations. Key discounts applied: Q2 net income was flattered by a $5.3M tax benefit (pre-tax income just $1.9M), six-month results are still a net loss, heavy distributor concentration (Tech Data 22%, Westcon 15% of revenue; Westcon 23% of AR) creates lumpy demand and receivable risk, and the stock's deep drawdown signals negative momentum that can persist. Cheapness alone is not the case — the case is an earnings/cash-flow inflection with identifiable near-term catalysts and de-risking legal events.
trades.catalyst: Fiscal Q3 FY19 earnings report (expected late April/early May 2019, inside the 90-day window) confirming a second consecutive quarter of GAAP operating income and continued cash generation; secondary: court final approvals of the securities class action (Apr 25 hearing) and derivative settlement (May 3 hearing) formally retiring legacy litigation overhangs.
trades.invalidation: Failure to sustain profitability at the fiscal Q3 FY19 print (return to operating losses or sharp sequential revenue decline), covenant pressure or reversal of the working-capital-driven cash flow benefit, or renewed selling tied to distributor concentration (Tech Data/Westcon) would invalidate the thesis; a decisive break below the pre-cutoff low also signals the rerating mechanism has failed.

trades.thesis: Skyline Champion (post-June 2018 reverse merger of Champion Holdings into Skyline) trades at $16.85, down ~52% from its 1-year high, yet the Dec-29-2018 10-Q shows an operationally improving business: Q3 net sales +20% YoY ($354.7M vs $294.4M), Q3 net income of $10.5M (vs $5.4M), nine-month operating cash flow of +$51.9M (vs -$0.7M), $129.0M cash against only $59.3M long-term debt with no short-term maturities and $32.1M undrawn revolver. The headline $(67.4)M nine-month loss is dominated by a one-time, non-cash $97.6M equity-based compensation charge tied to the Exchange — a known, dated item that mechanically distorts reported earnings rather than reflecting operating deterioration. The credible rerating mechanism is earnings normalization as the equity-comp charge laps and the market refocuses on pro forma profitability (pro forma nine-month loss only $(52.3)M, with Q3 solidly profitable) ahead of the FY2019 annual report due within the 90-day window. Cheapness alone would not qualify, but here it is paired with genuine top-line momentum (+20% growth) and a clean liquidity profile. Offsetting factors that cap conviction: Q3 operating income actually declined YoY ($15.9M vs $23.4M) on SG&A up 49% and gross margin compression (~18.2% vs ~19.1%) plus rising warranty expense — cost integration is not yet delivering; disclosure controls were concluded NOT effective due to an unremediated material weakness in raw-material inventory valuation, and ICFR assessment excluded Champion (~85% of revenue); $172.1M goodwill rests on a still-preliminary purchase price allocation that 'could differ materially'; governance is weak (NYSE transition exemptions, concentrated principal shareholders who took a $65.3M pre-close distribution). Net: a leveraged-to-housing-recovery, post-merger normalization story at a deeply discounted price, with real but manageable execution and accounting-quality risks.
trades.catalyst: FY2019 annual results (~May-June 2019) showing normalized profitability ex-equity-comp charges plus finalized purchase price allocation; potential resolution/remediation progress on the inventory material weakness; continued housing demand tailwind supporting order momentum for the combined Skyline-Champion platform.
trades.invalidation: Q4/FY2019 results showing continued gross-margin compression and SG&A growth outpacing revenue without offsetting synergy capture; any goodwill impairment discussion tied to the preliminary PPA; failure to remediate or further expansion of the ICFR material weakness; deterioration in factory-built housing order indicators.

trades.thesis: C&J Energy Services enters mid-Feb 2019 deeply discounted (-43% from 1y high, ~$11 vs $18 mid-2018) despite improving fundamentals: contract drilling backlog up 42% YoY to $770M, $731M operating cash flow, revolver fully repaid with $600M undrawn, cash of $245M, and shareholder-friendly actions (buyback authorization raised to $250M on Feb 7, dividend doubled to $0.04). As a high-beta oilfield services name, its dominant driver over a 90-day window is the oil-price/activity cycle rather than idiosyncratic fundamentals; crude had stabilized and recovered off the Q4-2018 lows, and OFS equities historically rerate sharply when activity expectations inflect. The bear case is real — persistent GAAP losses (-$367M pre-tax), a $211M goodwill impairment, Oklahoma fatality litigation with punitive damages sought, CHK contingent tax exposure, and $1.12B debt — but balance-sheet liquidity is adequate for the horizon and much of the distress appears priced in. This is a credible rerating mechanism (activity recovery + backlog conversion visible in Q1 earnings due within the window) paired with tolerable downside given liquidity, satisfying the long-candidate bar — though not with high conviction given unprofitability and cyclicality.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2019 earnings (late April/early May) showing backlog conversion into revenue and margin improvement as U.S. rig count and completion activity recover alongside firming crude prices; continued buyback execution under the enlarged $250M authorization.
trades.invalidation: Failure of backlog-to-revenue conversion in Q1 results (revenue/margin guidance cut), renewed oil price breakdown dragging rig counts lower, or disclosure of material litigation reserve or covenant stress tied to the $1.12B debt load.

trades.thesis: Small-cap, high-oil-beta E&P (Denver-based, Midland Basin/Eagle Ford focus) trading ~41% below its 1-year high at $17.50 after the Q4-2018 crude selloff. The filing shows genuine self-help rather than just statistical cheapness: operating cash flow +40% to $720.6M, long-term debt cut from $3.0B to $2.6B with maturities pushed to 2027 via new 6.625% notes, ~$999.8M undrawn revolver availability, Permian production +91% YoY (+11% retained-asset basis), reserves +18% retained-basis with RLI extended to 11.5 years, and 55 net Midland DUCs plus 12 third-party-funded Eagle Ford JV wells de-risking the 2019 program. The credible near-term rerating mechanism is leveraged torque to a recovering crude tape combined with demonstrated deleveraging and Permian volume momentum — small-cap E&Ps historically exhibit outsized beta off commodity-trough recoveries. Offsets that keep this a moderate-conviction idea, not a slam dunk: net downward reserve revisions of 68.8 MMBOE from Eagle Ford development plan changes (an estimate-quality/management-credibility flag), 2019 capex of $1.00–$1.07B exceeding CFO (negative FCF, continued reliance on JV funding/borrowing base), Midland takeaway-constraint risk to realizations, and a pending royalty-deduction class action. Net: favorable asymmetry with tolerable, well-identified downside channels.
trades.catalyst: Continued crude price recovery into the spring 2019 window combined with execution of the 2019 program: 55 net Midland DUCs turning in-line, 12 third-party-funded Eagle Ford JV wells completed, and Q1/Q2 prints demonstrating retained-asset production growth (+11% trend) against a shrinking debt load — supporting multiple repair from distressed-adjacent levels.
trades.invalidation: WTI reversing back toward the low-$50s or below; a spring borrowing-base redetermination cut; 2019 guidance misses or additional Eagle Ford reserve/PUD walk-backs; evidence of Midland differentials widening materially on takeaway constraints. Any of these would flip the setup to watch/reject.

trades.thesis: NVDA trades ~45% below its 1-year high after the cryptocurrency-mining bust, and the 10-K's negative signals (explicitly weaker FY2019 second-half revenue breaking seasonality, largely cancelable backlog, forecast-built semi-finished inventory, new securities class actions and a derivative suit over channel-inventory/crypto disclosures) are predominantly backward-looking and already public at the cutoff — consistent with much of the bad news being priced in. Against this, the franchise is structurally intact: >700k registered developers, fabless model, $7.42B cash and marketable securities (+4% YoY) versus modest $2B debt with the $1.5B convertible matured Dec 2018 (no conversion overhang), and an active $7B buyback authorization (Nov 2018). This is a washed-out quality compounder where the rerating mechanism is normalization of gaming/channel inventory plus continued datacenter growth, not cheapness alone. Position sizing must respect genuine near-term uncertainty: no dated catalysts are disclosed in the excerpts, visibility is poor (cancelable backlog), and litigation headlines can pressure the stock. Net: favorable asymmetry for a long candidate, but with wide error bars and meaningful tail risk if channel inventory proves worse than disclosed.
trades.catalyst: No single dated catalyst in the excerpts; the mechanism is washout-driven re-rating: crypto-bust drawdown (-45% from 1y high) fully discounting the disclosed H2 FY2019 revenue weakness, plus continued execution of the November 2018 $7B repurchase authorization against a net-cash balance sheet, and any stabilization signal in gaming channel inventory at upcoming earnings.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if forward guidance confirms accelerating demand deterioration (H2 weakness extending into FY2020 quarters), evidence of large unreported channel inventory build emerges, or litigation escalates into material operational remedies; a break below the December 2018 lows would signal the washout thesis is wrong.

trades.thesis: Arlo (ARLO) enters the window at $4.06, down ~82% from its 1-year high, following the August 2018 IPO at $16 and NETGEAR's full distribution of its ~84.2% stake on Dec 31, 2018 — mechanical supply overhang that has largely cleared. The bear case is concentrated in a headline $75.5M FY2018 GAAP loss, but roughly $27.3M of that is one-time separation expense; underlying revenue grew to $464.9M from $370.7M (+25%). With ~$201M in cash and short-term investments and no disclosed debt against a market cap near $350-400M, the enterprise value implies a deeply depressed multiple on a growing hardware/software platform with 2.85M registered users and a nascent subscription strategy. The setup fits a credible rerating mechanism: forced-sell/distribution pressure exhausted, first clean standalone quarters ahead, and optionality on recurring Arlo Smart revenue. Downside is tolerable because the net-cash balance sheet funds ≥12 months per management and provides asset backing near current prices. Offsets that keep this a moderate-conviction position rather than high: six pending securities class actions alleging pre-IPO concealment of quality problems and adverse sales trends (earnings-quality/credibility overhang), ASP compression versus Amazon/Ring and Google/Nest, ~58.5% revenue concentration in Best Buy/Costco/Amazon with no purchase commitments, AWS terminable on 30 days' notice, China tariff exposure, and EGC status without 404(b) attestation. Cheapness alone would not qualify it; here cheapness coincides with completed structural selling and a defined near-term catalyst path (first standalone earnings), so it qualifies as a long candidate with sized-down conviction.
trades.catalyst: First standalone quarterly report as an independent company (Q1 2019) demonstrating that the FY2018 loss was dominated by one-time separation costs while core revenue growth persists; exhaustion of NETGEAR distribution-related selling and potential index inclusion/analyst initiation coverage as the stock trades independently.
trades.invalidation: Next quarterly results showing revenue deceleration, gross-margin compression from ASP declines/tariffs, or operating cash burn materially above expectations; escalation of securities litigation (consolidation with large damages claims); any indication the $201M liquidity buffer is being consumed faster than planned, implying near-term dilution.

trades.thesis: Gran Tierra Energy (GTE, $22.80, -42% from 1y high) shows a genuine fundamental inflection in the just-filed FY2018 10-K: first net income since 2014 ($102.6M vs -$31.7M loss), oil & gas sales +45% to $613.4M, production +8% to 29,053 BOEPD, zero impairments versus $616.6M in 2016, working capital swung to a $33M surplus and the revolver fully repaid. The stock's deep drawdown prices substantial distress that the filings do not support near-term. As a leveraged, pure-play Colombia oil producer, GTE has high beta to Brent, which had been recovering off December 2018 lows toward the company's own $65/bbl self-funding threshold — a credible rerating mechanism via both commodity beta and confirmation of the earnings turnaround in upcoming Q1 results and early 2019 drilling results from the funded $320–340M program. This is not cheapness alone: there is a documented earnings inflection plus an execution catalyst calendar. Offsets are real — leverage rose materially ($300M new senior notes, LT debt $399.4M), royalties climbed to 20% of WI production, funding is explicitly contingent on Brent >=$65/bbl, semiannual borrowing-base redetermination creates a discrete refinancing tail, and 100% Colombia concentration adds social/political idiosyncratic risk. Net: asymmetric setup favoring modest positive excess return with meaningful but tolerable tail risk; size accordingly rather than conviction-weight.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2019 results and early wells from the $320–340M 2019 drilling program (roughly May–June), alongside continued Brent strength above the company's stated $65/bbl self-funding threshold, providing tangible proof points that the 2018 earnings inflection is sustainable.
trades.invalidation: Brent breaking decisively below ~$60/bbl, an adverse borrowing-base redetermination forcing debt repayment, material community/social disruption to Colombian operations, or Q1 results showing margin compression from rising royalties (20% of WI production and climbing).

trades.thesis: Madrigal is a single-asset clinical-stage biotech (MGL-3196, THR-beta agonist for NASH/HeFH) trading ~57% below its 1-year high (~$134 vs ~$315), yet it holds ~$483.7M in cash/marketable securities against only ~15.4M shares outstanding (~$2.1B market cap, ~23% cash coverage) and no debt. The fundamental case rests entirely on pipeline optionality: positive Phase 2 NASH data (12-wk endpoint met Dec 2017; positive 36-wk topline May 2018) and positive HeFH Phase 2 (Feb 2018), with registrational trials explicitly planned. The stock has already de-rated through the post-data air pocket typical of mid-cap biotech; the credible near-term rerating mechanism is disclosure flow around the completed 36-week biopsy dataset (extension study underway) and formalization/initiation of Phase 3 plans in a NASH field that commanded premium multiples in early 2019. Cash covers years of burn (~$40M operating loss, ~$25M operating cash use), so dilution is not a near-term forcing function despite boilerplate 'substantial additional capital' language. Risks are real: THR-class toxicity precedent (eprotirome failed Phase 3 on liver/cartilage toxicity), single-asset concentration, no completed pivotal trial, G&A nearly doubling, and insider-affiliated ownership of ~39.1% with preferred/options overhang. On balance, the setup — deep drawdown, funded runway, positive human efficacy data, and imminent data-dissemination catalysts — skews the 90-day distribution favorably enough to justify a long candidate stance, sized for binary clinical risk.
trades.catalyst: Presentation/publication of the completed 36-week NASH Phase 2 liver-biopsy histology data (extension/topline readouts due near-term) and initiation of registrational Phase 3 trials for MGL-3196 in NASH — either event can drive a sharp rerating in a single-asset name with a demonstrated history of large binary moves on data.
trades.invalidation: Any safety signal consistent with the eprotirome precedent (hepatic events, cartilage findings) in ongoing MGL-3196 extension/hepatic-impairment data; delay or retreat from stated registrational trial plans; a large equity raise signaling runway stress; or failure of the biopsy dataset to corroborate the earlier topline endpoints.

trades.thesis: UroGen enters March 2019 at $38.38, 41% below its 1-year high and below the $41.00 January 2019 follow-on price, despite materially de-risked fundamentals: Phase 3 OLYMPUS fully enrolled (71 patients) with a strong 57% ITT complete-response interim readout, Breakthrough Therapy/Fast Track designations, and a rolling NDA for UGN-101 expected to complete in H2 2019 — a dated regulatory catalyst largely inside the 90-day window. The balance sheet is unusually clean for a clinical-stage name: $101.3M YE2018 cash plus $161.8M net January proceeds (~$263M pro forma) against only $13.5M total liabilities and no debt, with unqualified F/S and ICFR audit opinions. The recent raise at $41.00 both funds the NDA pathway and provides a soft valuation anchor above spot. Bearish counterweights are real but mostly slow-burning: net loss widened to $75.7M (G&A $39.6M vs $8.8M), approval rests on a single-arm pivotal trial, Allergan collaboration is terminable at will, ~4.5M registration-rights shares create overhang, and management itself flags substantial future financing needs. The setup is a credible near-term rerating mechanism (NDA completion/priority review eligibility) paired with tolerable downside (funded runway, clean audit, anchor at the recent deal price), satisfying the long-candidate bar rather than cheapness alone.
trades.catalyst: Completion of UGN-101 rolling NDA submission in H2 2019 (within/near the 90-day window) with Breakthrough Therapy/Fast Track designations supporting priority-review eligibility; potential positive newsflow on OLYMPUS final data and UGN-102 Phase 2b progress as secondary catalysts.
trades.invalidation: FDA refusal-to-file or unexpected delay of the UGN-101 NDA, disclosure of additional pivotal-trial requirements beyond the single-arm study, accelerated cash burn signaling an earlier follow-on, or Allergan collaboration termination would invalidate the rerating thesis.

trades.thesis: Puma Biotechnology enters March 2019 down ~66% from its 1-year high (~$27.81) despite a genuine commercial inflection: NERLYNX product revenue grew from $26.2M (2017) to $200.5M (2018), license revenue added $50.5M, R&D declined to $164.9M, and operating cash burn collapsed to $24.1M from $172.5M — the company is approaching operating cash breakeven on a single approved asset with $108.4M cash. That combination (steep drawdown + rapidly improving unit economics + an approved drug ramping) creates a credible rerating mechanism: the next quarterly print (Q1 2019, due early May, inside the 90-day window) can demonstrate continued prescription growth and validate the path to self-funding, which the market is not pricing at a ~$1.2B market cap against ~$250M annualized product revenue. Offsetting this, risks are real and specific: the February 2019 Hsu jury verdict ($4.50/share, accrued at only $9.0M with uncertain upside), a fully drawn $155M SVB/Oxford facility with a minimum-revenue covenant, heavy customer concentration (three customers = 77% of revenue), diarrhea-related adherence risk, and explicit dilution language. On balance the fundamental momentum is verifiable from primary filings while the bear case is largely contingent/risk-factor-based; the asymmetry after a two-thirds drawdown favors a modest-sized long, not a conviction position.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2019 earnings (early May 2019, within the 90-day window): sequential NERLYNX prescription/revenue data validating the launch ramp against low post-drawdown expectations; secondary support from first ex-US partner launches under the September 2018 EC authorization.
trades.invalidation: Q1 2019 NERLYNX net sales flat-to-down sequentially or gross-to-net deterioration (payer pushback), signaling the 2018 ramp was channel-fill; any covenant disclosure, emergency financing, or material increase in litigation damages would invalidate the thesis immediately.

trades.thesis: The issuer enters the window deeply depressed (-41% from 1-year high, ~$94.89) despite demonstrably strong operations: Q1 FY2019 revenue +7.4% to $598.4M, operating income +42.5% to $68.6M, SG&A leverage from the organization redesign, and operating cash flow swinging to +$38.8M with capex nearly halved. The dominant overhang is the $347.9M current-liability convertible maturity due June 2019 against only $37.6M unrestricted cash — but the company has explicitly reserved $285.0M of ABL availability for this repayment, holds $65M restricted cash, has an undrawn revolver, and generates positive free cash flow, making resolution of this binary event the credible near-term rerating mechanism. Once the June 2019 notes are retired, the narrative shifts from refinancing distress to a leveraged-but-improving operator with ~$450M remaining buyback authorization. This is not cheapness alone: there is a dated, resolvable catalyst plus confirmed operating momentum. Risks are real — $(247.4)M stockholders' deficit after a debt-funded $250M buyback, two revised prior-period accounting errors, rising net interest expense (+$6.0M to $21.1M), a growing $60.1M legal settlement accrual, and 'no assurance' refinancing language for the 2020/2023 converts — so position sizing must respect an elevated left tail, but the asymmetry at a 41% drawdown with intact fundamentals favors a long candidacy.
trades.catalyst: Resolution of the $350M June 2019 convertible maturity (repayment via reserved ABL capacity or refinancing) within weeks of the cutoff removes the largest overhang, followed by Q2 FY2019 results in September that can confirm sustained revenue growth, SG&A leverage from the organization redesign, and positive free cash flow — supporting a rerating of a stock already down ~41% from its 1-year high.
trades.invalidation: Failure or adverse terms in refinancing/settling the June 2019 notes (e.g., ABL borrowing-base shortfall, punitive pricing, or equity-linked dilution well below expectations); additional covenant waivers or defaults; a Q2 guidance cut or reversal of the margin/SG&A leverage trend; material escalation of the legal settlement beyond the $60.1M accrual; or any new material weakness in internal controls.

trades.thesis: Micron at ~$31.87 (-45% from its 1-year high) prices in most of the visible memory downturn: FQ3'19 revenue fell 39% YoY and gross margin compressed from ~61% to ~38%, yet the company still generated $10.96B of nine-month operating cash flow versus $7.75B capex, holds ~$6.7B cash+ST investments against only ~$4.9B debt, and has ~$7.34B left on its buyback authorization after repurchasing $2.66B. This is a classic trough-multiple setup where the balance sheet caps fundamental downside while sentiment, not earnings power, drives the multiple. A credible rerating mechanism exists within the 90-day window: the dated IMFT buyout from Intel closes October 31, 2019, a ~$120M Singapore fab gain lands in FQ4, ongoing buybacks provide a persistent bid, and any sign of memory pricing/inventory stabilization (WIP build notwithstanding) typically triggers sharp re-rating off cyclical lows given how depressed expectations are. The bet is not on an earnings recovery but on the market recognizing trough economics at a net-cash-backed valuation. Risks are real — Huawei is 13% of revenue with unresolved export restrictions, inventories built 36% into falling prices, and securities/antitrust litigation (SAMR, class actions naming CEO/CFO) creates headline overhang — so position sizing must respect a wide distribution rather than treat cheapness as sufficient alone.
trades.catalyst: FQ4 results plus management commentary signaling inventory discipline and pricing stabilization; IMFT buyout closing October 31, 2019 simplifying the NAND JV structure; continued large buybacks against ~$7.34B remaining authorization; ~$120M Singapore fab sale gain in FQ4; potential de-escalation of Huawei export restrictions (macro event, not filing-grounded).
trades.invalidation: Further sequential DRAM/NAND ASP declines or supplier inventory liquidation; FQ4 guidance implying deeper margin compression; hardening of Huawei export restrictions cutting into the 13% revenue exposure; new inventory write-downs; SAMR/antitrust outcomes imposing material penalties.

trades.thesis: STAAR Surgical enters H2 2019 with genuinely accelerating fundamentals against a depressed stock (-40% from 1-year high at $30.30): Q2 net sales +17% YoY, ICL sales +26% with 34% unit growth, gross margin up to 75.4%, and operating margin expanding to 11.6% from 8.9% — clear operating leverage. Management affirms it is on track for FY2019 targets of 20% revenue / 30% ICL unit growth, and the EDOF ICL presbyopia trial met its primary endpoint with data submitted to the European Notified Body, plus a revised FDA submission for EVO lenses — a credible pipeline rerating mechanism. The balance sheet is a fortress ($103.3M cash vs ~$2.9M drawn LOC, $130.2M working capital, covenant compliance), removing financing tail risk. The 40% drawdown appears sentiment-driven (China concentration ~49% of Q2 sales via one distributor amid tariff fears, ASP pressure, declining other-product sales) rather than fundamental, since the core ICL franchise is accelerating. If China fears stabilize and the growth/leverage trajectory continues into Q3, a meaningful rerating is plausible; the $37.7M valuation allowance offers additional asymmetric upside. This is a momentum-plus-catalyst setup, not merely a cheap stock. Key risks temper sizing: heavy SBC ($5.2M H1, nearly equal to net income) with 4.6M option overhang, near-breakeven FCF, AR build, and binary China/tariff exposure.
trades.catalyst: Continued beat-and-raise cadence into Q3/Q4 2019 results with management reaffirming or raising the 20% revenue / 30% ICL unit growth targets, plus progression of the EDOF ICL regulatory submissions following the met primary endpoint; potential valuation allowance release as a secondary earnings kicker.
trades.invalidation: Q3 2019 results (due ~early November, near the end of the window) showing ICL unit growth decelerating below the 30% target, renewed China/tariff disruption to the ~49%-of-sales distributor channel, or withdrawal/lowering of the FY2019 growth targets; also any disclosure of material ASP collapse or new dilutive financing.

trades.thesis: The Q2 2019 10-Q documents a genuine operating inflection: first quarterly GAAP operating profit ($290K) and net income ($387K), revenue +15% YoY (+25% H1), gross margin up to ~58%, and a swing to +$7.7M H1 operating cash flow. Combined with $27.4M cash, zero debt, an undrawn $10M facility, and ~$59.3M of contracted RPO ($17.7M recognizable in the remainder of 2019), the company has both a credible rerating mechanism (sustained profitability confirmed by the Q3 print due within the window) and bounded downside (net cash, positive FCF, recurring ratable subscription revenue). The stock sits 43% below its 1-year high at $35.80, so even modest confirmation of the inflection could re-rate a small-cap (~$410M cap) that has crossed into GAAP profitability. However, skepticism is warranted: the cash-flow improvement leans heavily on a one-off $7.7M City of Chicago collection, short-term deferred revenue declined sequentially, two customers are 34% of revenue, the Simmons civil-rights litigation alleging fabricated evidence is an unquantified tail risk, ~3.3M residual S-3 shares create dilution overhang, and a known 3G-to-LTE sensor upgrade cost headwind begins mid-2020. This is a qualified long candidate, not a high-conviction one — position sizing should reflect the concentration, litigation, and earnings-quality caveats.
trades.catalyst: Q3 2019 earnings report (due early November, inside the 90-day window) as the next checkpoint to confirm the profitability inflection; secondary support from continued buyback execution under the May 2019 authorization and any new city contract/deployment announcements against the ~700 sq-mile contracted footprint.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 2019 results (or interim disclosures) show revenue growth decelerating below ~10%, a return to operating losses excluding the Chicago collection effect, further short-term deferred revenue erosion signaling weak renewals/new bookings, material adverse development in the Simmons litigation, or a shelf takedown of the residual S-3 shares.

trades.thesis: IRadimed-class microcap MRI-compatible device maker trading ~42% below its 1-year high ($19.55 pre-cutoff) despite objectively strong fundamentals: Q2 2019 revenue +25% YoY to $9.23M, operating income +42%, ~80% gross margins, $37.8M cash/investments with zero debt, and positive operating cash flow. The drawdown appears attributable to a discrete, identifiable overhang — the January 16, 2019 suspension of 3880 monitor shipments into CE-Mark markets — rather than deteriorating economics (US revenue drove all growth; international was flat, consistent with the suspension already being priced in). The rerating mechanism is credible and dated: renewed EC Certificates from new notified body PCBC are explicitly expected before end of August 2019, and management targets resumption of CE-Mark shipments near the beginning of fiscal Q4 2019 — both within the 90-day window. Resolution would restore an estimated ~$1.7M/quarter international monitoring stream and remove the primary narrative overhang. Downside is tolerable given the debt-free balance sheet, self-funded operations, and the fact that much of the bad news (suspension, flat international) appears already embedded after a 42% drawdown. Cheapness alone is not the case here — there is a specific, dated regulatory catalyst layered on genuine operating momentum. Key discounts applied: the FDA Warning Letter remains open as of June 30, 2019, AR grew faster than revenue (+40% vs +22%), S&M spend rose 45%, and CEO/Chairman insider control with a related-party lease caps governance quality. Microcap size (~11.4M shares, ~$2M/day dollar volume) limits position sizing and adds volatility.
trades.catalyst: Renewed EC Certificates from PCBC expected before end of August 2019 (dated, near-term), followed by 3880 monitor CE recertification via ECM and resumption of suspended CE-Mark shipments targeted near the start of fiscal Q4 2019 — restoring a suspended international revenue stream and removing a known overhang that likely drove the -42% drawdown from the 1-year high.
trades.invalidation: Failure of PCBC to issue renewed EC Certificates by early September 2019, further slippage of the 3880 ECM recertification beyond fiscal Q4 2019, or any adverse FDA action on the still-open Warning Letter would invalidate the thesis; a break below post-Q2 lows on heavy volume alongside catalyst slippage would exit the position.

trades.thesis: Moderna-type clinical-stage mRNA issuer trading ~55% below its 1-year high (~$12.85) roughly eight months post-IPO. The filing picture is fundamentally unattractive as a standalone long: revenue halved YoY ($13.1M vs $28.9M in Q2), H1 operating cash burn accelerated ~60% to $256M, management explicitly states it needs substantial additional funding via equity/debt issuance, and ASC 606 flattered neither side (revenue optics partly accounting-driven). However, the balance sheet is genuinely strong — ~$1.44B cash and investments versus only $33.6M of lease debt — giving multi-quarter runway and making a 90-day solvency event essentially impossible. The rerating case rests on mean reversion in a deeply de-rated recent IPO with real pipeline optionality (13 of 21 candidates in clinic, >1,000 subjects enrolled, Merck collaboration recently amended) rather than any disclosed dated catalyst. Skeptically applied, cheapness-plus-cash alone does not meet the bar for a long candidate: there is no credible near-term rerating mechanism visible in the filings, and the dilution overhang is explicit. The asymmetric setup (limited downside from cash coverage, wide distribution from pipeline optionality after a -55% drawdown) justifies a constructive watch posture, not initiation.
trades.catalyst: No dated catalysts disclosed in the filing; potential rerating drivers are non-filing events — interim clinical data readouts across the 13 clinical-stage candidates, expansion of the Merck collaboration (Fifth Amendment terms redacted), or a large strategic financing/licensing deal that pre-empts the dilution overhang. Absent one of these, the stock likely trades on biotech sector beta.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the company announces a discounted equity raise without a partnering offset (confirms dilution at weak prices), if a lead clinical program reports safety or efficacy failure, or if the stock breaks below the post-IPO low on volume — signaling the drawdown is fundamental repricing rather than sentiment.

trades.thesis: Veritone-type microcap AI software issuer trading at ~$6.81 after a -57% drawdown, implying roughly a $150M market cap against $45.3M net cash (no debt) and a ~$49M annualized revenue run-rate growing ~194% YoY (Q2'19 $12.27M vs $4.17M). The bear case — unremediated material weakness in disclosure controls, widening operating losses (-$16.7M Q2), negative operating cash flow (-$16.6M H1), and explicit dependence on dilutive ATM issuance ($35.5M remaining capacity) — is well telegraphed and substantially priced in at a 57% discount to the 1-year high. The bull case rests on a credible rerating mechanism: demonstrated hypergrowth with sharply improved customer concentration (top-10 down to ~26% from ~50%), an EV/revenue multiple near ~2x that can expand if the next quarterly print confirms organic momentum, and a cash-plus-no-debt balance sheet that makes near-term insolvency unlikely even under continued burn. This is not a cheapness-only thesis: the rerating driver is growth validation at the Q3 print within the 90-day window, while the -57% drawdown and net-cash cushion bound the downside. Conviction is deliberately modest because accounting-quality flags (unremediated material weakness tied to complex acquisition accounting, ongoing earnout share issuances) raise restatement/measurement risk, and ATM dilution mechanically caps excess returns in a small float name with ~$2.7M average daily dollar volume.
trades.catalyst: Q3 2019 earnings (early November 2019): another quarter of ~2x+ YoY revenue growth with improved customer concentration would be the first clean post-acquisition-integration proof point, providing the near-term rerating trigger for a deeply discounted AI software name.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 2019 results (due ~November 2019) show organic revenue deceleration or a sequential revenue decline versus Q2's $12.27M, if the material weakness expands beyond acquisition accounting into core revenue recognition, or if aggressive ATM issuance accelerates materially below current prices — any of which would confirm the market's discount is justified.

trades.thesis: American Eagle Outfitters trades at ~$12.02, down 44% from its 1-year high, implying a high-single-digit P/E on ~$1.50-1.60 normalized EPS and a ~4.6% dividend yield, despite fundamentally intact operations: record Q2 revenue (+7.9% to $1,041M), 18 consecutive quarters of positive comps (+2%), modest gross margin expansion, rising Aerie mix (19% vs 16%), and growing international revenue (+33%). The board just authorized a large incremental 30M-share buyback (37.4M total) while the company has no funded debt, $317M cash/investments, and an undrawn $400M revolver — a credible support/rerating mechanism into the seasonally strongest half. The bear case is real but mostly working-capital-timing rather than solvency: H1 OCF fell 23% on a 15% inventory build, shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow, SG&A deleveraged slightly, and markdown risk is explicitly flagged. Cheapness alone is insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with positive comps, an aggressive new buyback at depressed prices, and a dated catalyst (Q3/holiday report within the window). Base-rate skepticism on apparel retail tempers sizing: sector sentiment and tariff/markdown risk keep this a moderate-conviction candidate, not a high-conviction one.
trades.catalyst: Q3 FY2019 earnings report (~early December 2019) covering the back-to-school/holiday selling season — the filing explicitly notes H2 concentration of revenue and operating income; sustained positive comps (18 consecutive quarters) plus aggressive buybacks at ~$12 could drive a rerating from a distressed multiple toward a normal retail valuation.
trades.invalidation: Negative or sharply decelerating comparable sales through back-to-school/holiday, forced markdowns clearing the elevated inventory (gross margin compression), or guidance withdrawal — visible at the Q3 report or via interim sales commentary; also any drawdown of the revolver signaling liquidity stress.

trades.thesis: Ollie's has been de-rated ~42% from its 1-year high ($59.20 vs prior peak) largely on an investment-phase earnings air pocket: Q2 FY2019 net sales grew +15.9% to $333.9M but operating income fell 11.8% and diluted EPS dropped to $0.38 from $0.45, driven by ~200bps gross margin compression, SG&A growing faster than sales (+19.7%), doubled pre-opening expense, and quadrupled capex from an accelerated 332-store expansion. The core growth algorithm appears intact — double-digit sales growth, loyalty deferred revenue +37% signaling healthy Ollie's Army engagement — while the balance sheet is exceptionally clean: near-zero funded debt, no variable-rate debt, $78.5M cash plus $91.1M undrawn revolver (~$170M liquidity), light covenants in compliance. Management immediately deployed $13.5M of the $100M buyback post-quarter-end, providing a credible near-term support/rerating mechanism at a depressed valuation. The bear case is real but mostly cyclical/self-inflicted growth spending rather than demand deterioration; however, evidence gaps (no comparable-store sales data, truncated MD&A margin drivers) prevent high conviction, and YTD FCF ex-sale-leaseback is negative with inventory +23% outpacing sales — a markdown risk into holiday. Net: attractive asymmetry for a modest position, not a high-conviction slam dunk.
trades.catalyst: Continued open-market execution of the $100M buyback ($13.5M already repurchased through Sep 4, 2019) provides near-term demand, with a secondary path to rerating via stabilization of gross margin and pre-opening cost normalization as the 29-store YTD opening class matures into revenue contribution ahead of the holiday quarter.
trades.invalidation: Further sequential gross-margin erosion or disclosure of weak comparable-store sales / slow closeout sell-through into the holiday quarter would invalidate the thesis; a forced markdown cycle against the elevated inventory position or curtailment of buyback activity would signal the margin problem is structural rather than investment-phase.

trades.thesis: Insmed enters Q4 2019 with a genuine first-year product launch: ARIKAYCE posted $38.9M in Q3 revenue (vs $0 prior year), implying sequential acceleration within the $90.8M nine-month total, ~83% gross margin ex-amortization, and narrowing YoY Q3 operating losses ($56.5M vs $84.0M). Liquidity is adequate ($535.6M cash vs ~$70M/quarter burn, management asserting ≥12 months sufficiency; realistically ~2 years runway), so there is no imminent solvency event. However, the case for a 90-day long is weak on the required criteria: (1) no dated catalyst exists in the filings — Europe/Japan regulatory activities are described only aspirationally, with no submission or decision timelines disclosed; (2) SG&A (+41% YTD to $160.6M) still exceeds quarterly revenue, meaning the launch does not yet self-fund; (3) structural overhangs are real — $450M converts convertible at ~$39 (well above the $16.84 price), 80% customer concentration in three specialty pharmacies/distributors, single-product/single-market dependence, and a Chairman/CEO who sold 400k personal shares into the Q2 offering; (4) the stock's 48% drawdown reflects a prior dilution-heavy narrative, not obvious mispricing. The launch ramp is real and could drive sentiment-driven appreciation, but cheapness-on-cash alone is insufficient and the rerating mechanism inside 90 days rests on unquantified prescription uptake rather than any filing-grounded milestone. This is a monitorable story, not a high-conviction long at cutoff.
trades.catalyst: Sequential ARIKAYCE revenue acceleration into Q4 print plus formal European/Japanese regulatory submission announcements (currently undated); any narrowing of operating losses would support a launch-efficiency rerating narrative.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 ARIKAYCE revenue decelerates sequentially, if gross-to-net allowances expand materially, if an equity raise prices below current levels, or if Europe/Japan submissions slip without new dated milestones.

trades.thesis: SunCoke trades at $4.10, down ~51% from its 1-year high, after a headline $(163)M Q3 net loss driven almost entirely by a $247.4M non-cash impairment cluster in the Logistics segment (full goodwill write-off of $73.5M plus $173.9M long-lived asset impairment) triggered by customer credit events (Murray Chapter 11 on Oct 29; Foresight grace period). The core cokemaking franchise remains fundamentally healthy: Q3 revenue +11% YoY ($404.3M), cokemaking revenue +16.5%, positive nine-month operating cash flow of $120.5M, $90.5M of YTD debt reduction, an opportunistic below-par note repurchase, covenant compliance affirmed, and adequate liquidity ($93.7M cash + $244.5M revolver availability) with no major maturity inside 18 months after the August refinancing extended the revolver to 2024. The market appears to be pricing the GAAP loss and logistics contagion rather than the durable, contracted cokemaking cash flows.
