trades.invalidation: Q3 results (early Nov 2022) showing comps deteriorating beyond Q2's -1.5%, gross margin compression accelerating from markdowns on the +7.3% inventory build, ABL borrowings commencing, suspension of buybacks, or holiday guidance withdrawal — any of which would confirm a structural margin reset rather than a cyclical trough.

trades.thesis: Hovnanian screens as a deeply discounted, highly leveraged homebuilder whose two dominant risks have partially resolved while its core risk remains open. Bull case: (1) the August 19, 2022 revolver maturity extension to June 30, 2024 eliminates the most dangerous near-term refinancing cliff for a company that admits it cannot access capital markets competitively, and was paired with a $100M partial redemption of 7.75% notes — recourse debt already cut ~$100M to $1,148M; (2) trailing profitability is exceptional relative to a ~$41 price (Q3 pre-tax income $111.9M vs $61.8M PY; nine-month $169.9M net income on only ~6.4M shares outstanding), implying a very low multiple even after haircuts for earnings quality; (3) $1.13B of homes/lot inventory is substantially deliverable within 6-9 months, offering a genuine cash-conversion path that could rebuild cash and fund the newly adopted September 2022 buyback; (4) liquidity of $357.4M sits above target range with no impairments taken. Bear case, which keeps sizing modest: demand has inflected hard (net contracts -34.0% YoY, absorption 7.6 vs 12.0/community), operating cash flow is negative (-$28.6M) on a $332.9M inventory build increasingly financed off-balance-sheet via land banking ($140.2M draws vs $27.6M PY; consolidated inventory not owned tripled to $280.9M), nonrecourse mortgage costs jumped to 6.1%, and the ~$1.15B stack carries a punishing 9.5% weighted-average rate. The rerating mechanism is therefore credible but conditional: survival/deleveraging de-risked by the maturity extension plus cheapness plus buyback optionality, not a demand recovery. This justifies a small long candidacy rather than a pass, but the -34% order trend means the margin of safety rests on balance-sheet execution, and a leveraged beta name in a falling-rate-shock environment can gap down regardless of fundamentals.
trades.catalyst: Delivery of substantially all $1.13B homes/lot inventory within 6-9 months converts backlog to cash while the extended revolver (June 2024) removes forced-seller/refinancing risk; a newly authorized September 2022 buyback on a ~6.4M-share float provides an explicit per-share rerating channel if sentiment stabilizes.
trades.invalidation: Cancellation acceleration or disclosed price cuts/incentive escalation in coming monthly/quarterly data, any new inventory impairment beyond trivial write-offs, renewed land-bank draw escalation without corresponding deliveries, or loss of revolver availability would invalidate the thesis; also failure of the new buyback to be funded.

trades.thesis: MINISO trades at ~$4.56, down ~70% from its 1-year high, pricing in severe distress that the filings contradict. Fundamentals inflected positively in FY2022: revenue +11.2% to RMB10,085.6M, return to profit (RMB639.7M continuing ops vs prior-year RMB1,429.4M loss driven by non-cash fair-value items now nil), adjusted net profit RMB722.6M, overseas revenue +48.5%, inventory days improved to 70, and RMB5.35B cash against ~$2.8B market cap (~25%+ of cap in cash). The dominant driver of the drawdown appears to be the HFCAA delisting overhang rather than business deterioration. That overhang has a dated, credible resolution mechanism: the Aug 26, 2022 PCAOB-CSRC Statement of Protocol, with inspection outcomes plausibly landing within the 90-day window. Removal of the delisting discount plus continued overseas momentum offers a genuine rerating path, while the cash-rich balance sheet and restored profitability make downside more tolerable than typical distressed Chinese ADRs. Cheapness alone is not the case here — there is a specific near-term catalyst. Offsets keeping this below high conviction: management explicitly guides FY2023 to continued COVID drag and promotion-driven margin pressure, China revenue grew only 2.1%, a putative securities class action was filed Aug 17, 2022, franchisee deposit refund obligations create contingent liquidity risk, receivables loss allowances are rising against flat gross receivables with up-to-180-day credit terms, and PRC dividend repatriation constraints limit how much offshore cash value is accessible. Near-term headline risk exists as the company expects imminent Commission-Identified Issuer designation.
trades.catalyst: PCAOB inspection outcome under the Aug 26, 2022 Statement of Protocol (expected within the 90-day window), which would remove the HFCAA delisting discount; secondary: Q2 FY2023 results in January 2023 showcasing continued overseas momentum and any easing of China COVID restrictions reducing the guided FY2023 drag.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if PCAOB inspections do not proceed or are deemed incomplete (no removal of delisting risk), if Q2 FY2023 results show margin collapse or renewed China revenue decline beyond guidance, or if the securities class action escalates materially; a sustained break below the post-IPO low on heavy volume would signal structural de-rating rather than sentiment-driven weakness.

trades.thesis: Highwoods (HIW, ~$19.24, -43% from 1-year high) enters the window with its nearest maturity wall already removed: on 2022-10-17 it prepaid $250M of 3.625% notes due January 2023 using a new $200M two-year term loan plus cash/revolver, leaving ~$579.9M revolver capacity. Core operations are intact — Q3 rental revenues +5.9% YoY ($207.0M), nine-month operating cash flow up to $319.9M — supporting a maintained $0.50 quarterly dividend (~10.4% yield at cutoff), which historically anchors office REIT floors once refinancing fear abates. The strategic pivot (exiting Pittsburgh, ~6% of NOI, to fund Dallas Class AA development JVs) provides a discrete disposition catalyst within 90-180 days. At a 42.6% drawdown with positive growing cash flow, the stock embeds substantial distress probability that the completed refinancing partially invalidates; mean reversion plus yield support offers asymmetric upside versus SPY off an oversold base. This is a leveraged beta-plus-idiosyncratic-de-risking trade, not a quality compounder: interest expense is running +20% YoY, impairments ($36.5M YTD) confirm softening office values, occupancy is drifting down (91.2%→90.7%), free cash flow is negative before dividends, and disposition execution in a weak office market is genuinely uncertain ("buyers may not be available... pricing may not be adequate"). Position sizing should reflect that office REITs remain hostage to rate path and sentiment.
trades.catalyst: Pittsburgh exit dispositions (2.155M sq ft, ~6% of NOI) monetizing non-core assets at book-ish values to fund Dallas development JVs; each signed disposition is a visible NAV-affirming datapoint. Secondary: any peak-inflation/Fed-pivot signal compressing cap rates pressure would disproportionately re-rate a 10%+ yielding, recently de-risked office REIT trading at a >40% drawdown.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Pittsburgh dispositions stall or clear well below carrying value (confirming further markdowns), if the company cuts or signals a dividend cut given ~$23.1M cash and reliance on external capital, or if a broad office-sector credit event / renewed rate shock drives another leg down regardless of idiosyncratic progress.

trades.thesis: Frontier (FGHI/ULCC) screens as a deeply discounted ultra-low-cost carrier (-43% from 1y high, $9.92) with a genuine Q3 2022 inflection: GAAP net income of $31M (vs $23M PY), operating income $56M, and revenue +44% YoY to $906M, supported by rising air traffic liability ($296M vs $273M) indicating forward bookings. Direct debt is modest ($423M) against $674M cash, so balance-sheet solvency risk is low near-term. However, the case falls short of a high-conviction long: nine-month operating cash flow was negative $(172)M, cash declined $244M YTD, Q3 profitability was flattered by $49M sale-leaseback gains, fuel costs surged +84% YoY, working capital is inverted ($892M current assets vs $1,452M current liabilities), and ~$2.4B of lease obligations sit against only $468M equity. Governance is a structural overhang — an Indigo-managed fund owns ~82.1% with written-consent power, registration rights on 178.8M shares, and ability to sell control without minority approval. Cheapness plus a quarterly profit turn is real but the rerating mechanism lacks a hard-dated catalyst within 90 days, and the seasonally weak Q4/Q1 window plus fuel exposure create two-sided risk. Watch for confirmation that Q3 momentum persists (positive Q4 bookings/cash flow) before upgrading.
trades.catalyst: Q3 2022 GAAP profitability inflection (net income $31M vs $23M PY; operating income $56M) on +44% revenue growth, with air traffic liability up to $296M signaling forward booking strength; potential contingent $69M Spirit break fee if Spirit is acquired within 12 months; possible sector-wide demand-driven rerating of deeply discounted airline equities.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 guidance/bookings show margin compression from fuel and fare softening, if operating cash flow remains negative through year-end driving further cash erosion toward uncomfortable levels, or if Indigo signals secondary sales triggering registration-rights overhang pressure.

trades.thesis: Tenet (THC) trades at $42.52, down ~53% from its 1-year high, with a heavily bearish headline reading from the Q3 2022 10-Q: operating cash flow halved ($662M vs $1,211M), cash down $1.16B to $1,208M, and EPS crushed by absence of prior-year divestiture gains. However, decomposition shows much of the deterioration is mechanical rather than fundamental: ~$880M of the cash drain is one-time recoupment/repayment of COVID-era Medicare advances (vs $326M last year) plus a $942M working-capital outflow, while Adjusted EBITDA actually grew ($2,572M 9M22 vs $2,466M). The structural story is intact and improving in quality: Ambulatory Care (USPI) revenue grew +21% YoY, and the $406M Baylor buyout consolidates 100% of the highest-growth, highest-margin segment. Critically, the board authorized a $1B buyback in October 2022 — roughly 20%+ of the ~$4.5B market cap — a concrete capital-allocation signal at a deeply depressed valuation, alongside a $1.5B undrawn revolver providing liquidity tolerance despite elevated absolute debt ($15.1B). Against a skeptical base rate for leveraged hospital operators post-drawdown, the combination of (a) a dated, funded rerating mechanism (buyback execution), (b) mix-shift toward USPI, (c) fading one-time cash headwinds, and (d) a pending cyber insurance recovery gives a credible 90-day rerating path, while EBITDA coverage and revolver capacity make forced-deleveraging downside tolerable though not negligible given ~$10B goodwill impairment risk.
trades.catalyst: Execution of the fresh $1B buyback against a depressed ~$4.5B equity base, normalization of reported cash flow as the one-time Medicare advance recoupment laps, potential cyber insurance recovery recognition, and continued USPI-driven Adjusted EBITDA growth into year-end reporting.
trades.invalidation: A goodwill impairment charge, guidance cut driven by labor cost escalation or soft surgical volumes, evidence the buyback is not being funded (no repurchases disclosed next quarter), or further cash erosion below ~$1B without revolver stress relief would invalidate the thesis.

trades.thesis: The issuer (FPGA/programmable logic, ~$48.50 pre-cutoff, -43% from 1y high) pairs genuinely accelerating fundamentals with a washed-out valuation. Q3 FY2022 shows +31% YoY revenue growth, ~600bps gross-margin expansion to 68.8%, operating income nearly doubling (28.3% margin), and nine-month operating cash flow of $156.8M exceeding net income — high-quality growth, not accrual-driven. The balance sheet is self-funding: $118.8M cash, modest $150M revolver due 2027 with substantial undrawn capacity, and a fully utilized $100M buyback ($90.1M at avg $54.19) plus a new $150M authorization — insider-calibrated support near current prices. After a -43% drawdown, expectations are reset while fundamentals still compound, giving a credible rerating mechanism into the FY2022 print/guidance cycle. The bear case is real but mostly forward-looking: inventory up 39% to 159 days, ~90% distributor concentration, China at 44% of revenue under new export controls, restructuring charges, legal costs outside ordinary course, and a tax rate flattered by uncertain-position releases. These argue for sizing discipline, not avoidance; nothing in the filing evidences an actual demand break, controls are effective, and liquidity is explicitly sufficient for 12+ months.
trades.catalyst: No hard-dated catalyst in the filing; the rerating mechanism is a combination of (a) confirmation of sustained ~30% growth and ~28% operating margins at the FY2022 report/early-2023 guidance season against a deeply compressed multiple, and (b) continued aggressive buyback execution at depressed prices, with a new $150M authorization signaling management conviction.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4/FY2022 results or guidance show decelerating bookings/order intake, inventory days continuing to climb alongside slowing sell-through (channel-fill signal), further China restriction escalation hitting the 44% China mix, or distributor destocking announcements; a decisive break below the October low (~$43) on volume would also invalidate the oversold-rerating setup.

trades.thesis: CRISPR Therapeutics enters November 2022 down ~46% from its 1-year high at $52.34 (~$4.1B market cap on 78.3M shares) with a dated, filing-grounded rerating mechanism: FDA-granted rolling review of the exa-cel BLA begins this month with submission completing by end of Q1 2023, plus EMA/MHRA submissions by year-end. Because Phase 3 enrollment is complete and pivotal data were already presented at EHA in mid-2022, these are execution/regulatory milestones rather than fresh data readouts, making positive news flow over the next 90 days the base case. The bearish fundamentals are real but largely optical: the revenue collapse to $1.2M reflects lapping the one-time $900M Vertex upfront, not deterioration, and R&D growth (+51%) is pipeline investment. Critically, the balance sheet provides tolerable downside: ~$1.97B in cash and securities versus ~$4.1B market cap (~48% cash coverage), no debt, and only ~$127M/quarter burn implies multi-year runway without forced financing. This is a rare setup where cheapness is backed by both a credible near-term catalyst and a hard-asset floor; the main risks are sector beta in a weak biotech tape, potential sell-the-news dynamics around submission completion, and eventual dilution optionality (~72M authorized-unissued shares).
trades.catalyst: Exa-cel FDA BLA rolling review beginning November 2022 with submission complete by end of Q1 2023, plus EMA/MHRA submissions by end-2022 — a steady cadence of regulatory progress news within the 90-day window on a Phase 3-complete asset with a commercialization partner (Vertex) and $200M approval milestone attached.
trades.invalidation: Slippage or hold placed on the exa-cel BLA rolling review/submission timeline, a clinical or manufacturing setback disclosed in risk factors or 8-K, or acceleration of equity issuance against the ~72M-share authorized-unissued capacity; also a broad risk-off move in unprofitable biotech that overwhelms idiosyncratic catalysts.

trades.thesis: UPCIC/Universal is a deeply beaten-down (-46% from 1y high, ~$8.68, trading near depressed book value of ~$260.6M equity) Florida homeowners insurer whose Q3 collapse is dominated by an identifiable one-time event (Hurricane Ian) rather than franchise impairment. Direct premiums written grew +15.6% YoY, G&A was flat, investment income doubled, and nine-month operating cash flow remained solidly positive ($223.2M) even through the cat quarter — the cash engine works. The rerating mechanism is concrete and dated: FLOIR-approved overall rate increases take effect for renewals on November 4, 2022 (plus eight other states), so earned premium should reprice sharply just as the 90-day window opens, while the Florida market is consolidating around surviving carriers. Balance-sheet solvency risks are real but bounded near term: only $103M long-term debt, undrawn renewed $37.5M revolver, $307M cash, and a clean Plante & Moran interim review. The main unresolved unknown is the net retained Ian loss behind the $935.8M reinsurance recoverable; the market has already marked the equity down ~46%, so a survivable resolution plus visible rate-driven margin recovery is plausibly a positive surprise, while adverse development is partially pre-priced. This is a mean-reversion/value-with-catalyst setup, not a quality compounder — sized accordingly.
trades.catalyst: Q4 2022 earnings quantifying a survivable net Hurricane Ian loss plus collection of ceded recoverables; approved FLOIR rate increases hitting renewals from Nov 4, 2022 onward; continued consolidation/insolvency of weaker Florida homeowners competitors supporting pricing durability; potential AOCI recovery if rates stabilize.
trades.invalidation: Disclosure that net retained Hurricane Ian losses materially impair statutory surplus (recoverable collectability shortfall or reinsurer disputes), failure of the November renewal-season rate increases to show up in earned premium trajectory, or a further capital event (dividend cut followed by regulatory scrutiny, drawn revolver) would invalidate the thesis.

trades.thesis: Brookdale is a deeply discounted (-42% from 1y high, ~$4.37) leveraged seniors-housing operator with a credible, dated near-term rerating mechanism: the October 2022 Ventas master lease amendment covering 24 communities is explicitly expected to generate sale accounting and a non-cash gain in Q4 2022, with cleaner operating-lease treatment thereafter. Underlying momentum is genuinely improving — Q3 resident fees +8.3% YoY, segment operating income $194.5M vs $123.4M, operating cash flow swung positive ($51.8M nine months) — and the post-quarter $220M refinancing removed 2023 maturities while covenants were stated as met with 93.9% of debt non-recourse. The setup fits a mean-reversion-with-catalyst profile rather than pure cheapness. Material discounts apply: Q3 profitability is heavily flattered by ~$66.8M of one-time government grants, facility opex is growing faster than revenue, impairments are rising, equity ($491M) is thin against ~$4.4B of debt/financing leases, revolver capacity is nearly consumed, and ~60M potentially dilutive shares (converts + Ventas warrant at $3.00) cap upside. Net: modest positive expected excess return driven by the Q4 gain catalyst and occupancy-recovery narrative, with meaningful but tolerable tail risk given covenant compliance and non-recourse structure.
trades.catalyst: Q4 2022 disclosure of the non-cash sale-accounting gain from the October 2022 amended master lease (24 communities), alongside Q4 occupancy/revenue prints showing continued senior-housing demand recovery; secondary support from the completed $220M refinancing that removed 2023 maturities.
trades.invalidation: Core (ex-grant) operating losses continuing to widen, renewed impairments signaling stalled occupancy recovery, cash burn below the new $130M minimum liquidity covenant, or any covenant/cross-default event under the master leases would invalidate the thesis.

trades.thesis: Workday (inferred from filings: dual-class founders Duffield/Bhusri, Oct fiscal quarter end, subscription model) trades at $145.25, down ~48.5% from its 1-year high, yet the just-filed Q3 FY23 10-Q shows subscription revenue up 22% YoY ($1,432.4M), total revenue +20.5%, a $14.1B RPO backlog, and solidly positive operating cash flow ($408.7M in Q3, $962.7M nine months). The bear case is concentrated in GAAP losses driven by very heavy SBC ($933.7M nine months), cost growth (+24.7%) outpacing revenue, a declining unearned revenue balance, and a new interest burden from the April 2022 $3.0B refinancing — but none of these threaten solvency given $5.5B of cash plus marketable securities, zero near-term debt maturities (2027/2029/2032 notes), and a $1.0B undrawn revolver. With the stock de-rated ~50% while fundamentals grow >20%, the setup offers an asymmetric rerating mechanism: the late-January/February Q4 print plus fresh FY24 guidance can re-anchor multiples, supported by a newly authorized $500M buyback. Cheapness alone would be insufficient, but here cheapness coexists with intact double-digit recurring growth and fortress liquidity, giving tolerable downside. Skeptical discount applied for margin erosion, SBC dilution, unearned revenue softness, and entrenched dual-class governance that limits catalyst optionality.
trades.catalyst: Q4 FY2023 earnings report (late January/February 2023): if subscription revenue sustains ~20% growth with stable non-GAAP margins and management guides FY24 above consensus, the stock could rerate sharply from a depressed base; the newly authorized $500M buyback provides incremental support into the print.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 results show subscription growth decelerating below ~18%, non-GAAP margin guidance implying further compression below ~18%, or accelerating unearned revenue declines signaling bookings weakness; a broad risk-off leg taking SPY materially lower would also negate the excess-return setup.

trades.thesis: GitLab trades at $38.33, ~60% below its 1-year high, implying a heavily de-rated multiple (~13x annualized revenue EV/sales before ~$928M net cash, i.e., low-teens ex-cash) despite +69% YoY revenue growth ($112.98M in Q3 FY23), ~87% gross margin, growing deferred revenue ($217.8M current), and a debt-free balance sheet with ~$928M in cash and short-term investments (~16% of market cap). The rerating mechanism is credible: hyper-growth SaaS names compressed indiscriminately in 2022's rate shock, and any stabilization in rates/spending sentiment plus confirmation of growth durability at the next print offers substantial multiple-recovery torque. Downside is tolerable because there is no funding risk (no debt, multi-year runway against $(65.7)M nine-month operating burn) and much of the GAAP loss is surging SBC rather than cash burn. That said, this is not a clean setup: disclosure controls are NOT effective due to an unremediated ICFR material weakness over non-routine transactions, opex grew exactly as fast as revenue (zero operating leverage, operating loss widened to $(57.0)M), SBC ran ~29% of nine-month revenue with heavy share issuance, and the consolidated Chinese VIE JiHu (stake diluted to 55%) adds governance and FX complexity. Cheapness plus growth is present; the missing piece is a dated catalyst, so position as a candidate sized for the control/dilution overhangs rather than a conviction long.
trades.catalyst: No dated catalyst disclosed; most credible near-term rerating path is the upcoming fiscal Q4 report/guidance demonstrating sustained ~40%+ growth plus any early cost-discipline signal, amplified by a sector-wide multiple recovery in unprofitable high-growth software if rates stabilize.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the next quarterly print shows decelerating growth (YoY growth stepping down sharply), deferred revenue/RPO stagnation, accelerating operating burn without cost actions, or escalation of the ICFR material weakness into a restatement or auditor concern.

trades.thesis: Emergent-type profile (Gaithersburg life sciences, USG countermeasures + CDMO): stock is down ~72% from its 1-year high at $12.38, so expectations are heavily washed out. Against that depressed base sit two concrete, dated-or-near-dated positives inside the 90-day window: (1) a pending FDA OTC-switch decision for NARCAN Nasal Spray — a genuine rerating catalyst for the largest commercial franchise, with no disclosed date but historically fast review timelines for naloxone switches; and (2) the agreed Bavarian Nordic divestiture of the travel health business (~$270M cash per governance extraction), expected to close around Q2 2023, which directly addresses the most acute fear — liquidity into the October 2023 Senior Secured Credit Facilities maturity. The bear case is real but largely known and priced: ICFR material weakness on inventory capitalization, going-concern-adjacent funding language, securities class actions/derivative suits/government investigations, USG procurement uncertainty, and single-site manufacturing risk. With the equity already marked down 72%, incremental bad news has compressed marginal impact while the binary FDA catalyst offers asymmetric upside. This is a catalyst-driven special situation, not a quality compounder: cheapness alone would not qualify it, but the combination of a credible near-term regulatory rerating mechanism, divestiture-funded bridge liquidity, and a deeply discounted entry justifies a modest-sized long candidacy rather than rejection.
trades.catalyst: FDA decision on NARCAN Nasal Spray Rx-to-OTC switch application (pending as of filing; decision plausibly lands within the 90-day window), supplemented by expected Q2 2023 close of the Bavarian Nordic travel health sale bringing non-dilutive cash ahead of the October 2023 refinancing event.
trades.invalidation: Thesis weakens if the FDA issues a CRL or delays action on the NARCAN OTC application without a new decision date, if the Bavarian Nordic sale fails to close or is renegotiated, or if covenant stress/refinancing disclosures surface before the divestiture proceeds are secured.

trades.thesis: ImmunityBio-type clinical-stage biotech at $2.44 (−65% from 1y high) has exactly one credible near-term rerating mechanism: the Anktiva (N-803) BLA PDUFA date of May 23, 2023, which falls inside the 90-day window. However, the setup is a discounted binary, not a quality long. The FDA already failed to approve by the December 31, 2022 contractual milestone (terminating the ~$304M regulatory CVR), so ex-ante approval odds should be haircut well below a typical first-cycle accepted BLA. Fundamentals are weak: $108.0M cash/marketable securities vs. $737.4M related-party promissory notes held by entities affiliated with the Executive Chairman (76.7% owner), no product revenue, $2.4B accumulated deficit, explicit disclosure of needing additional financing with no committed capital. Notes convertible at $5.67/share imply roughly 130M shares of potential dilution on 435.8M shares outstanding, meaningfully capping approval-driven upside. Asymmetry is roughly balanced-to-slightly-positive: an approval could produce a large pop off a depressed base, while a second refusal would likely drive a further drawdown; the related-party lender makes forced insolvency unlikely within 90 days, which truncates the worst tail but does not remove equity downside. Cheapness plus a live binary is not sufficient for a long candidate under skeptical base rates — this warrants watch status pending stronger evidence on approval likelihood (e.g., late-cycle review clarity) rather than initiation.
trades.catalyst: Anktiva (N-803) BLA PDUFA action date of May 23, 2023 — a dated, hard regulatory catalyst falling inside the 90-day window that could drive a sharp rerating on approval.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if FDA issues a second refusal/CRL or extends the PDUFA date beyond the window (removes the rerating mechanism), or if the company announces deeply dilutive emergency financing below the $5.67 conversion price before the action date.

trades.thesis: This is a deeply drawn-down (-73% from 1y high) Nevada-incorporated Bitcoin miner whose FY2022 10-K (filed 2023-03-02) carries severe accounting-quality damage: a full restatement of FY2020/FY2021 annual and 2021-2022 interim financials determined 2023-02-27, management-concluded ICFR material weaknesses, explicit restatement risk on crypto accounting, securities class actions/derivative suits, and an admitted dependence on dilutive ATM issuance with further capital raises expected — with the ability to raise jeopardized by its own depressed share price. Against this, the only credible rerating mechanisms are cyclical/external: high-beta torque to any Bitcoin price recovery, plus operational milestones (Rockdale 400 MW expansion finalizing in Q1 2023, substation at 700 MW, Corsicana targeted for 2023). Cheapness after a 73% drawdown is real but insufficient under the mandate: there is no company-specific, verifiable near-term rerating catalyst while the restatement magnitude (Note 2), cash runway, debt schedule, and impairment figures are all absent from the supplied excerpts. The equity is effectively a leveraged, governance-impaired call option on Bitcoin with an active accounting scandal and probable dilution inside the 90-day window — asymmetric both ways, with a fat left tail if financing stress forces discounted issuance or litigation escalates.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2023 completion of the fourth Rockdale building finalizing the 400 MW expansion, plus any stabilization/rally in Bitcoin prices that restores hash-rate economics; secondary: clarity on restatement magnitude in Note 2 that could cap the accounting discount.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if Note 2 reveals large misstatement magnitudes affecting reported revenue/earnings, if the auditor qualification/litigation escalates, or if Bitcoin breaks below marginal-cost levels forcing distressed equity issuance — any of which would deepen the discount rather than close it.

trades.thesis: Clinical-stage biotech (atacicept in IgAN) trading at $7.30, ~69% below its 1-year high, with two dated, quote-grounded catalysts inside the 90-day window: full 36-week ORIGIN data and planned pivotal Phase 3 IgAN initiation, both in Q2 2023. The January 2023 positive 24-week topline (statistical significance at 150 mg) partially de-risks the readout. Balance sheet is adequate near-term ($114.7M cash, ≥12-month runway) versus a ~$323M market cap, so downside is bounded by cash rather than imminent insolvency, though long-term going-concern language, a fully drawn $25M Oxford loan, and sharply accelerating burn ($89.1M FY2022 loss) make dilution highly probable beyond the window. This is a catalyst-driven rerating setup, not a value setup: expectations are depressed after the drawdown, and a clean 36-week dataset plus Phase 3 start could re-rate the name, while the April 3 lock-up expiry and eventual financing needs cap conviction. Modest sizing appropriate given binary-event variance.
trades.catalyst: ORIGIN 36-week full dataset readout in Q2 2023 (deeper proteinuria reduction trend already signaled) plus planned pivotal Phase 3 IgAN initiation in Q2 2023 — both dated inside the forecast window.
trades.invalidation: Ambiguous or disappointing 36-week proteinuria data, slippage of the Phase 3 IgAN initiation past the window, an early-waived lock-up driving insider selling into weakness, or a discounted equity raise before the readouts.

trades.thesis: Carnival's Q1 FY23 10-Q shows an unambiguous operating inflection: revenues nearly tripled YoY to $4.4B, operating loss narrowed to $(172)M from $(1,491)M, operating cash flow turned positive (+$388M), and customer deposits built +$596M to $5.5B — all filed at a cutoff where the stock sits ~54% below its 1-year high (~$9.18). The rerating mechanism is credible and dated: management guides occupancy back to historical levels in summer 2023 with per-passenger revenue above 2019, and each booking update through June should mechanically validate it. The equity is a leveraged call option on this recovery, so modest fundamental beats translate into outsized percentage moves. That said, this is not a clean story: ~$36B debt against $6.2B equity, $539M quarterly interest expense, and the March 13, 2023 interest-coverage covenant waivers (through May 31, 2024) confirm strained covenant headroom even amid recovery. The waivers cut both ways — they signal stress but also eliminate the nearest technical-default trigger, buying time for the seasonal ramp. With $8.1B liquidity and positive OCF, near-term solvency/dilution risk is tolerable, though cross-default provisions and $11.7B floating-rate debt keep the left tail non-trivial. Cheapness alone would be insufficient; here cheapness coincides with a verifiable, cash-flow-backed demand recovery and a dated catalyst window, which meets the bar for a long candidate — sized conservatively given leverage-driven volatility.
trades.catalyst: Summer 2023 peak-season booking/occupancy updates and quarterly results demonstrating return to historical occupancy with above-2019 per-passenger revenue; continued customer-deposit builds converting the narrative from survival to deleveraging optionality on a deeply depressed equity (-54% from 1y high)
trades.invalidation: Booking/deposit momentum stalls or summer occupancy guidance is walked back; any new equity raise or convertible issuance signaling liquidity stress; fuel-price spike re-widening losses; further covenant amendment requests beyond those already secured

trades.thesis: Disc Medicine is a pre-revenue clinical-stage hematology biotech trading ~64% below its 1-year high (~$22 vs. prior peak), with a dated, high-materiality catalyst inside the 90-day window: bitopertin BEACON Phase 2 interim data guided to H1 2023, plus an FDA-authorized NIH-sponsored DBA trial starting by mid-2023. Unlike typical distressed microcaps, the balance sheet does not force a raise within the window — $194.6M cash at YE2022, positive equity of $176.6M after preferred conversion, no debt disclosed, and management-guided runway into 2025 — so the primary risk over 90 days is binary clinical data, not solvency. The clean unqualified EY audit and absence of litigation/restatements remove accounting-quality disqualifiers. The setup is a classic asymmetric binary-event profile: positive interim EPP data would likely drive a sharp rerating of a ~$420M market cap with validated proof-of-concept across two bitopertin trials, while a miss would compress the stock materially given zero revenue and pure option value. Skeptical base rates for Phase 2 interim success (~40-50%) temper enthusiasm, and the company itself caveats that interim data may change with additional patients. Net: credible rerating mechanism plus tolerable (data-risk-dominated, not funding-forced) downside justifies a long-candidate designation at modest conviction, sized for binary variance.
trades.catalyst: Bitopertin BEACON Phase 2 interim efficacy data expected in H1 2023 — a dated, company-disclosed readout falling inside the 90-day forecast window, with secondary support from the FDA-authorized NIH-sponsored DBA trial start by mid-2023.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if BEACON interim data are delayed past Q2 2023, show weak/ambiguous hemoglobin response, or if the company announces a substantial discounted equity raise before the readout; also invalidated by disclosure that SVB cash losses were material to the stated runway.

trades.thesis: China NEV maker trading ~43% below its 1-year high ($23.13 pre-cutoff) despite fundamentals that argue for a rerating rather than distress: FY2022 revenue grew ~68% to RMB45.3bn, operating cash flow was positive for a third straight year (RMB7.4bn), and the balance sheet carries RMB38.5bn cash plus RMB18.0bn time deposits/short-term investments against modest borrowings. The principal regulatory overhang (HFCAA delisting risk) was materially defused by the PCAOB's Dec 15, 2022 vacatur of its inspection determination, and ICFR was effective with auditor attestation — removing two of the classic China-ADR discount drivers. The bear case is real but mostly backward-looking: the net loss widened to RMB2.0bn in 2022 as opex scaled faster than gross profit, and ~111M share awards outstanding create dilution drag. The credible 90-day rerating mechanism is an earnings-inflection catalyst: with new models ramping and scale now achieved, the next quarterly report is the natural event where margins stabilize and the loss narrows, which historically drives sharp multiple recovery in this cohort when it happens. Cheapness alone would not qualify it; here cheapness coincides with (a) removal of the HFCAA tail, (b) self-funding operations, and (c) a dated, checkable catalyst within the window. Position sizing should respect genuine structural risks: VIE consolidation with no equity ownership, RMB9.5bn restricted onshore net assets and RMB48bn intercompany loans (stranded-cash/tax-drag scenario could cut after-tax income to ~50.6% of pre-tax), founder control at 67.5% voting power, and an ongoing EV price war that could delay the margin inflection.
trades.catalyst: Near-term quarterly earnings and monthly delivery disclosures expected within the 90-day window, which can demonstrate the operating-leverage inflection (gross margin recovery and narrowing operating loss) following the new-model ramp; secondary support from continued normalization of the HFCAA/PCAOB overhang already resolved in Dec 2022.
trades.invalidation: Next quarterly print shows gross-margin compression or further operating-loss expansion driven by EV price cuts, or delivery momentum stalls versus peers; also any renewed US-China audit/regulatory escalation or adverse VIE/cash-transfer policy news would invalidate the rerating case.

trades.thesis: TSLA trades at $165, down ~52% from its 1-year high, after a Q1'23 print that confirmed deliberate price-cut-driven margin compression (gross profit $4.51B vs $5.46B YoY; operating income -26%) alongside robust volume-led growth (+24% revenue to $23.3B). The bear case — margin reset — is now disclosed and partially priced; the bull case rests on demand elasticity (price cuts converting to unit growth), a scaling energy storage business (+148% YoY revenue, Shanghai Megafactory announced), and a fortress balance sheet ($16.0B cash + $6.4B ST investments vs only $1.77B debt, covenant compliance, minimal financing dependence) that makes the downside self-funded and survivable through a prolonged price war. With the stock deeply discounted from highs while the fundamental growth engine remains intact, asymmetric mean-reversion potential exists if any delivery/margin stabilization lands within the window. This is a credible rerating mechanism paired with tolerable, liquidity-backed downside — cheapness alone is not the argument; the argument is growth optionality at a distressed-chart price with no balance-sheet risk.
trades.catalyst: Sequential re-acceleration in deliveries as price cuts convert to orders (demand elasticity), continued energy storage/Megapack ramp plus new Shanghai Megafactory, Cybertruck event visibility in H2'23, and IRA-driven affordability tailwinds — any of which can shift the narrative from 'margin collapse' to 'volume-led share gains at acceptable margins.'
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q2'23 data show volumes NOT responding to price cuts (inventory build accelerating beyond the $14.4B level), gross margin breaking below ~18%, or OCF turning negative — indicating a structural demand problem rather than an elastic-pricing strategy. A Delaware Supreme Court reversal on the SolarCity appeal or adverse CEO award ruling would add governance overhang.

trades.thesis: Varonis (VRNS) at $23.23, -47% from its 1-year high, screens as a beaten-down but fundamentally intact security-software name in mid-SaaS-transition. Grounded positives from the Q1'23 10-Q: total revenue +11.5% YoY with subscriptions +20.3% to $83.0M, gross margin up to ~83.6%, operating cash flow positive at $36.8M (vs $24.5M), and a fortress balance sheet — $756.3M cash/securities/deposits against only $253M principal of 1.25% converts due Aug 2025 (net cash roughly $500M, a meaningful fraction of the ~$2.4B market cap). The rerating mechanism is credible rather than merely cheapness-driven: (1) the SaaS/subscription mix shift is visibly accelerating and should be rewarded if guidance/ARR commentary confirms momentum; (2) a dated catalyst exists inside the window — the converts become redeemable Aug 20, 2023 and the revolver matures Aug 21, 2023, forcing capital-structure clarity; capped calls limit conversion dilution to a $47.24 cap, so the overhang is bounded. Downside is tolerable because net cash plus positive OCF make insolvency/dilution risk low near-term, though not zero given persistent GAAP losses (-40% operating margin), SBC at ~34% of revenue, declining deferred revenue/receivables, EMEA weakness (-5.3%) and management-flagged lengthening sales cycles. Net: asymmetric setup with modest positive expected excess return, contingent on subscription momentum holding through the next print.
trades.catalyst: Q1'23 print (filed at cutoff) showing +20% subscription growth and narrowing losses; 2025 Notes become redeemable Aug 20, 2023 and revolver matures Aug 21, 2023 — a dated capital-structure event within the 90-day window that can force resolution of the convert overhang; potential guidance raise on SaaS momentum.
trades.invalidation: Next quarter's print showing subscription growth decelerating below ~20%, ARR/SaaS migration metrics missing targets, or further deferred-revenue/backlog contraction confirming demand deterioration; also any need for equity issuance or distressed-sounding refinancing language around the Aug 2023 convert/revolver dates.

trades.thesis: Vicor enters the window at $41.61, ~49% below its 1-year high, despite a genuinely strong Q1'23: revenue +10.8% YoY to $97.8M, gross margin up ~500bps to ~47.6%, operating income more than doubled to $10.4M, and OCF of $10.1M roughly matching net income ($11.2M, $0.25 diluted EPS vs $0.11). The balance sheet is a fortress — $192.9M cash (~$5.9/share, ~14% of market cap), zero debt, 6.8:1 current ratio, $312.7M working capital — which caps fundamental downside and removes financing risk. The setup is a profitable, cash-rich niche power-conversion supplier trading at a deep drawdown while earnings momentum inflects upward; that combination historically supports mean-reversion/rerating when the next print confirms the trend. Key risks temper enthusiasm rather than kill the thesis: backlog fell sequentially ($304.4M → $271.3M), distributor channel mix shifted sharply toward stocking distributors with rising sales allowances (possible pull-forward), Advanced Products declined on Asia weakness, FCF was ~breakeven against $19.3M capex commitments, and the SynQor willful-infringement verdict carries treble-damages tail risk beyond the fully accrued $6.5M pending court rulings. Cheapness alone is insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with demonstrated operating leverage and a clean balance sheet, giving a credible near-term rerating mechanism via earnings confirmation, with tolerable downside given net-cash support.
trades.catalyst: Continuation of the Q1'23 inflection into the next earnings print — gross margin holding near ~47% and operating income sustaining the doubled run-rate would force a rerating of a stock still ~49% below its 1-year high; secondary upside optionality from a favorable SynQor post-trial ruling and potential future DTA valuation-allowance release (non-operating EPS).
trades.invalidation: Backlog erosion accelerating (already -10.8% sequentially to $271.3M), reversal of stocking-distributor channel fill in next quarter's revenue, Advanced Products weakness spreading into Brick Products, or an adverse SynQor ruling with treble damages/fees materially above the accrual.

trades.thesis: GitLab presents an asymmetric setup: +45% YoY revenue growth with ~89% gross margin and improving SaaS mix, a debt-free balance sheet carrying ~$937.6M in cash plus short-term investments (~17% of the ~$5.4B market cap), and a just-completed ~7% headcount restructuring that creates a credible path to narrowing losses. Trading ~49% below its 1-year high, the stock embeds deep pessimism that conflicts with the disclosed fundamentals. The near-term rerating mechanism is the next earnings cycle showing growth durability plus operating leverage, amplified by the AI-in-DevOps narrative. Key offsets that keep this below high conviction: unresolved ICFR material weaknesses with explicit restatement risk (a genuine tail hazard for a recent IPO), widening GAAP operating loss (-$58.2M), dual-class control limiting governance catalysts, and heavy SBC dilution. The cash floor makes downside tolerable while the growth/margin profile offers real upside optionality into the next print.
trades.catalyst: Next quarterly report (Q2 FY24, ~early September 2023) demonstrating continued ~40%+ growth with narrowing losses on the restructuring; ongoing AI-feature monetization narrative in DevSecOps driving multiple expansion off a depressed post-IPO valuation.
trades.invalidation: Q2 FY24 print showing deceleration below ~35% growth, continued or widening GAAP losses despite the restructuring, RPO/billings softness, or disclosure of restatement/remediation failure tied to the material weaknesses. A break below the ~$30 level (net-cash-adjusted support) would signal the market is pricing fundamental deterioration rather than macro noise.

trades.thesis: Small-cap furniture DTC retailer trading ~41% below its 1-year high ($22.69) immediately after a mixed Q1 print (net sales +9.1% to $141.2M but swing to a $4.2M net loss on 27% SG&A deleverage). The bearish headline is offset by two credible forward-looking positives grounded in the filing: (1) customer deposits more than doubled YoY to $15.4M from $6.8M — a tangible order-backlog/demand-inflection signal for a Q4-weighted seasonal business, not yet reflected in trailing P&L; and (2) operating cash flow turned positive (+$6.3M vs -$21.8M LY) via deliberate inventory drawdown, indicating working-capital discipline. Balance sheet is clean: $45.1M cash, zero drawn on the $40M revolver, no funded debt — downside is bounded by cash generation rather than solvency risk, though ~$164M PV of lease obligations is the real fixed-claim overhang. Internet channel +28.7% shows the growth engine intact. The rerating mechanism is concrete: if deposit build converts to revenue in coming quarters while SG&A growth normalizes, the stock re-rates off a depressed base; the newly filed results are already public, so the classic post-earnings drift/setup is the near-term vehicle. This is not cheapness alone — there is an identifiable demand signal plus self-help inventory/cash levers. Risks are real: negative operating leverage could persist, barter media credits ($28.5M unused, no impairment) are judgmental, RSU overhang (~1.28M units, ~8% of shares) has doubled, and small-cap retail beta is high. Position as a modest-sized long candidate, not a conviction overweight.
trades.catalyst: Conversion of the doubled customer-deposit backlog into recognized revenue through the seasonally dominant second half, plus the next quarterly report demonstrating SG&A cost control; a demonstrated return toward breakeven EBITDA would drive a rerating off a -41% drawdown base.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if next-quarter results show continued double-digit SG&A growth without commensurate sales acceleration, or if customer deposits roll over rather than convert to shipments — evidence that the deposit build reflects longer lead times rather than genuine demand inflection.

trades.thesis: Root-style direct-to-consumer auto insurer at $10.93 (-56% from 1y high) offers an asymmetric setup: unit economics are inflecting sharply (net combined ratio 150.5% vs 217.3%, gross loss ratio 65.5% vs 87.0%, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$11.9M from -$63.2M) while the balance sheet carries $628.0M cash — $520.3M of it outside regulated entities — against $297.4M debt, implying unencumbered net cash on the order of the entire equity value at the pre-cutoff price. The bear case (policies in force -32% YoY, premiums earned -25%, ongoing burn of ~$94M/H1, SOFR+9% term loan, unremediated ICFR material weakness from employee fraud) is real but largely known and priced into a 56% drawdown. The rerating mechanism is concrete: two more quarters of demonstrated EBITDA-loss compression toward breakeven, backed by rate increases (+26% premiums per policy) already earning in, plus surging investment income ($6.8M vs $0.7M) — a small beat versus expectations on a tiny ~$200M-class market cap with heavy short interest typical of the name can produce outsized moves. Downside is cushioned by hard asset value well above the equity quote even under stress scenarios, making risk/reward tolerable for a long candidate despite governance noise.
trades.catalyst: Q3 2023 earnings (early November) demonstrating sequential adjusted EBITDA improvement toward breakeven and stabilization/inflection of policies in force; continued favorable prior-year reserve development and rising investment income could force a rerating of a stock trading below net cash.
trades.invalidation: Q3 results showing re-acceleration of cash burn, renewed deterioration in loss ratio from claims severity inflation, further double-digit decline in policies in force without premium-per-policy offset, or disclosure of covenant pressure/unencumbered cash approaching the $200M floor would invalidate the thesis; a second consecutive quarter without operating-loss narrowing removes the rerating mechanism.

trades.thesis: TG Therapeutics presents a rare commercial-stage biotech setup: BRIUMVI (FDA-approved Dec 2022, EC-approved for RMS) is compounding rapidly off a small base — Q2'23 net product revenue of $16.0M vs $0.6M a year ago and roughly double Q1'23's implied ~$7.8M — while the stock sits 68% below its 1-year high, implying the market has largely written off the launch. The single biggest bear argument (financing dependence) was partially defused after cutoff-relevant events: the $140.0M Neuraxpharm ex-US/EU upfront was received in July 2023, putting pro-forma liquidity near ~$285M against ~$51M/quarter operating burn (roughly 6+ quarters of runway even before revenue contribution). A credible rerating mechanism exists over the next 90 days: each successive quarter of >50% sequential BRIUMVI script/revenue growth forces the street to re-anchor from 'cash-burning story' toward 'commercial ramp,' and the Q3 print (November) lands inside the window. Offsets are real: SG&A (+77% H1 YoY) is outpacing revenue, Q2 operating loss widened YoY, equity cushion is thin ($40.5M), debt rose to $97.7M, and unproven first-year gross-to-net reserves create estimate risk. This is a momentum-on-launch bet with tolerable but non-trivial downside, not a value or quality position; cheapness alone does not qualify it — the accelerating revenue inflection plus de-risked liquidity does.
trades.catalyst: Q3 2023 earnings (early November): sequential BRIUMVI net product revenue growth off the $16.0M Q2 base, plus first disclosure of EU/Neuraxpharm launch progress and updated pro-forma liquidity (~$285M), which together would validate the commercial trajectory and defer dilution fears.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 BRIUMVI revenue shows flat-to-down sequential growth or heavy gross-to-net reserve building, or if management signals a near-term equity raise despite the Neuraxpharm upfront; a break back toward the lows on volume would indicate the launch narrative is not being believed.

trades.thesis: Madrigal (MDGL) trades at $179.49, down ~42% from its 1-year high, after the pivotal MAESTRO-NASH topline was released in December 2022 — meaning the largest binary data risk is already absorbed in the price. The filings reveal a credible near-term rerating mechanism: G&A grew +59% YoY specifically on 'commercial preparation activities' including headcount build, and the Hercules facility's Tranche 2 draws were enabled by achieved clinical milestones with Tranche 3 contingent on FDA approval — both consistent with management and lenders expecting an NDA submission/acceptance window in H2 2023. A pre-commercial biotech with positive pivotal data, an active launch build-out, and ~$298M liquidity offers asymmetric upside if regulatory confirmation lands within the 90-day window, while the December-2022 derating limits how much failure risk remains priced in. Financial posture is genuinely weak (zero revenue, $159.4M H1 burn, debt doubled to $99.2M at 10.70%, equity halved to $103.5M, explicit statement that additional capital raises are required, $200M ATM overhang), so this is a catalyst-driven position, not a value position: cheapness alone does not qualify it, but the combination of a de-risked pivotal asset, visible launch preparation, and a compressed valuation does. Position sizing should be moderate given dilution dependence and single-asset concentration.
trades.catalyst: Likely resmetirom NDA submission/FDA acceptance with priority review in H2 2023 (implied by commercial launch preparation and milestone-linked debt structure); any regulatory confirmation would re-rate the equity toward pre-derating levels.
trades.invalidation: Delay or absence of an NDA submission/acceptance announcement through Q4 2023; heavy ATM issuance below current prices; loss of Hercules covenant compliance or inability to access milestone tranches; any negative regulatory feedback from FDA.

trades.thesis: AMSC shows a genuine, quote-grounded operating inflection in Q1 FY2024 (quarter ended 6/30/23): revenue +33% YoY to $30.3M, gross margin expanded to ~20.8% from ~9.8%, operating loss narrowed to $(5.3)M from $(8.9)M, and operating cash burn improved to $(2.2)M. A large deferred revenue build ($50.9M current portion, up from $43.6M) signals funded demand conversion, and a ~5% workforce restructuring adds ~$5M annualized savings. The stock sits 46% below its 1-year high at $8.70, so positive surprises are not pre-priced. However, this is not yet a long candidate: cash is only $22.0M against recurring losses and a $1.06B accumulated deficit, management explicitly states there is 'no assurance' it can raise additional capital, and a $250M shelf expires February 2024 — creating a live dilution overhang squarely inside the 90-day window. The Q1 burn improvement also included a one-time $2.1M ERC reimbursement. The rerating mechanism (continued growth + margin expansion toward breakeven) is credible but unproven for a second consecutive quarter, and no dated near-term catalysts (contract awards, backlog figures) were disclosed in the excerpts. Net: constructive operating momentum offset by financing dependence; wait for either a second quarter of confirmation or removal of the financing overhang.
trades.catalyst: Sequential quarterly results showing sustained >25% revenue growth and further loss narrowing, plus disclosure of backlog/order intake converting the $50.9M current deferred revenue into recognized sales; any de-risking of the financing question (revenue-funded breakeven trajectory) would be the primary rerating trigger.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if the next quarter shows revenue growth deceleration or gross-margin reversal, operating cash burn re-widens ex-ERC items, or the company announces an equity offering under the expiring shelf — any of which would confirm the dilution/liquidity constraint dominates the operating story.

trades.thesis: SentinelOne-style high-growth cybersecurity platform trading at ~$16.28, down ~44% from its 1-year high, implying roughly 6x EV/ARR ($612M ARR, ~295.7M shares, ~$1.14B net cash, no debt) for a business growing revenue +46% YoY. Fundamentals are not broken: RPO of $676.1M, deferred revenue rising sequentially, gross margin ~69%, and operating cash burn improved sharply (-$40.0M vs -$111.5M for the six months). The June 2023 restructuring plus improving cash efficiency creates a credible margin-inflection narrative that the market can re-rate on at the next quarterly report (early December, inside the 90-day window). The deep drawdown means sentiment, not solvency, is the binding constraint — liquidity is a >10-year runway at current burn. Offsetting this, metric quality is genuinely impaired: a one-time ~5% downward ARR correction, an ARR methodology change made amid declining consumption, NRR deceleration from 135%+ to 115%+, management-disclosed enterprise usage declines and deal downsizing, heavy SBC (~38% of revenue), and dual-class control. These argue for a discounted position rather than exclusion: the valuation already embeds substantial growth-quality skepticism, and the asymmetry at ~6x EV/ARR with net cash is tolerable. This is a moderate-conviction, catalyst-dependent long: cheapness plus improving cash economics plus a dated rerating event (Q3 earnings), not cheapness alone.
trades.catalyst: Q3 FY2024 earnings report (due early December 2023, within the 90-day window): if the company shows continued ~40%+ growth, further operating cash burn reduction, and stabilization of NRR post-restructuring, the market could re-rate the multiple toward high-growth cyber peers; a broader software/cyber sector de-rating reversal (rates-driven) would amplify the move.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 FY2024 results (or pre-announcement) show ARR growth decelerating below ~35%, NRR slipping under 110%, renewed ARR metric corrections, or re-accelerating cash burn; a break to new 52-week lows on the report would signal the market is pricing structural growth-quality impairment rather than sentiment overshoot.

trades.thesis: ARMOUR is a deeply discounted, externally managed agency mREIT trading at roughly 0.37x stated book value (equity ~$1.24B over ~49.0M post-split shares implies ~$25/sh book vs. $9.27 price) after a -47% drawdown. The bear case is real and grounded: net interest income collapsed to $3.6M as repo costs consumed interest income, Q3 GAAP loss was $(179)M, leverage is ~9-11x with 50% of funding through related-party BUCKLER, and governance/fee alignment is poor. But the marginal negatives are largely recognized: the dividend has already been cut ($1.20 vs $1.50), haircuts improved (2.73% vs 3.85%), liquidity is solid ($499M: $133.5M cash + $365.6M unencumbered agencies), no preferred arrears exist, and ATM capacity ($450M raised YTD, shelf open) demonstrates continued capital-markets access that makes near-term forced deleveraging improbable. The rerating mechanism is macro-mechanical, not idiosyncratic: agency MBS valuations and repo carry are directly levered to the rate path, and at ~0.37x book with a fresh reverse split and cut dividend, even a stabilization-to-modest-decline in long rates produces outsized NAV-per-share recovery and multiple expansion versus SPY. Cheapness alone is insufficient, so this is sized as a convexity/reversion position contingent on rates peaking — not a quality long.
trades.catalyst: A pause or pivot in Fed policy / decline in front-end rates would immediately relieve repo funding costs (the dominant driver of the NII collapse), stabilize or raise Agency MBS prices, and allow the ~0.37x P/B to close toward historical mREIT trading ranges; secondary catalysts are the Q3 book value print quantifying the discount and the 12/29/2023 Javelin dismissal review removing legal overhang.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if long rates re-accelerate higher (10Y making new highs above ~5%), driving another quarter of large trading losses and book value erosion; if the company continues issuing equity well below book value at an accelerating pace; or if repo funding tightens (BUCKLER concentration, haircuts widening beyond the improved 2.73%) forcing asset sales. A further dividend cut signaling distress rather than prudence would also invalidate.

trades.thesis: Cullen/Frost trades at $76.67 after a -45.6% drawdown from its 1-year high, pricing in regional-bank contagion fears that the filing largely refutes. CET1 of 13.32% is far above well-capitalized thresholds, liquidity buffers are substantial (~$7.0B at the Fed, ~$5.4B FHLB capacity, ~$14.1B unencumbered securities), and core earnings power is intact with Q3 NII up 8.4% YoY and loans +7.3% YTD. The stock sits near tangible book value even after recognizing the full -$1.78B AOCI mark, so much of the rate-driven unrealized loss is already embedded in price. Management began buying back stock ($40.5M YTD) and raised the dividend, signaling confidence. The credible rerating mechanism is macro rather than idiosyncratic: if long rates peak or decline from October's highs, the AOCI/securities mark pressure eases and deeply discounted high-quality Texas banks re-rate sharply, as seen in prior regional recoveries. Cheapness alone would not suffice, but here it combines with fortress capital, ample liquidity, growing NII, and an active buyback — a genuine near-term rerating setup with defined downside near book.
trades.catalyst: Peak-rate repricing: any decline in long-term Treasury yields directly narrows the $1.78B AOCI hole and re-rates the stock toward tangible book, while the active buyback ($40.5M YTD) and rising dividend ($0.92/qtr) provide ongoing per-share support; Q4 earnings in January would showcase NII momentum if deposit outflows stabilize.
trades.invalidation: Deposit outflows accelerating beyond the $3.0B nine-month pace, further widening of AOCI losses with rising yields, nonaccruals continuing to climb sharply (already up to $67.2M from $37.8M), or a break below tangible book support (~$47/share) would invalidate the mean-reversion setup.

trades.thesis: ResMed enters the window deeply de-rated (-42% from 1-year high, ~$134.70 pre-cutoff) while its just-filed Q1 FY24 10-Q shows accelerating fundamentals: revenue +16% YoY to $1,102.3M, SaaS +32%, US masks/consumables +23%, and a sharp working-capital inflection driving operating cash flow to $286.3M from $44.7M. The disconnect between depressed valuation and improving fundamentals is the core setup. Management is leaning in: dividend raised to $0.48/share and the buyback reactivated in October 2023 after suspension since FY2019 — a credible, quote-grounded signal that insiders see value, and a mechanical support for shares. Liquidity is solid ($209.1M cash, $825M undrawn revolver, no material maturities before 2026), controls effective, litigation ordinary-course. The bear case embedded in the drawdown is largely narrative-driven rather than reflected in reported demand, giving room for rerating as results keep landing. Offsets that temper sizing: GAAP gross margin declined YoY (54.4% vs 56.9%), device COGS grew faster than device revenue, net interest expense doubled, warranty accruals nearly tripled, and a new $7.9M Astral field-safety charge was excluded from non-GAAP — modest earnings-quality flags. Net: credible rerating mechanism (cash-flow inflection + shareholder returns + strong prints against a washed-out price) with tolerable downside given fortress liquidity and recurring consumables/SaaS revenue.
trades.catalyst: Fresh Q1 FY24 beat just delivered at cutoff (filed 2023-10-27): +16% revenue, +32% SaaS, $286M operating cash flow, dividend raised to $0.48 and buyback reactivated October 2023 — a concrete management signal of confidence immediately following a -42% drawdown, with the reactivated repurchase program (12.9M shares authorized through June 2024) providing a near-term bid while sentiment on sleep-health demand resets.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the margin compression proves structural rather than mix/transitory — specifically continued device COGS growing faster than device revenue into the December quarter, further field-safety/warranty charges beyond Astral, or disclosure of demand destruction in core sleep-device prescriptions (e.g., guidance cuts or slowing masks/consumables growth) that would validate the drawdown's bearish premise.

trades.thesis: Newell-type consumer products name trading at $6.45, down ~54% from its 1-year high, after a Q3 print that was unambiguously bad (sales -9% YoY, $(159)M operating loss, $263M impairments including $241M Baby goodwill, covenant relief, CP market access lost, ratings downgraded to BB/Ba2). The bearish news is largely disclosed and, we believe, substantially discounted at a price embedding deep distress. The case for a long is not cheapness alone but a dated rerating mechanism: Project Phoenix is guided to be substantially implemented by end of 2023, giving management a concrete cost-savings narrative for the Q4 report inside the 90-day window, while the worst working-capital drag (retailer destocking) is visibly exhausting — a $411M inventory drawdown drove operating cash flow to +$679M, short-term debt fell to $376M, the dividend was already cut to $0.07, and a new $225-275M receivables facility plus an undrawn $1.5B revolver maturing 2027 fund the company through the window. Non-cash impairments at trough EBITDA tend to mark sentiment lows rather than propagate to equity value. Risks are real: further impairment sensitivity (~$115M incremental on a 10% Baby EBITA cut), rising interest expense, and macro warning language argue against sizing up. Net: modestly favorable asymmetry from a washed-out base, contingent on demand stabilization rather than any fundamental inflection yet visible.
trades.catalyst: Project Phoenix declared substantially implemented at end of 2023, followed by Q4/FY2023 reporting (early 2024) that frames a lower-cost 2024 exit rate just as retailer destocking abates; any stabilization commentary on Baby/Outdoor demand supports multiple repair from a -54% drawdown base.
trades.invalidation: Q4 results showing sequential demand deterioration beyond destocking effects, another large impairment signaling forecast unreliability, or renewed covenant/ratings stress would invalidate the mean-reversion thesis; also invalid if the stock fails to participate in a broad risk-on move over the next month.

trades.thesis: Dyne Therapeutics is a pre-revenue clinical-stage biotech trading at $6.62 (~$406M market cap on 61.4M shares) versus $157.8M cash+securities, down 56% from its 1-year high. The bull case rests on a genuinely dated, quote-grounded catalyst: initial DYNE-251 MAD data (safety, dystrophin expression) expected early January 2024, plus DYNE-101/DYNE-251 proof-of-concept readouts within a runway funded 'through 2024.' However, the setup fails the strict long-candidate bar on several counts: (1) burn is accelerating sharply (Q3 R&D $55.3M, +59% YoY; 9M operating cash use $153.2M), implying roughly one quarter of unraised runway beyond mid-2024 and a probable dilutive financing within or just after the 90-day window — the company already raised ~$104.6M gross-equivalent in 2023 across two follow-ons and an ATM priced at $12.01, far above the current price; (2) the January readout is an early safety/dystrophin dataset, not proof of efficacy, and the company has never completed a clinical trial — binary risk is high; (3) accumulated deficit of $565.9M and equity down to $152M confirm structural cash consumption. The 56% drawdown partially prices this in, and clean DYNE-251 safety to date offers some support, but cheapness relative to cash is not sufficient when the cash is committed to burn and the catalyst outcome is a coin flip weighted by base rates unfavorable to early-stage readouts. Expected value is roughly flat-to-slightly-negative: a strong dystrophin signal could drive a sharp rerating, but dilution pressure and binary downside offset it. This is a watchlist name pending clearer readout timing/enrollment evidence or a de-risked entry.
trades.catalyst: DYNE-251 initial MAD data (safety/tolerability/dystrophin expression) expected early January 2024 per the 10-Q, followed by DYNE-101/DYNE-251 proof-of-concept readouts within the funded runway through 2024.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if DYNE-251 January 2024 MAD data shows meaningful dystrophin expression increases with clean safety (rerating case strengthens toward long), or conversely if the company announces a large discounted financing or data slippage before year-end (downside case hardens).

trades.thesis: First Solar presents a genuine operating inflection — Q3 FY2023 net sales +27% YoY to $801.1M, gross profit swinging from $21M to $376M, diluted EPS $2.50 vs $(0.46) — underpinned by a contracted 77.6 GW / $23.0B backlog through 2030 and deferred revenue up 43% to $1.72B on customer advances. The stock sits 41% below its 1-year high at $136.32, suggesting substantial pessimism already priced. The rerating mechanism is credible: demonstrated GAAP profitability at scale, legislated Section 45X credits (~17c/W through 2032) converting the cost structure, India production start unlocking Tamil Nadu subsidies, and removal of legal overhangs (class action and derivative suits dismissed with prejudice). Liquidity is adequate near term ($1.8B cash+securities, undrawn revolver) versus ~$500M debt. However, conviction is tempered materially: gross margin expansion is largely policy-driven (45X credit of $204.6M in Q3) rather than unit economics, nine-month OCF of only $41.2M against $481.5M net income reveals poor accrual/cash conversion, ~$1.9B of remaining capex implies continued external funding dependence (bridge financing explicitly flagged), IRS guidance risk hangs over recognized benefits, and an SEC subpoena on India operations remains an unquantified tail. This is a modest-edge long candidate, not a high-conviction one: the demand visibility and legislative earnings floor are real, but earnings quality and financing dependence cap upside confidence, and the -41% drawdown reflects legitimate ASP/momentum concerns rather than pure mispricing.
trades.catalyst: Post-Q3 analyst estimate revisions and forward guidance incorporating the now-demonstrated 45X-driven margin structure; incremental contract bookings against the 77.6 GW backlog; first India module shipments monetizing Tamil Nadu incentives; progress on 45X credit monetization/bridge financing reducing the funding-overhang discount.
trades.invalidation: Adverse IRS guidance narrowing 45X credit scope or monetization; new module bookings at materially lower ASPs compressing backlog economics; equity issuance or large bridge financing signaling the $1.9B capex plan cannot be self-funded; further deterioration in OCF-to-net-income conversion; renewed India-related regulatory escalation (SEC subpoena).

trades.thesis: Hims & Hers enters November 2023 at $6.48, down 46% from its 1-year high, yet the just-filed Q3 10-Q shows a business inflecting rather than deteriorating: revenue +56% YoY ($226.7M), gross margin up ~370bps to 82.7%, operating loss cut by more than half to $(8.6)M, and a swing to positive nine-month operating cash flow (+$51.5M vs -$19.8M). The balance sheet is clean — $212.5M cash and short-term investments, no debt, modest $18.5M contractual obligations — so downside is cushioned by roughly 15% of market cap in net cash and a $50M buyback authorization. The setup combines a credible near-term rerating mechanism (path to GAAP profitability on hyper-growth, with the market pricing a broken story) with tolerable fundamental downside. Key discounts: earnings quality is low (SBC of $48.3M ≈ the entire OCF; working-capital inflow is payables-driven), dilution is heavy ($105.1M unrecognized RSU expense, evergreen plan, dual-class control), and marketing at ~51% of revenue leaves the model dependent on sustained acquisition efficiency. On balance, improving fundamentals at a washed-out valuation justify a long candidate stance, sized with respect for the dilution and low-quality cash conversion.
trades.catalyst: Q3 print (filed on the cutoff date) showing first sustained positive operating cash flow plus a credible path to GAAP profitability; follow-through in Q4/FY2023 guidance and continued margin expansion could force re-rating of a stock still priced for stagnation at -46% from its 1-year high; $50M buyback authorization provides incremental support near lows.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 2023 results show decelerating revenue growth (<40% YoY), stalled or reversing gross-margin gains, marketing spend re-accelerating above ~55% of revenue without commensurate growth, or guidance implying GAAP profitability recedes beyond FY2024; a regulatory action against telehealth prescribing would be an immediate exit trigger.

trades.thesis: Coherus (CHRS, $3.61, -66% from 1y high) has one genuine positive catalyst — FDA approval of LOQTORZI on 2023-10-27 — but that news predates the cutoff and is already embedded in the price, while the 90-day window offers no comparable fresh rerating event: the LOQTORZI launch itself is only expected in Q1 2024 with negligible initial revenue from a small NPC indication carrying a 20% royalty. Against this, the filing shows deteriorating fundamentals: nine-month revenue flat YoY ($165.7M) despite +64% Q3 growth, a $(106.6)M trade receivables build driving nine-month operating cash burn to $(161.9)M, only ~$131M liquidity against ~$473M debt at a 13.76% rate, a $(133.6)M stockholders' deficit, and escalating minimum-net-sales covenants ($210M TTM by Q1 2024) that the current run-rate does not comfortably clear. The Sept 21 CRL on the UDENYCA on-body injector adds regulatory execution risk. With heavy reliance on dilutive financing (shares up ~38% YTD), the balance-sheet overhang dominates any residual LOQTORZI optimism; cheapness here reflects distress, not mispricing.
trades.catalyst: LOQTORZI U.S. launch in Q1 2024 plus potential UDENYCA on-body injector PAS approval following the Oct 5 resubmission; both are already partially priced and offer limited upside unless launch metrics materially beat expectations.
trades.invalidation: Thesis weakens if the company reports a successful capital raise/deleveraging on favorable terms, demonstrates LOQTORZI launch traction ahead of plan, or receives UDENYCA on-body injector approval with clear covenant headroom.

trades.thesis: Axogen trades at $3.93, ~70% below its 1-year high, yet the Q3 2023 10-Q shows genuine fundamental improvement: revenue +11.7% YoY ($41.3M), opex growing slower than revenue, and operating cash burn cut 68% ($(5.5)M vs $(17.4)M). Critically, multiple dated catalysts land inside the 90-day window: the pre-BLA FDA meeting expected early Q1 2024, the start of the rolling Avance BLA submission in Q1 2024, and the Q1 2024 Avive+ launch. At this depressed valuation with covenant compliance confirmed and management asserting a 12-month runway, even partial execution on these milestones offers a credible rerating mechanism rather than mere cheapness. The setup is asymmetric: a de-risked regulatory path or successful launch could re-rate a deeply beaten micro-cap, while the main downside is a costly but not immediately threatening capital structure ($32.6M cash vs $50M debt due 2027/28). Conviction is tempered by weak earnings quality (SBC of $13.1M nearly equals the $17.8M net loss), ~280bps gross margin compression, explicit reliance on future equity/debt issuance, and an unresolved lender dispute over make-whole payments potentially up to ~$12M — so sizing must reflect meaningful uncertainty around both catalyst timing and financing risk.
trades.catalyst: Pre-BLA FDA meeting expected early Q1 2024 followed by start of rolling Avance BLA submission in Q1 2024 (complete by Q2), plus planned Q1 2024 launch of Avive+ Soft Tissue Matrix — all dated inside the 90-day forecast window.
trades.invalidation: Slippage of the pre-BLA meeting or rolling submission past Q1 2024, an equity raise announced before/at the catalysts, adverse resolution of the make-whole dispute (~$12M exposure), or renewed margin deterioration would invalidate the thesis.

trades.thesis: The issuer (NYSE-listed, ~$14.75, -63% from 1-year high, ~$820M market cap on 55.6M shares) shows a genuine fundamental inflection masked by a deep sentiment de-rate. Quote-grounded 10-Q evidence: Q3 FY24 revenue +25% YoY to $91.6M (nine months +28% to $261.3M) across all lines including subscriptions +29%; S&M essentially flat YoY while revenue grew ~28% — real operating leverage; operating loss narrowed to $(32.0)M from $(39.8)M; operating cash burn improved sharply to $(29.3)M nine months from $(74.2)M prior year (Q3 only $(6.3)M). At ~$370M annualized revenue run-rate, enterprise value (~$730M net of $103.4M cash, ~$13.6M debt, ~$10.3M deferred consideration) implies roughly 2x EV/S for 25% growth with visible margin improvement — an undemanding multiple if the leverage trend continues. Liquidity risk is mitigated near term: the December 4, 2023 Capital One ABL replaces the terminated SVB revolver, and at current improved burn rates cash covers well over two years even with modest M&A. A dated catalyst exists: fiscal Q4 FY24 earnings due within ~30 days of cutoff, where continued beat-and-improve would directly challenge the bear case. This is not cheapness alone — there is a credible rerating mechanism (operating leverage toward adjusted EBITDA breakeven confirmed by a January print) and tolerable downside (cash cushion, new facility, no material litigation, no impairments). Offsets keeping this below high conviction: management explicitly guides to continued losses/negative cash flow for at least a year, FCF remains negative ($(46.5)M nine months), goodwill jumped to $75.5M on three FY24 acquisitions adding integration risk, AR allowance rose ~48%, SBC is heavy ($53.7M nine months) with ongoing dilution mechanics, and covenants on the new facility constrain flexibility.
trades.catalyst: Fiscal Q4 FY2024 earnings report expected in early January 2024 (~30 days post-cutoff): if it confirms the Q3 pattern of ~25% revenue growth with flat S&M and sequential EBITDA/burn improvement, the ~2x EV/S multiple is vulnerable to upward rerating. The December 4, 2023 Capital One ABL signing also removes the SVB-related financing uncertainty as an overhang before that print.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the January print shows decelerating organic revenue (growth driven mainly by acquisitions), renewed opex/burn expansion, covenant pressure under the Capital One facility, or any need for dilutive equity issuance; a break below the post-drawdown lows on heavy volume would signal the de-rate is fundamental, not sentiment-driven.

trades.thesis: TG Therapeutics enters March 2024 as a newly commercial-stage company trading ~50% below its 1-year high ($17.63), with a credible near-term rerating mechanism: BRIUMVI's first full quarters of US sales under the J-code effective July 2023, the Feb 26, 2024 German/EU launch via Neuraxpharm (triggering a $12.5M milestone from up to $492.5M remaining), and a Q1 2024 print that will be the first clean read on launch trajectory. The balance sheet is adequately funded near term ($217.5M cash/investments vs. $100.1M drawn debt, $85M undrawn Hercules capacity, $140M Neuraxpharm upfront received), audits are clean (unqualified FS and ICFR opinions), and management does not expect to require new capital — limiting dilution overhang during the window. The bear case is real but partially discounted by the drawdown: earnings quality is weak (GAAP net income driven by one-time license revenue; core operations still loss-making), working capital assets are untested, debt is secured by substantially all assets with restrictive covenants, and revenue is concentrated in a single product competing against ocrelizumab/ofatumumab.
